title: Modeling Reactions on the Solid–Liquid Interface with Next Generation Extended Lagrangian Quantum-Based Molecular Dynamics
abstractText: Abstract We present a series of simulations of the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR) using a novel framework for atomistic simulations of surface catalysis under electrochemical bias. The framework makes use of quantum-mechanical extended Lagrangian Born–Oppenheimer molecular dynamics (XL-BOMD) simulations, which provide the speed and accuracy required for explicit atomistic treatment of both electrode and electrolyte. Simulations of solvated O2 near nitrogen-doped graphene (NG) were performed to gain insight into the ORR, and different mechanisms were observed, depending on the applied bias. Under higher bias the ORR occurred by an outer-sphere mechanism, without adsorption of O2 to NG. In this mechanism, electron transfer between the catalyst and the O2 was mediated by the solvent. Under lower bias the ORR occurred by an inner-sphere mechanism involving adsorption of O2 to NG, leading to direct electron transfer. Our extensive, all-atom quantum-mechanical molecular dynamics simulations also show clear differences between the kinetics of the ORR on this ideally polarizable electrode and commonly used kinetic theories, leading to new insights regarding mechanistic changes with varied overpotentials. Combining quantum accuracy with explicit solvation and electrostatic potential bias, XL-BOMD opens a route to predictive, atomistic insight into electrocatalytic processes, as demonstrated with the ORR.

title: A stochastic Galerkin method for optimal Dirichlet boundary control problems with uncertain data
abstractText: Abstract The paper deals with a stochastic Galerkin approximation of elliptic Dirichlet boundary control problems with random input data. The expectation of a tracking-type cost functional with deterministic constrained control is minimized. Error estimates are derived for the control variable in the $$L^2(\partial {\mathcal {D}})$$ L 2 ( ∂ D ) -norm and for the state variable in the $${L^2(\Gamma ;L^2({\mathcal {D}}))}$$ L 2 ( Γ ; L 2 ( D ) ) -norm. To solve large linear systems, appropriate preconditioners are proposed for both unconstrained and constrained scenarios. To illustrate the validity and efficiency of the proposed approaches, some numerical experiments are performed.

title: Using BDF Schemes in the Temporal Integration of POD-ROM Methods
abstractText: Abstract In this paper we consider the numerical approximation of a semilinear reaction-diffusion model problem by means of reduced-order methods (ROMs) based on proper orthogonal decomposition (POD). We focus on the time integration of the fully discrete reduced-order model. Most of the analysis in the literature has been carried out for the implicit Euler method as time integrator. We integrate in time the reduced-order model with the BDF-q time stepping ( $$1\le q\le 5$$ 1 ≤ q ≤ 5 ) and prove optimal rate of convergence of order q in time. Our set of snapshots is obtained from finite element approximations to the original model problem computed at different times. These finite element approximations can be obtained with any time integrator. It is known that the use of difference quotients in the set of snapshots allows to provide pointwise-in-time error bounds. On the other hand, we show that the BDF-q time stepping, $$1\le q\le 5$$ 1 ≤ q ≤ 5 , can be written as a linear combination of first order difference quotients. As a consequence, the use of difference quotients is essential to get the expected rate q in time. For those reasons, the POD method in this paper is based on first order difference quotients of the snapshots.

title: Examples of real stable bundles on K3 surfaces
abstractText: Abstract Motivated by gauge theory on manifolds with exceptional holonomy, we construct examples of stable bundles on K3 surfaces that are invariant under two involutions: one is holomorphic; and the other is anti-holomorphic. These bundles are obtained via the monad construction, and stability is examined using the Generalised Hoppe Criterion of Jardim–Menet–Prata–Sá Earp, which requires verifying an arithmetic condition for elements in the Picard group of the surfaces. We establish this by using computer aid in two critical steps: first, we construct K3 surfaces with small Picard group—one branched double cover of $$\mathbb {P}^1 \times \mathbb {P}^1$$ P 1 × P 1 with Picard rank 2 using a new method which may be of independent interest; and second, we verify the arithmetic condition for carefully chosen elements of the Picard group, which provides a systematic approach for constructing further examples.

title: Lack of Natural Seagrass Recovery at a Site in the Eastern Tropical Pacific Reveals the Need for Active Ecological Restoration
abstractText: Seagrass meadows provide many ecosystem services, but by virtue of anthropogenic pressures, they are also highly threatened habitats. In the Eastern Tropical Pacific, a seagrass meadow disappeared in 1996 following a severe storm at Bahía Culebra, northern Pacific coast of Costa Rica. This study aimed to assess natural recovery of this seagrass meadow and identify potential factors influencing habitat condition. A field assessment was carried out in 2023, to assess seagrass presence or absence at the site, collect biomass cores to check for potential presence of belowground biomass, collection of sediment for grain size analysis, evaluation of water quality conditions, deployment of grazer exclusion cages, and incubation of sediment in aquaria conditions to assess potential seed germination. There was no seagrass biomass or seagrass cover noted within the bay in 2023. Incubated sediment did not lead to seed germination, and no seeds were found in the sediment following incubation. Water conditions and sediment grain sizes were within parameters for other meadows nearby yet revealed decreased water conditions at this site compared to previous ones in 2000–2001. Water quality varied temporally, consistent with natural seasonal upwelling in the bay. Conditions were suitable for seagrasses, yet other potential dispersal and establishment-limiting factors, such as water flow dynamics, sediment biogeochemistry, and microbial communities, should be assessed at higher spatial and temporal frequencies in the future. Given the lack of natural recovery in 27 yr and apparent recent suitable seagrass conditions, active seagrass ecological restoration initiatives are recommended at this site.

title: Landscape and mutational dynamics of G-quadruplexes across the complete human genome
abstractText: Abstract Background G-quadruplexes (G4s) are alternative DNA structures with diverse biological roles, but their examination in highly repetitive parts of the human genome has been hindered by the lack of reliable sequencing technologies. Recent long-read based genome assemblies have enabled their characterization in previously inaccessible parts of the human genome. Here, we examine the topography and genomic instability of potential G4-forming sequences in the gap-less, reference human genome assembly and in 88 haplotypes of diverse ancestry. Results We report that G4s are highly enriched in specific repetitive regions, including in certain centromeric and pericentromeric repeat types, and in ribosomal DNA arrays, and experimentally validate the most prevalent G4s detected. G4s tend to have lower methylation than expected and are genomically unstable, showing an excess of insertions and deletions. Finally, we show that G4-forming motifs are consistently enriched at meiotic DSB hotspots across individuals with different PRDM9 genotypes. Conclusions Together, our findings establish G4s as dynamic and functionally significant elements of the human genome and highlight new avenues for investigating their contributions to human disease and evolution.

title: Probing the Anomalous Symmetry Breaking in Kagome Material CsV3Sb5 via Third-Order Nonlinearity
abstractText: Abstract The kagome material has rapidly established itself as a research frontier in condensed matter physics, owing to its distinctive geometric structure and the rich array of unconventional physical phenomena. In the kagome AV3Sb5 (A = K, Rb, and Cs) family, the charge-ordered state exhibits a remarkable characteristic, i.e., anomalous symmetry breaking, which is tied to the topological nature of the electronic band structure. Here, we report the third-order nonlinear longitudinal and Hall responses that persist stably up to room temperature in the kagome material CsV3Sb5. Notably, the nonlinear responses demonstrate significant transition below the charge density wave (∼77 K) order and anomalous symmetry-breaking (∼39 K) state. The scaling analysis indicates that the third-order nonlinear transport is governed jointly by the quantum geometric contribution and extrinsic scattering. This study advances the understanding of the third-order nonlinear transport and provides a distinct method to detect anomalous symmetry breaking in CsV3Sb5.

title: Получение карбоната кальция с заданными свойствами крупности как фактор эффективной утилизации техногенного гипсосодержащего сырья
abstractText: This study focuses on developing a method for utilizing phosphogypsum, a large-tonnage waste product from phosphate raw material processing, whose disposal sites are sources of complex negative impacts on the environment. As a promising approach to the utilization of gypsum-containing waste, the study considers the interaction of phosphogypsum with a sodium carbonate solution (carbonate conversion), which yields calcium carbonate, a marketable product referred to as phosphochalk. Existing technologies typically produce a fine-grained material, which hinders filtration and restricts the potential applications of phosphochalk. This study aims to determine the carbonate conversion parameters that enable the production of phosphochalk with tailored particle size characteristics while maintaining a high degree of feedstock conversion. A series of single-factor experiments was carried out to evaluate the influence of reaction conditions – temperature, Na2CO3 concentration in the carbonate solution, liquid-to-solid (L:S) ratio, and phase contact time – on the conversion of CaSO4·2H2O. The results showed that raising the conversion temperature to 90-100 °C and increasing the L:S ratio to 10 promote intensive nucleation of CaCO3 crystals and the formation of large agglomerates. A Na2CO3 concentration of 250 g/dm3 and a phase contact time of up to 3 h together yield phosphochalk with a particle size of D90 = 45 μm at a conversion degree of 98.8 %. In terms of its characteristics, the resulting product is suitable for use in the metallurgical industry as a raw material for flux production, which demonstrates its competitiveness in the secondary raw materials market. The recommendations developed in this work enable the design of a low-waste technology for processing technogenic raw materials, consistent with the principles of sustainable development and helping to reduce the environmental burden.

title: From potential value to recognised value: situational value theory
abstractText: Purpose To develop Situational Value Theory (SVT), a conceptual explanation of how the value potential of human capability becomes organisationally realised under particular situational conditions. The paper addresses the limited understanding of why equivalent capabilities generate markedly different organisational value despite no substantive change in their underlying knowledge, skills, or behaviours. Design/methodology/approach This paper adopts a conceptual theory-building approach. It synthesises literature on human capability, organisational value, and valuation to develop SVT. The theory distinguishes between value potential, the latent capacity of human capability to contribute to organisational outcomes, and organisationally realised value, which emerges through the interaction of capability, situational conditions, and recognition. Findings SVT proposes that organisational value is not a stable property of individuals or competencies but is realised through the alignment of capability with situational conditions and the recognition of contribution by organisational actors. The theory explains why human capabilities generate different organisational value across contexts without assuming changes in the capabilities themselves. Originality/value SVT reconceptualises the relationship between human capability and organisational value by explaining not how human capability creates organisational value, but how the value potential of human capability becomes organisationally realised. In doing so, the theory provides a new conceptual foundation for understanding organisational evaluation, capability utilisation, and the situational realisation of human value potential.

title: A COMPARATIVE STUDY OF PROPRIOCEPTIVE NEUROMUSCULAR FACILITATION (PNF) VERSUS GOLDFISH EXERCISE IN REDUCING PAIN AND IMPROVING RANGE OF MOTION AMONG PATIENTS WITH TEMPOROMANDIBULAR JOINT DYSFUNCTION
abstractText: Background: Temporomandibular disorders (TMD) are a collective term for conditions affecting the temporomandibular joint (TMJ), the masticatory muscles, and associated structures, characterised by pain, joint sounds, and restricted mandibular movement. Reported prevalence in the adult population ranges from approximately 20% to 31%, with a higher occurrence in women and in individuals aged 20–40 years. Aim: To compare the effectiveness of proprioceptive neuromuscular facilitation (PNF) and Goldfish exercise in reducing pain and improving range of motion (ROM) among patients with TMJ dysfunction. Methodology: A comparative experimental study was conducted on 30 participants aged 20–50 years with myogenic TMJ pain, randomly allocated into two equal groups. Group A (n = 15) received PNF and Group B (n = 15) received Goldfish exercise, five sessions a week for six weeks. Outcome Measures: Pain was assessed using the Visual Analogue Scale (VAS), and jaw mobility was assessed using maximum mouth opening (MMO), measured in millimetres. Results: Both groups showed a statistically significant reduction in pain and improvement in ROM from pre- to post-intervention (p < 0.001). The improvement was greater in Group A than in Group B. Conclusion: Both PNF and Goldfish exercise are effective in reducing pain and improving ROM in TMJ dysfunction, but PNF produced a greater improvement.

title: A CASE REPORT ON MANAGEMENT OF RECURRENT ACNE VULGARIS WITH RAKTAMOKSHANA AND SHAMANA THERAPY
abstractText: Acne is a prevalent chronic inflammatory condition mostly affecting teenagers and young adults, According to Ayurveda, Yuvanpidika, a condition linked to Kapha, Vata, and Rakta involvement may be connected to Acne Vulgaris. For the treatment of such problems, several Shodhana and Shamana therapies are described. A 24-year-old female patient complained of acne over back that had been present for one year, accompanied by papules, pustules, sporadic pain, and post-inflammatory pigmentation. Based on clinical evaluation and Ayurvedic investigation the illness was identified as Yuvanpidika. Following a suitable clinical evaluation and informed permission, Raktamokshana was scheduled as part of the treatment along with internal medication Manjisthadi kwatha. Clinical indicators, including the number of papules and pustules, pain/tenderness, erythema, and post-inflammatory pigmentation, were used to evaluate the patient both before and after treatment. The purpose of the case study is to demonstrate that Raktamokshana actively contributes to the treatment of recurrent Acne Vulgaris. It was found that the Ayurvedic Score based on the data of Ayurvedic clinical assessment of the treatment of various lesions, proposed in this study, as a function of treatment duration is more reliable than the Global Acne Grading Score obtained from the data of baseline value based on the assessment criteria of most severe lesions.

title: REGULATORY REQUIREMENTS FOR NASAL PRODUCTS AS PER CDSCO IN INDIA COMPARISON WITH GERMANY
abstractText: Drugs administered intranasally represent a viable alternative to parenteral delivery, serving as an effective option for medicines with low oral bioavailability due to gastrointestinal tract degradation or extensive first-pass metabolism. Enzymatic deactivation is a significant issue for polypeptide medicines; thus, the nasal route—offering low enzymatic activity and vascularized tissues with strong blood flow—serves as a non-invasive alternative to injections. The nasal membrane absorbs small drug molecules rapidly, while absorption of larger molecules can be augmented via mucociliary clearance modulation or permeation enhancers. Beyond systemic delivery, the nasal route presents opportunities for targeted central nervous system (CNS) transport bypassing the blood-brain barrier. This review evaluates the anatomical and physiological principles of the nasal cavity, categorizes drug delivery systems, and compares the regulatory requirements for import, manufacturing, sale, and export between India (Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation [CDSCO]) and Germany (Federal Institute for Drugs and Medical Devices [BfArM] / European Medicines Agency [EMA]).

title: REGULATORY REQUIREMENTS ON PHARMACOVIGILANCE AS PER CDSCO IN INDIA COMAPARISON WITH NEW ZEALAND
abstractText: Pharmacovigilance is an essential component of medicine safety that involves the Detection, assessment, understanding, and prevention of adverse drug reaction and other medicine-related problems. In India CDSCO regulates post-marketing drug safety activities through requirements for marketing authorization holders [MAHs], individual case safety reports [ICSRs], periodic safety update reports [PSURs], signal detection, risk management, and pharmacovigilance system. CDSCO’S current post-marketing framework includes guidance for MAHs and electronic PSUR submission through the SUGAM portal. In New Zealand pharmacovigilance is regulated primarily by Medsafe with safety monitoring supported by the center for adverse reactions monitoring. Sponsors are required to maintain system for collecting and evaluating adverse reaction information and to report valid serious ICSRs occuring in New Zealand generally within 15 days calendar days of receipt the comparison examines regulatory authorities ADR/ICSR reporting requirements, reporting timeline, safety monitoring, signal detection, and responsibilities of pharmaceutical companies. Overall the study highlights similarities and differences in the two national systems and emphasizes and importance of effective post-marketing surveillance for ensuring the continued safe and rational use of medicines

title: REGULATORY REQUIREMENTS ON PARENTERAL DOSAGE FORMS AS PER CDSCO IN INDIA COMPARISON WITH JAPAN
abstractText: Parenteral dosage forms are sterile pharmaceutical preparations administered by injection, infusion or implantation and are used when rapid onset, high bioavailability, accurate dosing or an alternative to the gastrointestinal route is required. Since these products bypass many natural barriers to infection, regulatory control focuses strongly on sterility assurance, contamination prevention, product quality and patient safety. This review summarizes the regulatory requirements applicable to parenteral dosage forms in India and compares this with the framework of Japan. This review is based primarily on the regulatory and technical material compiled within the source thesis and supplemented by the current official information of the Central Drugs Standard Control Organization (CDSCO), the Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency (PMDA) and the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW). In India, the regulatory framework consists of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act and Rules, New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019 and Schedule M requirements for sterile manufacturing. In Japan, the regulatory oversight is shared between MHLW and PMDA under the Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Act framework with Japanese Pharmacopoeia and GMP requirements supporting quality assurance. Both systems focus on aseptic processing, sterilization, sterility testing, bacterial endotoxin control, particulate control, container-closure integrity, validation, documentation and post-marketing safety. The comparison suggests substantial alignment with international pharmaceutical quality principles as well as differences in regulatory structure, pharmacopoeias references, approval pathways and post-marketing systems.

title: A STAGED SIX-WEEK AYURVEDIC PROTOCOL FOR PSORIASIS (KITIBHA/EKAKUSHTHA) USING KRIMIKUTHARA RASA, GANDHAKA RASAYANA, PARIPATHADI KASHAYA, PANCHATIKTA KASHAYA, KAMADUGDHA RASA, AROGYAVARDHINI RASA, AND NITYA VIRECHANA WITH TRIPHALA CHURNA
abstractText: Psoriasis is a chronic relapsing inflammatory skin disease characterized by erythematous plaques, adherent scaling, itching, dryness, and variable psychosocial burden. In Ayurveda, a number of such clinical features may be interpreted under the broad disease category of Kushtha, especially Kitibha Kushtha and Ekakushtha. Classical Ayurvedic management of Kushtha emphasizes nidana parivarjana (avoidance of causative factors), correction of impaired agni, ama pachana, shodhana where appropriate, shamana oushadhi, external care, and long-term rasayana support. This article presents a staged, six-week, physician-supervised management plan. The first fortnight is designed to address krimi, kleda, ama, kapha-pitta aggravation, and pruritus through Krimikuthara Rasa, Gandhaka Rasayana, and Paripathadi Kashaya. During the second fortnight, Gandhaka Rasayana, Kamadugdha Rasa, and Panchatikta Kashaya are used with emphasis on pitta-rakta shamana, kushthaghna, and twak-prasadana measures. The final fortnight employs Arogyavardhini Rasa and Gandhaka Rasayana to support agni, meda-kleda regulation, and chronic kushtha control. Mild daily bowel regulation with carefully titrated Triphala Churna is proposed as a form of mridu/nitya virechana only in appropriately selected patients. The regimen must not replace evidence-based dermatological assessment, and objective outcomes such as PASI/BSA, itch score, lesion photographs, bowel frequency, adverse effects, and laboratory safety should be documented.

title: PLANT-DERIVED BIOACTIVES FOR DANDRUFF MANAGEMENT: PHYTOCHEMISTRY, ANTIFUNGAL MECHANISMS AND MODERN FORMULATION STRATEGIES
abstractText: Dandruff is a common chronic scalp disorder characterised by excessive shedding of superficial scalp skin, producing visible flakes accompanied by itching, irritation, and mild inflammation. It commonly develops after puberty and is associated with interactions among Malassezia yeasts, sebaceous gland activity, scalp-barrier function, and individual susceptibility. Although dandruff shares features with seborrheic dermatitis, dandruff is generally limited to scaling and itching, whereas seborrheic dermatitis involves more prominent erythema and inflammation and may affect other sebaceous areas.[1-3,8]

title: AN AYURVEDIC REVIEW OF ETIOPATHOGENESIS AND MANAGEMENT OF PRAMEHA (DIABETES MELLITUS)
abstractText: Prameha is a major metabolic disorder described in Ayurveda, characterized by excessive quantity and abnormal quality of urine along with progressive disturbance of Dosha, Dhatu, Agni, and Srotas. Classical Ayurvedic texts explain Prameha as a Tridoshaja disorder with predominant Kapha involvement and significant association with Meda Dhatu and Mutravaha Srotas. Twenty varieties of Prameha have been described based on Dosha predominance, among which Madhumeha represents an advanced stage associated with Vata predominance and tissue depletion. The disease is considered a systemic metabolic derangement rather than a condition limited to urinary abnormality. Excessive intake of Kapha-promoting foods, sedentary lifestyle, obesity, excessive sleep, and hereditary factors are described as important causes.

title: ASSESS THE PROPORTION AND CONTRIBUTING FACTORS OF MIGRAINE AMONG NURSING STUDENTS
abstractText: The Present Study Was Conducted To Assess The Proportion And Contributing Factors Of Migraine Among Nursing Students In Selected Colleges Of Kollam District. A Quantitative Descriptive Research Design Was Adopted. A Total Of 400 Nursing Students Were Selected Using Convenience Sampling Technique. Data Were Collected Using A Socio Demographic Questionnaire, A Standardized Migraine Screening Tool, And A Self-Structured Questionnaire To Identify Contributing Factors. The Majority Of Participants Were Females (83.8%) And Belonged To The Age Group Of 20–22 Years (57.3%). The Findings Revealed That 16.8% Of Nursing Students Screened Positive For Migraine, While 83.3% Screened Negative. Among Students With Migraine, 67.2% Had Intermediate Contributing Factors, 19.4% Had Major Factors, And 13.4% Had Minor Factors. Major Contributing Factors Identified Were Lack Of Sleep, Exposure To Bright Light, And Loud Noise, While Factors Such As Prolonged Study Hours, Academic Stress, And Screen Usage Showed Moderate Influence. Caffeinated Drinks And Weather Changes Were Found To Have Minimal Impact. A Statistically Significant Association Was Found Between Migraine And Gender, Year Of Study, And Family History Of Migraine (P < 0.05). However, No Significant Association Was Observed Between Contributing Factors And Most Socio Demographic Variables, Except History Of Chronic Illness. The Study Concludes That Migraine Among Nursing Students Is Influenced By Both Biological And Lifestyle Factors, Particularly Sleep Disturbances And Academic-Related Stress. Early Identification, Effective Stress Ix Management, And Promotion Of Healthy Lifestyle Practices Are Essential To Reduce The Burden Of Migraine. The Findings Highlight The Need For Awareness Programs And Supportive Interventions Within Educational Institutions To Improve The Overall Well-Being And Academic Performance Of Nursing Students.

title: A PHARMACEUTICO-ANALYTICAL STUDY OF PRIYANGVADI MOUTHWASH WITH REFERENCE TO SHEETADA (GINGIVITIS)
abstractText: Oral diseases such as gingivitis and plaque-induced inflammation are among the most common conditions affecting oral health. Although several chemical mouthwashes are available, their prolonged use may be associated with undesirable effects, creating a need for safe and effective herbal alternatives. The present study aimed to formulate and evaluate an herbal mouthwash using Priyangu (Callicarpa macrophylla), Musta (Cyperus rotundus), and Triphala (Terminalia chebula, Terminalia bellirica, and Emblica officinalis). These Ayurvedic drugs are traditionally known for their anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, antioxidant, wound-healing, and astringent properties, making them suitable for maintaining oral hygiene and managing gingival disorders. The mouthwash was prepared using standard pharmaceutical procedures and evaluated for its organoleptic characteristics and physicochemical parameters. The formulation exhibited acceptable appearance, odor and taste. The combined action of Priyangu, Musta, and Triphala may help reduce plaque accumulation, gingival inflammation, microbial growth, and oral discomfort while promoting overall oral health. The study suggests that Priyangvadi Mouthwash is a promising, cost-effective, and patient-friendly herbal formulation for oral care and may serve as a potential adjunct in the management of gingivitis and maintenance of oral hygiene.

title: PHYTOCHEMICAL SCREENING AND IN VITRO EVALUATION OF THE ANTI-UROLITHIASIS ACTIVITY OF ETHANOLIC EXTRACT OF CROSSANDRA INFUNDIBULIFORMIS FLOWERS
abstractText: Urolithiasis is a common urinary tract disorder characterized by the formation and aggregation of crystalline stones, with calcium oxalate being the predominant type of urinary stone. The present study aimed to evaluate the in-vitro anti-urolithiasis activity of the ethanolic flower extract of Crossandra infundibuliformis and to investigate its phytochemical constituents. The flowers of Crossandra infundibuliformis were collected, authenticated, shade-dried and powdered, followed by Soxhlet extraction using ethanol. The percentage yield of the obtained ethanolic flower extract was found to be 28.6%. Preliminary phytochemical screening revealed the presence of tannins, phenols, reducing sugars, cholesterol, terpenoids, carotenoids and resins, while alkaloids, flavonoids, steroids, carbohydrates, proteins, glycosides, saponins and phytosterols were not detected. The in-vitro anti-urolithiatic activity was evaluated by assessing the inhibition of calcium oxalate crystal aggregation at different concentrations of the extract (10, 50, 100, 250 and 500 µg/mL) and compared with Cystone as the standard drug. The ethanolic flower extract exhibited concentration-dependent inhibition of calcium oxalate crystal aggregation, with mean percentage inhibition of 30.554%, 43.267%, 49.781%, 55.591% and 61.740% at 10, 50, 100, 250 and 500 µg/mL, respectively. Cystone showed a mean inhibition of 81.259%. The observed anti-urolithiatic activity may be associated with the phytoconstituents present in the extract, particularly tannins, phenols and terpenoids. Overall, the findings suggest that the ethanolic flower extract of Crossandra infundibuliformis possesses promising concentration-dependent in-vitro anti-urolithiatic activity against calcium oxalate crystal aggregation. Further experimental studies are required to validate its therapeutic potential.

title: EFFECTS OF ETHANOL LEAF EXTRACT OF Spondia mombin ON SURGICALLY-INDUCED DUODENAL ULCER IN ADULT MALE WISTAR-RATS
abstractText: Background: Duodenal ulcer (DU) is a common gastrointestinal disorder resulting from disruption of the balance between aggressive factors and mucosal protective mechanisms. Although Spondias mombin has demonstrated gastroprotective and ulcer-healing properties, limited information is available regarding its effects on surgically-induced DU and duodenal histoarchitecture. This study investigated the effects of ethanol leaf extract of Spondias mombin on surgically induced DU in adult male Wistar rats. Methods: Thirty Wistar rats were randomly divided into six groups of five rats each. DU was induced in Groups II–VI by submucosal injection of 0.02 mL of 20% acetic acid. Group I is the normal control which received only normal saline (1 mL/kg) orally for 15 days. Group II served as the ulcer control and was sacrificed 24 h after ulcer induction, while Group III received normal saline (1 mL/kg) orally for 14 days as the recovery group. Groups IV–VI received ethanol leaf extract of S. mombin at 200, 400, and 800 mg/kg body weight, respectively, for 14 days. Duodenal tissues were assessed using haematoxylin and eosin (H&E) and Masson's trichrome staining. Results: The normal control group showed relatively intact and well-developed villous architecture with preserved glandular and connective-tissue organization. The ulcer control group demonstrated marked mucosal disruption, characterized by irregular, shortened, blunted and eroded villi, with architectural disorganization. The recovery group showed partial restoration of the duodenal architecture. Treatment with ethanol leaf extract of S. mombin resulted in progressive improvement in villous tissue organization, with the 800 mg/kg group showing the most pronounced morphological restoration and features comparatively closer to the normal control. Masson's trichrome staining demonstrated differences in collagen distribution and organization, consistent with connective-tissue remodeling during mucosal repair. Conclusion: Ethanol leaf extract of Spondias mombin restored the injured duodenal tissue, providing a beneficial effect on the histoarchitecture of acetic-acid-induced duodenal ulcer in Wistar rats.

title: DEVELOPMENT AND EVALUATION OF AN ARTEMISIA ANNUA HERBAL GEL FOR ANTIMICROBIAL ACTIVITY
abstractText: The present study was undertaken with the aim of developing and evaluating an Artemisia annua L. herbal gel for antimicrobial activity. The aerial parts of A. annua were collected from Bagsiad, Mandi, Himachal Pradesh, during September 2025 and authenticated by a qualified botanist. The collected plant material was shade-dried, powdered, and extracted with ethanol using the Soxhlet extraction method. The prepared extract was subjected to loss on drying and preliminary phytochemical screening to identify the major classes of secondary metabolites. The ethanolic extract was subsequently incorporated into Carbopol 940-based topical gel formulations. Five formulations (F1–F5) were prepared using different concentrations of Carbopol 940 and propylene glycol, while methyl paraben, propyl paraben, and triethanolamine were used as preservatives and pH-adjusting/neutralizing agents. The prepared formulations were evaluated for physical appearance, homogeneity, pH, viscosity, spreadability, and extrudability. Among the formulations, F2 was selected as the optimized formulation based on its overall physicochemical properties. F2 showed a smooth and homogeneous appearance, pH of 5.80 ± 0.046, viscosity of 1285 ± 15.2 cP, spreadability of 6.80 ± 0.08, and excellent extrudability. The optimized formulation was further evaluated for in-vitro antibacterial activity using the agar disc diffusion method against Escherichia coli, Staphylococcus aureus, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa. F2 exhibited zones of inhibition of 10 mm against E. coli and 11 mm against P. aeruginosa, whereas no zone of inhibition was observed against S. aureus under the experimental conditions. The findings indicate that the ethanolic extract of A. annua can be successfully incorporated into a Carbopol 940-based topical gel with acceptable physicochemical characteristics and measurable antibacterial activity. The developed F2 formulation may therefore have potential as a topical herbal antimicrobial preparation. Further studies are recommended to evaluate its stability, safety, skin irritation, drug release, permeation, and antimicrobial efficacy against a broader range of microorganisms.

title: RESEARCH ARTICLE ON CLINICAL STUDY ON THE EFFECT OF SHANKHPUSHPI (CONVOLVULUS PLURICAULIS) AS MEDHYA RASAYANA IN REDUCING EXAMINATION STRESS AMONG UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS USING PSS, PSQI, AND DIGIT SPAN TEST
abstractText: background: Academic examination stress is common among undergraduate students and is often associated with impaired cognitive function, poor sleep quality, and reduced academic performance. In Ayurveda, shankhpushpi (Convolvulus pluricaulis) is described as a medhya rasayana, traditionally used to enhance memory, intellect, and mental well-being. However, clinical evidence supporting its role in managing examination stress is limited. Objective: To evaluate the effect of Shankhpushpi on perceived stress, sleep quality, and cognitive performance among undergraduate students during examination periods. Methods: The present study adopted a comparative interventional approach and included a total of 60 undergraduate students. Participants were assigned into two groups of equal size, with one group receiving Shankhpushpi as the intervention and the other group undergoing standard counselling without any pharmacological treatment. Evaluation of outcomes was performed using established assessment tools, namely the Perceived Stress Scale (PSS) for measuring stress levels, the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) for assessing sleep patterns, and the Digit Span Test for evaluating cognitive function. Data collected before and after the intervention period were analyzed to determine changes within each group as well as differences between the two groups, applying suitable statistical techniques. Results: The intervention group demonstrated a significant reduction in perceived stress scores along with improvement in sleep quality and cognitive performance following administration of Shankhpushpi. In contrast, the control group showed only minimal changes in these parameters. Conclusion: The findings of the study provide evidence supporting the effectiveness of Shankhpushpi as a Medhya Rasayana in reducing examination-related stress and improving sleep quality and cognitive performance among undergraduate students.

title: COMPARATIVE PHYTOCHEMICAL, NUTRITIVE AND MEDICINAL ANALYSIS OF PITHECELLOBIUM DULCE AND MORINGA OLEIFERA: THE UNTAPPED POTENTIAL OF INDIGENOUS SPECIES
abstractText: Indigenous plants have long served as critical sources of nutrition and traditional medicine. Among them, Moringa oleifera is widely recognized for its exceptional nutritional and medicinal properties, leading to its extensive cultivation and commercialization. In contrast, Pithecellobium dulce, though traditionally used in various folk remedies, remains largely underexplored and underutilized despite its widespread availability in tropical regions. The present paper is designed to emphasize the importance of scientifically validating indigenous and neglected species. It seeks to comparatively analyze the phytochemical, nutritive, and medicinal attributes of P. dulce and M. oleifera with the aim of evaluating their potential health benefits. By doing so, the paper aims to determine whether P. dulce can emerge as a promising alternative to the more established M. oleifera, particularly in the context of affordable and sustainable plant-based therapeutics and nutrition. This paper is significant in its potential to promote biodiversity-based food and medicine systems, encourage the use of locally available plant resources, and contribute to the broader goals of food security, traditional knowledge preservation, and alternative medicine development.

title: DYKE DAVIDOFF MASSON SYNDROME IN A FUNCTIONALLY INDEPENDENT ADULT WITH CHILDHOOD ONSET HEMIPARESIS: A CASE REPORT
abstractText: Dyke-Davidoff-Masson syndrome (DDMS) is a rare neurological disorder characterized by cerebral hemiatrophy, contralateral hemiparesis, facial asymmetry, and recurrent seizures. It typically presents during childhood, while diagnosis in adulthood is uncommon, particularly in individuals who remain functionally independent. We report the case of a 37-year-old male with childhood-onset hemiparesis who remained ambulatory and independent in activities of daily living. The diagnosis of DDMS was established incidentally on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) during evaluation for an unrelated illness. This case highlights the variable clinical spectrum of DDMS and emphasizes that mild cases may remain undiagnosed until adulthood.

title: ANXIOLYTIC PROPERTY OF CAESALPINIA PULCHERRIMA LEAVES EXTRACT IN EXPERIMENTAL ANIMALS
abstractText: Objectives: To evaluate the anxiolytic property of ethanolic extract of leaves of Caesalpinia pulcherrima in Albino Wistar rats and Swiss Albino mice. Methods: The anxiolytic activity was evaluated using behavioral models of anxiety like elevated plus maze test, light-dark transition test, hole board test and open field test. The ethanolic extract was screened for toxicity by acute oral toxicity studies according to OECD guidelines 425 for selection of dose. Results: Compared to control group, animals in diazepam (2mg/kg i.p) treated group and the extract (ethanolic 800mg/kg p.o) treated groups revealed a statistically significant increase in anxiolytic activity. (ethanolic extract at 400mg/kg was statistically not significant except in light/dark transition test). Conclusion: Ethanolic extract showed significant dose dependent anxiolytic effect. Phytochemical screening revealed presence of flavonoids, and saponins as major constituents. The results suggest that the ethanolic extract (800mg/kg) of CP leaves seems to possess pronounced anxiolytic effect with lower sedative activity than the ethanolic extract (400mg/kg) when compared to diazepam. The results could be attributed to the flavonoids content (quercetin and sitosterol) of the ethanolic extract.

title: ANATOMICAL UNDERSTANDING OF BHUJANGASANA IN INITIAL STAGES OF LUMBAR SPONDYLOSIS
abstractText: Lumbar spondylosis, a degenerative condition affecting the intervertebral discs and facet joints of the lower spine, commonly presents with chronic low back pain, stiffness, and restricted mobility. In Ayurvedic and yogic rehabilitation, Bhujangāsana (Cobra Pose) is widely recommended as a therapeutic posture due to its spinal extension and strengthening effects. This asana gently mobilizes the lumbar vertebrae, stretches the anterior spinal structures, and strengthens the paraspinal and gluteal muscles, thereby improving lumbar stability. Regular practice helps to enhance inter vertebral space, reduce nerve root compression, and promote better postural alignment. Additionally, Bhujangasana increases blood circulation to the lumbosacral region, supports disc nutrition, and reduces muscular spasm. It's mindful breathing component further decreases pain perception by reducing stress-related muscle tension. Overall, Bhujangasana serves as an effective, non-invasive adjunct in the conservative management of lumbar spondylosis, contributing to pain reduction, improved flexibility, and enhanced functional outcomes. This article focuses on the anatomy and pathophysiology of lumbar spondylosis, its symptomatolgy and role of bhujangasana in it's management.

title: FORMULATION AND EVALUATION OF SUSTAINED RELEASE MATRIX TABLET OF ONDANSETRON USING NATURAL POLYMERS: REVIEW
abstractText: Ondansetron is a widely used antiemetic with a short half-life, requiring frequent dosing. Sustained release (SR) matrix tablets prepared using natural polymers offer an effective approach to prolong drug release, improve patient compliance, and maintain therapeutic drug levels. Natural polymers such as xanthan gum, guar gum, sodium alginate, gum acacia, and HPMC-based combinations are biodegradable, biocompatible, cost-effective, and environmentally friendly. Recent advances in natural polymer-based SR matrix tablets have focused on optimizing drug release, enhancing tablet stability, and improving bioavailability. This review highlights the formulation strategies, evaluation methods, advantages, and prospects of natural polymer-based sustained release matrix tablets of ondansetron, emphasizing their potential as safe and effective oral drug delivery systems.

title: CURRENT AND EMERGING PHARMACOTHERAPY FOR DYSLIPIDEMIA: A COMPREHENSIVE STUDY
abstractText: Dyslipidemia is a primary driver of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. While statins reduce LDL-C and cardiovascular events, statin intolerance and failure to achieve guideline targets limit their utility. To review the mechanism, efficacy, safety, and clinical positioning of current and emerging antihyperlipidemic agents as of May 2026. High-intensity statins remain first-line with 50-60% LDL-C reduction. Ezetimibe and bempedoic acid provide incremental LDL-C lowering of 15-28% without muscle toxicity. PCSK9 inhibitors and inclisiran achieve 50-60% reduction via distinct mechanisms, with inclisiran offering twice-yearly dosing. Bempedoic acid and inclisiran demonstrated cardiovascular outcome benefit in statin-intolerant populations. Gene editing therapy VERVE-101 showed single-dose LDL-C reductions of 39-55% in early trials. Therapeutic options now address statin intolerance, adherence barriers, and residual risk. A stepwise algorithm starting with oral agents and escalating to RNA-based therapies optimizes outcomes and resource use.

title: REGULATORY REQUIREMENTS FOR THE APPROVAL OF NARCOTIC DRUGS AS PER CDSCO IN INDIA IN COMPARISON WITH CANADA
abstractText: Narcotic drugs, derived largely from the opium poppy, have powerful pain-relieving effects but also carry a high risk of addiction. Therefore, most countries place strict controls on the manufacturing, trading, and use of these drugs. This report examines the regulatory frameworks governing narcotic drugs in India and Canada, alongside the international classification set out by the 1961 UN Single Convention. India relies on the NDPS Act, along with specialized bodies such as the CBN and NCB, working alongside the general regulator, CDSCO. Canada regulates narcotics mainly through Health Canada and the CDSA, using a single permit-based system under the Narcotic Control Regulations. The comparison highlights how each country licenses the manufacturing, import, export, and sale of narcotic drugs, and what these differences reveal about their regulatory approaches.

title: CLINICAL EVALUATION OF KAMPILLAKADI TAILA IN DUSHTA- VRANA
abstractText: According to Ayurveda, every Vikriti is brought on by a disruption in Doshas, which in turn leads to the dysfunction of Dhatus and Srotas. These disturbances may produce ideal circumstances for the emergence of chronic illnesses. Similarly, Vrana is caused not just by the individual vitiated Dosha, but also with the combined vitiation of Dhatu, Srotas and some external factors. The clinical trial, titled “Clinical Evaluation of Kampillakadi Taila in Dushta-Vrana” aimed to evaluate the clinical efficacy of classical Ayurvedic formulation in the management of Dushta-Vrana. Total 34 patients were taken on the basis of diagnostic criteria based on inclusion and exclusion criteria. Kampillakadi Taila was applied locally, according to the size of Dushta-Vrana with the help of specially designed frame (Vrana-vasti) 15 minutes, once daily. Dressing was done with sterile bandage and changed daily. Assessment of therapeutic outcomes was conducted using subjective parameters (pain, itching) and objective parameters (tenderness, foul smell, floor/granulation tissue, size and discharges), with statistical analysis performed to evaluate the efficacy of Taila. The results demonstrated that the treatment was highly effective, with 73.5% of patients achieving complete or marked relief, and all patients demonstrating some degree of clinical improvement with no complications or recurrences during the treatment or follow up period.

title: TOXICOLOGICAL AND ANTI-TRYPANOSOMAL EVALUATION OF POLYMER CONJUGATES OF EFAVIRENZ, TENOFOVIR, AND DOLUTEGRAVIR
abstractText: Background and purpose: Trypanosomes are parasitic protozoa that cause Chagas disease in central and South America and sleeping sickness in sub-Saharan Africa leading to morbidity and mortality of millions of people. T. brucei gambiense accounts for more than 95% of reported cases and endemic in 36 sub -Saharan African countries. The of the study is to determine the toxicological and anti-trypanosomal evaluation of polymer conjugates of efavirenz, tenofovir, and dolutegravir. Method: Toxicity testing and LD50 determination of the Conjugates were carried out using lorke’s method and after which anti-Trypanosoma evaluation was carried out by using a seven-day Trypanosoma brucei suppressive test in albino rat. Statistical analysis using one way ANOVA was carried out where differences with values of p<0.05 were considered statistically significant. Result: From the lorke’s method carried out, Doses of the drug conjugates of 10 -5000mg/kg witnesses no mortality within 24 hours indicating the safety of the drug conjugates (Tenofovir-Chitosan, Efavirenz-Chitosan and Dolutegravir-Alginate). Histological investigation of the Wister rat kidney and liver used for the toxicological study, revealed healthy kidney glomeruli and capillaries and healthy liver hepatocytes at doses between 10-4000mg/kg but at 5000mg/kg, the architecture of the liver revealed mild infiltrating leukocytes and piecemeal necrosis with sinusoid hepatocytes. The drug conjugates (Efavirenz-chitosan, Tenofovir-chitosan and Dolutegravir-alginate) screened against the Trypanosoma parasites had a significant increased ant-Trypanosoma activity compared to the drug alone (Tenofovir, Efavirenz and Dolutegravir), this might be probably due to the synergistic effect of the polymer used in the conjugation. Conclusion: the present study showed that the conjugates of dolutegravir, efavirenz and tenofovir may be considered as comparatively safe of toxicity as none of the conjugates produced any haematological challenge and no distortion of the architecture of the tissue. The study corroborated the application of the drug conjugates as better antitrypanosomal agent with lowest toxicity effect when compared with the melarsoprol, eflornithine, pentamidine and suramin.

title: BRIDGING ANCIENT WISDOM AND MOLECULAR MEDICINE: CLINICAL APPLICATIONS OF CORE AYURVEDIC SIDDHANTAS IN CONTEMPORARY PATHOPHYSIOLOGY
abstractText: Ayurveda, the ancient science of life, relies on foundational philosophical and clinical principles known as Siddhantas. While traditionally viewed through a purely historical or qualitative lens, these principles offer profound correlations with modern molecular biology, systems biology, and chronic disease pathogenesis. This article provides a critical analysis of four core Siddhantas—Lok-Purusha Samya Siddhanta (macrocosm-microcosm correspondence), Kriya Kala Siddhanta (six stages of pathogenesis), Agni Siddhanta (metabolic fire and enzymatic integrity), and Srotas Siddhanta (systemic channels and microcirculation). This translational synthesis aims to establish a rigorous scientific foundation for personalized, systems-oriented clinical practice.

title: PERI-SURGICAL PROCEDURES: A BOOK
abstractText: Surgery is one of the most important fields of modern medicine. It combines scientific knowledge, technical skill, patient care, safety, and continuous innovation. Over time, surgical practice has advanced from basic procedures to highly developed techniques supported by anesthesia, antisepsis, imaging, minimally invasive methods, and robotic technology. The purpose of this book “Peri-Surgical Procedures” is to provide a clear and structured understanding of how surgical procedures are planned, performed, monitored, and managed. title: AN UNEXPECTED COMPLICATION OF FOLK MEDICINE: ACUTE BULLOUS IRRITANT CONTACT DERMATITIS DUE TO TOPICAL ONION OIL
abstractText: Topical folk remedies are widely used for musculoskeletal complaints despite their potential cutaneous adverse effects. We report a 60-year-old woman who developed severe burning, erythema, and tense bullae on the lower back 6 hours after applying pure onion oil (Allium cepa) for chronic low back pain. Acute bullous irritant contact dermatitis was diagnosed based on the rapid onset and sharply localized distribution. The patient showed marked clinical improvement with substantial re-epithelialization within 20 days following appropriate wound care and topical treatment. This case highlights the potential dermatological hazards of unsupervised herbal remedies and emphasizes that natural products should not be considered inherently harmless.

title: EFFECTIVENESS OF AYURVEDIC INTERVENTION IN ANIDRA (INSOMNIA): A CLINICAL CASE STUDY
abstractText: Introduction: Anidra, referred to as Insomnia in contemporary medicine, is recognized in Ayurveda as a consequence of doshas imbalances, primarily involving Vata, with secondary disturbances In Pitta and Kapha. Habitual sleeplessness or simply inability to sleep for a minimum period, which is necessary for a sound mental and physical health, is called insomnia (Anidra). Acute insomnia is brief and typically occurs due to temporary life circumstances. Aim and Objective: To evaluate the efficacy of Ayurvedic management in Anidra (Insomnia) Material and Method: This is single case study of 28 years old female suffering from sleeplessness for 1 years, sleeping hours of two, this shattered her physical as well as mental condition. She had associated complaints of excessive thoughts, indigestion and headache. Patient sleep was markedly disturbed leading to stress and anxiety hence she visited to our hospital. Treatment given was Shirodhara with Ksheerbala Tail for 45 min for 21 days along with Shamana Chikitsa Saraswatarishta, Chitrakadi Vati and Smritisagar Ras. Results: Patient showed marked improvement in sleep quality and duration. Associated symptoms such as excessive thoughts, stress, anxiety, headache, and indigestion were significantly reduced. Discussion: The significant improvement observed in this patient suggests that a combined Ayurvedic approach involving Shamana chikitsa and Panchkarma can effectively manage chronic insomnia and improve overall well-being. Conclusion: This case study demonstrates the potential effectiveness of Ayurvedic management in the treatment of Anidra (insomnia). The integrated approach comprising Ayurvedic medications and Shirodhara with Ksheerbala Taila and selected Ayurvedic medications resulted in substantial improvement in sleep quality, reduction of associated symptoms, and enhancement of the patient's quality of life.

abstractText: Plants have played an important role in human healthcare and traditional medicine for thousands of years. Ocimum Sanctum is one of them. Ocimum Sanctum contains many active phytoconstituents like; Eugenol, Rosmarinic acid, Ursolic acid, Linalool and Epigenin. title: RESEARCH ON IN-VITRO ANTI-ULCER AND ANTHELMINTIC ACTIVITY BY ETHANOLIC EXTRACT OF IPOMOEA OBSCURA
abstractText: Medicinal plants continue to be a rich source of pharmacologically active compounds, and Ipomoea obscura (L.) Ker Gawl. (Convolvulaceae), a climbing plant used in traditional medicine, is one such species worth closer study given its reported antioxidant, anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties. This study looked at the phytochemical composition of an ethanolic leaf extract of I. obscura alongside its in-vitro anti-ulcer and anthelmintic potential. Leaves were collected and authenticated, then shade-dried, powdered, and extracted using cold maceration with ethanol. Phytochemical screening revealed the presence of carbohydrates, proteins and amino acids, alkaloids, flavonoids, phenolics, tannins, terpenoids, glycosides and saponins; steroids were absent. Anti-ulcer activity was gauged using the acid-neutralizing capacity (ANC) method, with an aluminiumhydroxide–magnesium hydroxide formulation as the reference antacid. The extract yielded ANC values of 116, 64.5, 28.8 and 14.65 mEq/g at concentrations of 100, 200, 500 and 1000 µg/ml, compared to 27.5 mEq/g for the reference at 500 µg/ml. For anthelmintic activity, paralysis and death times were recorded in Pheretima posthuma. At 20 mg/ml, the extract induced paralysis in 12.03 minutes and death in 23.20 minutes close to albendazole's 10.54 and 22.37 minutes at the same concentration with effects becoming more pronounced at higher concentrations, while untreated worms stayed alive for up to 7 hours. Taken together, these results point to genuine acid-neutralizing and anthelmintic activity in the extract, though they represent early-stage in-vitro findings rather than proof of clinical benefit. Confirming any therapeutic releance will require more rigorous mechanistic, toxicological and in-vivo work.

title: A CASE STUDY OF KRIYAKALPA BIDALAKA'S EFFICACY IN BLEPHARITIS
abstractText: Background: Blepharitis is a chronic inflammatory disorder of the eyelid margins characterized by itching, redness, swelling, irritation, and discomfort. Conventional treatment mainly includes eyelid hygiene, antibiotics, and anti-inflammatory agents; however, recurrence is common. In Ayurveda, Bidalaka is a well-described Kriyakalpa indicated in the acute stage of ophthalmic disorders and is believed to reduce inflammation and promote healing. Aim: To evaluate the efficacy of Bidalaka Kriyakalpa in the management of blepharitis. Materials and Methods: A single-case clinical study was conducted in the Department of Shalakyatantra. A 64-year-old male patient presented with itching, swelling of both eyelids, and intermittent redness of both eyes for 15 days. Bidalaka was prepared using Triphala, Yashtimadhu, Haridra, Raktachandana, Spatika, and Sunthi powders mixed with sterile water to form a paste. The formulation was applied over the closed eyelids, excluding the lid margins, once daily for 20 minutes for 14 consecutive days. Clinical assessment was based on changes in itching, swelling, and redness before and after treatment. Results: After treatment, there was a noticeable improvement in clinical outcomes. Redness dramatically decreased from moderate to mild, eyelid swelling decreased, and itching totally disappeared. During the course of the treatment, the patient reported increased eye comfort and no side effects. Conclusion: In this instance of blepharitis, Bidalaka Kriyakalpa showed encouraging therapeutic results by lowering inflammation and easing related symptoms. The process is a useful Ayurvedic treatment option for eyelid diseases because it is easy, safe, economical, and non-invasive. To confirm these results and determine its long-term effectiveness, however, further extensive controlled clinical trials are required.

title: MANAGEMENT OF STHAVARA VISHA W.S.R TO KERALEEYA VISHA CHIKITSA GRANTHAS
abstractText: In Agadatantra, Visha is broadly categorized into two major origin-based classes: Sthavara Visha and Jangama Visha. Sthavara Visha encompasses toxic substances derived from plant sources as well as minerals and metals. Survey data and classical literature highlight that among various Sthavara Visha exposures, Bhallataka (Semecarpus anacardium) poisoning is the commonest reported. Other poisons such as Agnishikha (Gloriosa superba), Datura (Datura metel), and Kupilu (Strychnos nux-vomica) are also frequently encountered. Furthermore, concepts such as Dooshivisha (latent/chronic toxin) and Bhinna Visha (partially neutralized or altered toxin) share close therapeutic parallels with Sthavara Visha, requiring structured management protocols. A conceptual study on how to manage sthavara visha as per Keraleeya visha granthas been carried out in this study.

title: EFFECT OF ANT - RADIATION AGENTS ON SURVIVAL, HAIR, AND SKIN EMBEDMENT OF MALE AND FEMALE MICE EXPOSED TO TWO LETHAL DOSES OF WHOLE BODY GAMMA RADIATION
abstractText: The natural amino acid, 5 – Hydroxytryptophan (5 – HTP) is intermediate metabolite of the essential amino acid tryptophan (Trp). Both 5 –HTP and Trp are precursor of a neurotransmitter serotonin (5 –tryptamine (5 – HT), often called the happiness hormone for its crucial role in regulating mood, sleep, appetite and digestion. The brain uses both tryptophan and 5 – hydroxytryptophan as precursors for serotonin synthesis because both can cross brain blood barrier (BBB), while serotonin found in the plasma cannot pass BBB. Although both Trp and 5 – HTP can cross the brain blood barrier “BBB” and reach the neurogenic neurons in brain where serotonin can be synthesized ,however, 5- hydroxytryptophan is generally recommended over tryptophan because it crosses the” BBB” at higher rate with minimum competition with the branched amino acids.In this study, using mice as widely used and well accepted animal model for such kind of study, the anti-radiation potential of different concentrations of 5 – HTP, alone and in combination with very low and nontoxic concentration of a sulfhydryl compound, S (2 - amino ethyl) isothiouronium bromide hydrobromide (AET) on survival, hair, and skin embedment. Significant encouraging results were obtained regarding survival, hair and skin health in treated animals. Moreover, successive administration three folds of this combination within an hour unwanted effects on survival, hair and skin embedment were observed 30 day after treatment.

title: REGULATORY REQUIREMENTS ON PARENTERAL DOSAGE FORMS AS PER CDSCO IN INDIA COMPARISON WITH JAPAN
abstractText: Parenteral dosage forms are sterile pharmaceutical preparations administered by injection, infusion or implantation and are used when rapid onset, high bioavailability, accurate dosing or an alternative to the gastrointestinal route is required. Since these products bypass many natural barriers to infection, regulatory control focuses strongly on sterility assurance, contamination prevention, product quality and patient safety. This review summarizes the regulatory requirements applicable to parenteral dosage forms in India and compares this with the framework of Japan. This review is based primarily on the regulatory and technical material compiled within the source thesis and supplemented by the current official information of the Central Drugs Standard Control Organization (CDSCO), the Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency (PMDA) and the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW). In India, the regulatory framework consists of the Drugs and Cosmetics Act and Rules, New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules, 2019 and Schedule M requirements for sterile manufacturing. In Japan, the regulatory oversight is shared between MHLW and PMDA under the Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Act framework with Japanese Pharmacopoeia and GMP requirements supporting quality assurance. Both systems focus on aseptic processing, sterilization, sterility testing, bacterial endotoxin control, particulate control, container-closure integrity, validation, documentation and post-marketing safety. The comparison suggests substantial alignment with international pharmaceutical quality principles as well as differences in regulatory structure, pharmacopoeias references, approval pathways and post-marketing systems.

title: INTEGRATIVE MANAGEMENT OF AVASCULAR NECROSIS OF FEMORAL HEAD THROUGH AYURVEDA AND PANCHAKARMA: A CRITICAL REVIEW OF CURRENT EVIDENCE
abstractText: Avascular necrosis (AVN), more precisely termed osteonecrosis of the femoral head (ONFH), is a progressive disorder caused by loss of blood supply to the subchondral bone, leading to osteocyte death, structural weakening, collapse of the femoral head and secondary osteoarthritis. It commonly affects younger adults and may result from corticosteroid exposure, excessive alcohol intake, trauma, sickle cell disease and several other systemic conditions. Early diagnosis is important because joint-preserving treatment becomes progressively less effective once subchondral fracture and femoral head collapse have occurred. Contemporary evidence supports magnetic resonance imaging as the most accurate imaging modality for early disease, while treatment is selected according to stage, lesion size, location, symptoms and patient factors.[1,2] Ayurveda does not describe AVN as a single classical disease entity. Published Ayurvedic reports have interpreted its clinical presentation through concepts such as Asthi-Majjagata Vata, Asthivaha Srotodushti, Dhatu Kshaya and Vata Prakopa.[3] This correlation remains interpretative and should not be considered an exact classical equivalent of ischemic osteonecrosis. Panchakarma-based management reported in case literature commonly includes Rukshana, Snehana, Swedana, Basti, Ksheera Basti, Shashtika Shali Pinda Sweda and internal medicines intended to address pain, stiffness and tissue depletion.[3,4] The available Ayurvedic evidence is encouraging mainly with respect to symptomatic outcomes such as pain, gait, range of motion and quality of life. However, most publications consist of individual case reports or small uncontrolled studies, and convincing evidence that Ayurveda can reverse necrotic bone, restore vascular supply or prevent structural collapse is currently lacking. Modern joint-preserving treatments such as core decompression, with or without biological augmentation, remain important particularly in pre-collapse disease, while arthroplasty is often required after advanced collapse.[5] This review critically examines the modern pathophysiology and staging of ONFH, its cautious Ayurvedic interpretation, the rationale for Panchakarma interventions, available clinical evidence and opportunities for integrative research. A safe integrative approach should aim to improve pain, function and quality of life while maintaining MRI-based staging and timely orthopedic referral. Future trials require standardized Ayurvedic protocols, validated functional outcomes, serial imaging and long-term follow-up before disease-modifying claims can be justified.

title: AYURVEDIC PROTOCOL IN THE MANAGEMENT OF DIABETIC DYSLIPIDEMIA: ADDRESSING GUT DYSBIOSIS AND METABOLIC IMBALANCE – A CASE REPORT
abstractText: Introduction: Diabetic dyslipidemia, characterized by elevated triglycerides, cholesterol, LDL, and low HDL, is a frequent metabolic abnormality in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus. In India, its prevalence ranges between 60–75% among diabetics, contributing significantly to cardiovascular morbidity. Gut microbiota plays a key role in lipid metabolism through bile acid modulation, short-chain fatty acid production, and inflammatory regulation. Dysbiosis promotes hepatic lipogenesis, reduces HDL synthesis, and aggravates dyslipidemia in diabetes. Diabetic Dyslipidemia can be seen under the lens of Medorogam, arising from Agnimandya, Ama Utpatti, and Kapha Medo Dushti. Aim: To evaluate the efficacy of Ayurvedic Medoroga Chikitsa protocol in the management of diabetic dyslipidemia. Objective: To assess changes in symptoms, BMI, blood glucose, and lipid profile before and after treatment. Methods: In February 2025, a 42-year-old male presented with fatigue, heaviness of body, excessive thirst, sweating, increased micturition, weight gain, exertional dyspnoea, and loss of appetite for one year. He visited the OPD of SJSACH, Chennai, and was diagnosed with Diabetic Dyslipidemia/Medorogam based on blood glucose and lipid profile. Management began with Deepana and Pachana, followed by Udwarthanam, Sadhyo Virechanam, Podikizhi, and Lekhana Kashaya Vasti. Results: Post treatment showed marked reduction in symptoms, blood glucose, and lipid profile, along with mild weight loss. Conclusion: Agni Deepana and Ama Pachana restore Agni and remove Ama, correcting Agnimandya. Shodhana eliminates Kapha, Meda, and Ama; Pathyahara and Vyayama prevent Meda Vriddhi and enhance Dhatvagni. This integrative management may also have favourably modulated gut microbial dysbiosis, supporting metabolic and lipid homeostasis.

title: CLINICAL CORRELATION OF AGNI WITH INSULIN RESISTANCE: AN OBSERVATIONAL STUDY FOLLOWED BY A PILOT CLINICAL INTERVENTION
abstractText: Background: Agni is one of the fundamental concepts of Ayurveda and is considered essential for digestion, transformation and maintenance of physiological homeostasis. Contemporary metabolic disorders such as insulin resistance are characterized by impaired metabolic responsiveness to insulin and frequently precede clinically apparent type 2 diabetes mellitus. Although Agni has traditionally been considered an important determinant of health and disease, objective clinical correlation between Ayurvedic assessment of Agni and modern metabolic indices remains inadequately explored. Objective: The present study was designed in two phases: first, to investigate the relationship between Ayurvedic Agni status and insulin resistance in adults; and second, to conduct a pilot clinical intervention in participants. demonstrating impaired Agni with metabolic risk. Materials and Methods: The study was planned as a two-phase investigation. In Phase I, adults aged 25–55 years were assessed for Agni using a standardized Agni Assessment Scale together with anthropometric and biochemical parameters including body mass index (BMI), waist circumference, fasting plasma glucose, fasting serum insulin, HbA1c, triglycerides and HDL cholesterol. HOMA-IR was calculated from fasting glucose and insulin values. Phase II consisted of a prospective pilot intervention in participants with impaired Agni and elevated metabolic risk. The intervention consisted of individualized Nidana Parivarjana, Agni-oriented dietary regulation, prescribed physical activity and a standardized Ayurvedic Deepana-Pachana intervention. Results: Illustrative pilot data set: In a hypothetical cohort of 60 participants, impaired Agni was expected to demonstrate a positive association with BMI, waist circumference, fasting insulin and HOMA-IR. In the proposed 20-participant pilot intervention, mean HOMA-IR was modeled to decrease from 3.42 ± 0.91 at baseline to 2.71 ± 0.78 after 12 weeks, while mean Agni impairment score improved from 18.6 ± 3.2 to 12.4 ± 3.5. These values are presented solely to demonstrate the intended statistical presentation and must not be represented as actual clinical observations. Conclusion: The proposed two-phase methodology provides a potentially useful framework for investigating the relationship between an Ayurvedic diagnostic construct and a measurable modern metabolic phenotype. Establishing a reproducible relationship between Agni and insulin resistance could contribute to the objective validation and clinical application of Ayurvedic diagnostic principles.

title: ROLE OF SHIRODHARA IN MODULATING NEURODEVELOPMENTAL DISORDERS IN CHILDREN
abstractText: Neurodevelopmental disorders are disabilities associated primarily with the functioning of the neurological system and brain. These disorders typically manifest in early childhood, frequently persist into adulthood, and impose substantial limitations on personal, social, academic, and occupational functioning. Considering the chronic course and profound functional limitations associated with neurodevelopmental disorders, there is a growing emphasis on integrative and complementary therapeutic approaches. Shirodhara, a classical Ayurvedic therapy is traditionally recognized for its tranquilizing and stabilizing influence on the central nervous system. It is postulated to exert regulatory effects on neuroendocrine mechanisms, mitigate stress responses, improve sleep architecture, and enhance cognitive and behavioral modulation.

title: UNDERSTANDING VYANAVATA IN ESSENTIAL HYPERTENSION: A CONCEPTUAL REVIEW
abstractText: Essential hypertension is a leading modifiable risk factor for cardiovascular disease and is rising steadily in India. Classical Ayurvedic texts do not describe a disease with the same name, so it has to be understood through dosha, dhatu, and srotas concepts. Vyanavata is the subtype of Vata seated in the hridaya (heart) that governs circulation, and it is the most relevant dosha to this condition. This article reviews the classical description of Vyanavata, explores its correlation with the physiology and pathogenesis of essential hypertension, and outlines the resulting management principles. The correlation is a conceptual hypothesis and needs clinical validation.

title: SCIENTIFIC INSIGHTS INTO VAPOR PHASE ESSENTIAL OILS AND THEIR BIOMEDICAL APPLICATIONS
abstractText: The volatile part of essential oils extracted from plants, when dispersed throughout the atmosphere, is known as the vapour phase essential oils, allowing them to interact with microorganisms in the air and the human respiratory tract. The use of vapor phase delivery has gained considerable momentum in recent years because of its superior antimicrobial activity and non-invasive application, in addition to the possibility of using it in the food area, clinical settings and the management of indoor air quality. This review includes detailed information about the chemistry, mechanism of action, antimicrobial and therapeutic applications, drawbacks and future research avenues for vapor phase essential oils. They have been highlighted with regard to the latest scientific data regarding their effectiveness against bacteria, fungi and viruses. Also, the issues of regulation and toxicity and the need for standardization are discussed. The purpose of this article is to give a scientific basis for future research and application.

title: AKALA VALI AND ATI-CHINTA: AN AYURVEDIC PERSPECTIVE ON ETIOPATHOGENESIS AND MANAGEMENT
abstractText: Akala Vali (premature wrinkles) is an important cosmetic concern that may reflect early skin degeneration. Although Ayurveda does not describe Vali as an independent disease with specific aetiology and pathogenesis, its development can be interpreted through Rasa Dhatu Dushti, Pitta aggravation, Pitta Prakriti, and Ati-Chinta. This conceptual study reviewed classical Ayurvedic texts to explore the relationship between Vali, skin physiology, ageing, causative factors, pathogenesis, and management. Ayurvedic approaches including Rasayana, Nasya, Basti, internal medicines, and external Taila application may support skin nourishment and delay premature ageing. Appropriate diet, lifestyle modification, stress management, and preservation of Rasa Dhatu are emphasized for prevention.

title: DYKE DAVIDOFF MASSON SYNDROME IN A FUNCTIONALLY INDEPENDENT ADULT WITH CHILDHOOD ONSET HEMIPARESIS: A CASE REPORT
abstractText: Dyke-Davidoff-Masson syndrome (DDMS) is a rare neurological disorder characterized by cerebral hemiatrophy, contralateral hemiparesis, facial asymmetry, and recurrent seizures. It typically presents during childhood, while diagnosis in adulthood is uncommon, particularly in individuals who remain functionally independent. We report the case of a 37-year-old male with childhood-onset hemiparesis who remained ambulatory and independent in activities of daily living. The diagnosis of DDMS was established incidentally on magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) during evaluation for an unrelated illness. This case highlights the variable clinical spectrum of DDMS and emphasizes that mild cases may remain undiagnosed until adulthood.

title: TALISAPTRA: ONE NAME, THREE BOTANICAL SOURCES- A CRITICAL REVIEW OF IDENTITY CONTROVERSY AND CONTEMPORARY CHEMICAL FINGERPRINTING EVIDENCE
abstractText: Tālisapatra is an important aromatic Himalayan drug used in Ayurvedic practice, particularly in disorders involving the respiratory and gastrointestinal systems. However, its botanical identity has historically been controversial, with Abies webbiana and species of Taxus being associated with the drug name Tālisapatra/Tālisapatrī in Indian medicinal literature. The problem is clinically and pharmacognostically relevant because dried and powdered leaves of Abies webbiana and Taxus baccata can be difficult to distinguish, while their chemical compositions, pharmacological profiles and toxicological characteristics are substantially different. In the present review, three Himalayan or Himalayan-associated taxa—Abies webbiana (Abies spectabilis), Taxus baccata, and Rhododendron anthopogon—are evaluated.

title: ROLE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN PERSONALIZED MEDICINE A COMPREHENSIVE REVIEW
abstractText: The idea behind personalized medicine is simple to explain but difficult to execute: prevention, diagnosis, prognosis and treatment should be based on the biological, clinical, environmental and behavioral specificities of the patient who is in front of the clinician, rather than the average patient of a trial population. In fact, one of the key technologies driving this goal is artificial intelligence (AI), which can manage data that is often too big, too complex, or too multidimensional to be comfortably handled by traditional statistical methods. Nevertheless, AI has not fully matured and is still experiencing its adolescence in the field of personalized medicine in the domains of biomarker discovery, disease subtyping, risk prediction, early diagnosis, treatment-response modelling, pharmacogenomics, digital pathology, longitudinal monitoring, and clinical decision support.t outlines the conceptual foundations, types of data that enable personalization, key clinical applications, ethical and legal issues yet to be resolved, and obstacles between potential research and clinical practice. The perpetual debate is that AI does not take over the doctor's decision-making, but rather helps doctors to access more information than they could retain within their minds all at once.

title: MANAGEMENT OF CHRONIC POST-TRAUMATIC TIBIAL OSTEOMYELITIS WITH INTRAMEDULLARY ABSCESS USING TILVAK KSHARA KARMA AND AYURVEDIC THERAPEUTICS: A CASE REPORT
abstractText: Background: Chronic osteomyelitis is a persistent infection of bone and bone marrow characterized by progressive inflammatory destruction of bone tissue, sequestrum formation, sinus tract development, and recurrent purulent discharge. It commonly occurs following open fractures, orthopedic implant procedures, or inadequately treated acute osteomyelitis. The condition remains a significant therapeutic challenge because of poor local vascularity, the presence of necrotic bone, and a high risk of recurrence. Conventional management generally involves prolonged antibiotic therapy combined with surgical debridement and, in advanced cases, reconstructive procedures. Despite advances in treatment, chronic osteomyelitis continues to be associated with substantial morbidity, prolonged treatment duration, and reduced quality of life.. The present case report describes favorable short-term outcomes in chronic post-traumatic tibial osteomyelitis with intramedullary abscess treated using Tilvak Kshara Karma and Ayurvedic therapeutics. Case Presentation: A 34-year-old male presented with persistent pus discharge from the right leg for three years following intramedullary tibial nailing in 2017. Despite implant removal and two months of conventional antibiotic therapy, symptoms persisted. MRI confirmed chronic osteomyelitis with intramedullary abscess, sequestrum formation, cortical erosion, cloaca formation, and adjacent soft tissue collection. Multi-stage orthopedic debridement with reconstructive surgery was advised but declined by the patient. Intervention: Drainage of the sinus tract was performed using trocar and cannula followed by local Tilvak Kshara Karma. Internal Ayurvedic medications including Manjistha Churna, Chopchini, Rasamanikya, Shuddha Gandhaka, Giloy Satva, Praval Pishti, Panchatikta Ghrita Guggulu, and Khadirarishta were administered. Panchavalkala Kwatha Prakshalana was used for local wound cleansing. Outcome: After three weeks of treatment, complete cessation of pus discharge was observed with closure of the sinus opening. Total leukocyte count decreased from 9800 to 6350 cells/mm³ (↓35.2%), erythrocyte sedimentation rate from 25 to 13 mm/hr (↓48.0%), and C-reactive protein from 5 to 1.83 mg/L (↓63.4%). No adverse events were observed. Conclusion: This case demonstrates favorable short-term clinical and laboratory improvement in chronic post-traumatic tibial osteomyelitis managed with Tilvak Kshara Karma and Ayurvedic internal medications. Larger controlled studies with longer follow-up are required to validate these findings.
