title: MANAGEMENT OF TELOGEN EFFLUVIUM (INTITHAR AL-SHA'R) THROUGH UNANI INTERVENTION: A CASE REPORT
abstractText: Background: Telogen Effluvium is a prevalent cause of diffuse hair loss that significantly impacts emotional well-being and quality of life. Conventional treatments often fail to provide complete resolution and may be associated with adverse effects and poor adherence. In the Unani medical system, diffuse hair loss is termed Intithar al-Sha’r and is attributed to an imbalance in temperament (Su’-i-Mizaj), particularly ghalba-e-safrāwī mizāj. This report presents a successful case of Telogen Effluvium managed using a holistic Unani therapeutic approach. Case Presentation: A 24-year-old female presented with severe hair loss persisting for three months, onset following a febrile illness five months prior. She had no history of thyroid dysfunction, polycystic ovary syndrome, or androgenetic alopecia. Physical examination revealed pallor with stable vital signs and unremarkable systemic findings. Scalp examination demonstrated diffuse thinning with a positive hair pull test at multiple sites, without scarring, scaling, or central part widening. Nails, eyebrows, eyelashes, and body hair were normal. The clinical diagnosis was Telogen Effluvium (Intithar al-Sha’r). Intervention: Following informed consent, treatment comprised oral administration of Itrifal Ustukhuddus 10 g twice daily and nightly scalp massage with 5 mL of Roghan-e-Zaitoon. Supportive hair care advice included rinsing with cold water, avoiding hot water and tight hairstyles, maintaining scalp oiliness, and minimizing heat-based styling. Dietary recommendations emphasized nutrient-rich foods high in protein, iron, and essential fatty acids, such as egg yolk, milk, yogurt, leafy greens, nuts, and fruits. Treatment response was monitored biweekly using the Hair Shedding Visual Analog Scale (HSVS) and Dermatology Life Quality Index (DLQI). Outcome: After 60 days, HSVS decreased from 9 to 3, indicating a substantial reduction in hair shedding. DLQI improved from 17 to 5, reflecting enhanced quality of life and emotional well-being. No adverse effects were reported, and laboratory parameters remained within normal limits, supporting the safety and tolerability of the intervention. Conclusion: This case demonstrates that a holistic Unani regimen, incorporating Itrifal Ustukhuddus, topical Roghan-e-Zaitoon, personalized hair care, and dietary modifications, effectively reduces hair shedding and improves quality of life in Telogen Effluvium associated with ghalba-e-safrāwī mizāj. The favorable clinical response and absence of side effects underscore the potential of Unani medicine in managing diffuse hair loss. Larger, controlled studies are warranted to validate these findings.

title: PHYTOCHEMICAL SCREENING AND IN VITRO EVALUATION OF THE ANTI-UROLITHIASIS ACTIVITY OF ETHANOLIC EXTRACT OF CROSSANDRA INFUNDIBULIFORMIS FLOWERS
abstractText: Urolithiasis is a common urinary tract disorder characterized by the formation and aggregation of crystalline stones, with calcium oxalate being the predominant type of urinary stone. The present study aimed to evaluate the in-vitro anti-urolithiasis activity of the ethanolic flower extract of Crossandra infundibuliformis and to investigate its phytochemical constituents. The flowers of Crossandra infundibuliformis were collected, authenticated, shade-dried and powdered, followed by Soxhlet extraction using ethanol. The percentage yield of the obtained ethanolic flower extract was found to be 28.6%. Preliminary phytochemical screening revealed the presence of tannins, phenols, reducing sugars, cholesterol, terpenoids, carotenoids and resins, while alkaloids, flavonoids, steroids, carbohydrates, proteins, glycosides, saponins and phytosterols were not detected. The in-vitro anti-urolithiatic activity was evaluated by assessing the inhibition of calcium oxalate crystal aggregation at different concentrations of the extract (10, 50, 100, 250 and 500 µg/mL) and compared with Cystone as the standard drug. The ethanolic flower extract exhibited concentration-dependent inhibition of calcium oxalate crystal aggregation, with mean percentage inhibition of 30.554%, 43.267%, 49.781%, 55.591% and 61.740% at 10, 50, 100, 250 and 500 µg/mL, respectively. Cystone showed a mean inhibition of 81.259%. The observed anti-urolithiatic activity may be associated with the phytoconstituents present in the extract, particularly tannins, phenols and terpenoids. Overall, the findings suggest that the ethanolic flower extract of Crossandra infundibuliformis possesses promising concentration-dependent in-vitro anti-urolithiatic activity against calcium oxalate crystal aggregation. Further experimental studies are required to validate its therapeutic potential.

title: PRESCRIBING PATTERNS OF PSYCHOTROPIC DRUGS IN PATIENTS WITH SCHIZOPHRENIA IN A TERTIARY CARE HOSPITAL: A CROSS-SECTIONAL STUDY
abstractText: Background: Prescription pattern studies help assess the rational use of medicines in real-world clinical practice. Objective: To describe psychotropic prescribing patterns and World Health Organisation and International Network for Rational Use of Drugs (WHO-INRUD) prescribing indicators among outpatients with schizophrenia. Methods: This cross-sectional observational study included 154 adults with DSM-5 schizophrenia attending the psychiatry outpatient department of Pt. B. D. Sharma PGIMS, Rohtak, Haryana. Prescription details were recorded and analysed descriptively. Results: The mean age was 45.75 ± 14.42 years; 80 participants (52.0%) were women. Second-generation antipsychotics accounted for 173 of 190 antipsychotic orders (91.05%) and olanzapine was the most frequently prescribed agent (104 orders, 54.74%). Two or more psychotropics were prescribed to 129 patients (83.8%), whereas high-level polypharmacy (five or more psychotropics) was seen in one patient (0.64%). Antidepressants were used in 72 encounters, mainly selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (67, 93.06%). The mean number of drugs per prescription was 2.65 and 97.98% of psychotropic drugs were prescribed by generic name. Injectable drug use was 1.30%, no fixed-dose combination was prescribed and 90.75% of psychotropic drugs were listed in the Government of Haryana Essential Drug List.

title: FORMULATION AND EVALUATION OF SUSTAINED RELEASE MATRIX TABLET OF ONDANSETRON USING NATURAL POLYMERS: REVIEW
abstractText: Ondansetron is a widely used antiemetic with a short half-life, requiring frequent dosing. Sustained release (SR) matrix tablets prepared using natural polymers offer an effective approach to prolong drug release, improve patient compliance, and maintain therapeutic drug levels. Natural polymers such as xanthan gum, guar gum, sodium alginate, gum acacia, and HPMC-based combinations are biodegradable, biocompatible, cost-effective, and environmentally friendly. Recent advances in natural polymer-based SR matrix tablets have focused on optimizing drug release, enhancing tablet stability, and improving bioavailability. This review highlights the formulation strategies, evaluation methods, advantages, and prospects of natural polymer-based sustained release matrix tablets of ondansetron, emphasizing their potential as safe and effective oral drug delivery systems.

title: EVALUATION OF AGNIKARMA AND MARMA CHIKITSA AS AYURVEDIC INTERVENTIONS IN CERVICAL SPONDYLOSIS: A COMPARATIVE STUDY
abstractText: In today’s fast-paced lifestyle, prolonged sitting, reduced physical activity, and poor postural habits have become increasingly common across different age groups. These lifestyle changes have contributed to a growing incidence of musculoskeletal problems, including cervical spondylosis. From an Ayurvedic perspective, the clinical features of cervical spondylosis can be correlated with Manyastambha, which is primarily characterised by pain, stiffness, and restricted movement in the neck region.[1] Classical Ayurvedic texts offer several therapeutic approaches for managing such conditions, among which Agnikarma and Marma Chikitsa are particularly noteworthy. Both therapies have shown promising results in relieving symptoms; however, their comparative effectiveness may help determine which approach provides faster and more lasting relief.

title: EFFECTIVENESS OF AYURVEDIC INTERVENTION IN ANIDRA (INSOMNIA): A CLINICAL CASE STUDY
abstractText: Introduction: Anidra, referred to as Insomnia in contemporary medicine, is recognized in Ayurveda as a consequence of doshas imbalances, primarily involving Vata, with secondary disturbances In Pitta and Kapha. Habitual sleeplessness or simply inability to sleep for a minimum period, which is necessary for a sound mental and physical health, is called insomnia (Anidra). Acute insomnia is brief and typically occurs due to temporary life circumstances. Aim and Objective: To evaluate the efficacy of Ayurvedic management in Anidra (Insomnia) Material and Method: This is single case study of 28 years old female suffering from sleeplessness for 1 years, sleeping hours of two, this shattered her physical as well as mental condition. She had associated complaints of excessive thoughts, indigestion and headache. Patient sleep was markedly disturbed leading to stress and anxiety hence she visited to our hospital. Treatment given was Shirodhara with Ksheerbala Tail for 45 min for 21 days along with Shamana Chikitsa Saraswatarishta, Chitrakadi Vati and Smritisagar Ras. Results: Patient showed marked improvement in sleep quality and duration. Associated symptoms such as excessive thoughts, stress, anxiety, headache, and indigestion were significantly reduced. Discussion: The significant improvement observed in this patient suggests that a combined Ayurvedic approach involving Shamana chikitsa and Panchkarma can effectively manage chronic insomnia and improve overall well-being. Conclusion: This case study demonstrates the potential effectiveness of Ayurvedic management in the treatment of Anidra (insomnia). The integrated approach comprising Ayurvedic medications and Shirodhara with Ksheerbala Taila and selected Ayurvedic medications resulted in substantial improvement in sleep quality, reduction of associated symptoms, and enhancement of the patient's quality of life.

title: ASSESSMENT OF ADR DETECTION, REPORTING AWARENESS, AND RISK PERCEPTION AMONG PHARMACY STUDENTS: A CROSS-SECTIONAL INSTITUTIONAL STUDY
abstractText: Adverse drug reactions (ADRs) are an important concern in healthcare and can contribute to patient morbidity, mortality, increased healthcare costs, and prolonged hospital stay. Pharmacovigilance plays an important role in identifying, monitoring, assessing, and preventing adverse effects associated with medicines. ADR reporting is an important part of pharmacovigilance because it helps in detecting safety problems that may not be identified during clinical trials. Pharmacy students are future healthcare professionals and should have adequate knowledge about ADR detection, reporting procedures, and pharmacovigilance systems. The present study was conducted to assess ADR detection knowledge, reporting awareness, risk perception, and reporting practices among pharmacy students. A descriptive cross sectional institutional study was conducted among 400 pharmacy students over a period of three months. A structured, self-administered questionnaire was used for data collection. The questionnaire consisted of four sections covering demographic characteristics, ADR detection knowledge, ADR reporting awareness, and risk perception and reporting practices. The findings showed that 77.3% of respondents correctly identified the definition of an ADR, while 82.5% were aware of the WHO definition of ADR. About 71.5% were aware of ADR classification types and 77.8% reported that they could identify clinical signs of common ADRs. However, only 63.7% were familiar with causality assessment scales. Regarding reporting awareness, 81.3% recognized that ADR reporting is important for patient safety, 69.5% knew where ADRs could be reported in India, and 72.3% were familiar with the Pharmacovigilance Programme of India (PvPI). However, misconceptions were observed regarding who can report ADRs and the appropriate reporting timeframe. Regarding practice, 60.9% of students had observed an ADR during clinical practice, whereas 53% had reported an ADR. ADR Monitoring Centres were the most commonly used reporting channel. A large majority of respondents, 81%, supported mandatory pharmacovigilance and ADR reporting training in the pharmacy curriculum. The study indicates that pharmacy students have generally good basic knowledge and awareness regarding ADRs, but gaps remain in practical reporting knowledge and reporting behaviour. Regular pharmacovigilance education, practical ADR reporting exercises, clinical exposure, and awareness programmes may help improve ADR reporting practices among pharmacy students.

title: FORMULATION AND EVALUATION OF EMULGEL FOR TOPICAL DRUG DELIVERY
abstractText: Topical drug delivery systems offer a convenient and effective mode of delivery of drugs to the skin surface, which increases local concentration of the drug while minimizing systemic adverse effects. Emulgels are considered as one of the potential dosage forms, which offer solution for topical drug delivery. They are mixtures of an emulsion and gel matrix and allow delivery of both hydrophilic and hydrophobic drugs. This article highlights a discussion on topical drug delivery and emulgels, including their types, formulating ingredients, methods of preparation, and evaluation parameters. A brief description on the anatomy of the skin and its barrier properties towards topical drug delivery is also presented. Emulgels are described with a focus on the aqueous and oily phases, emulsifying agents, permeation enhancers, and gelling agents. The physiological, physicochemical, and formulation factors that may influence topical drug absorption are also outlined. Moreover, the article discusses the various types of emulgels: macroemulgels, microemulgels, and nanoemulgels, and their characteristics such as particle size and stability. Other evaluation parameters include physical appearance, pH, viscosity, stability, irritation, and zeta potential, particle size distribution, polydispersity index, swelling index, drug content, spreadability, and extrudability. Emulgels can be used as a versatile topically applicable dosage form due to their enhanced spreading ability, patient acceptability, high drug loading, stability, and controlled release property. Future work focused on the evaluation and formulation of emulgels would be of paramount importance in topical and transdermal drug delivery.

title: OPTIMIZATION, DEVELOPMENT AND VALIDATION OF A STABILITY INDICATING RP-HPLC METHOD FOR SIMULTANEOUS QUANTIFICATION OF AMLODIPINE, OLMESARTAN AND CHLORTHALIDONE IN PHARMACEUTICAL FORMULATIONS
abstractText: The present study aimed to develop and validate a simple, rapid, accurate, precise, and stability-indicating RP-HPLC method for the simultaneous estimation of Amlodipine, Olmesartan, and Chlorthalidone in combined tablet dosage forms. The optimized method used a C18 column (250 × 4.6 mm, 5 µm) with Acetonitrile and Potassium Dihydrogen Phosphate buffer (60:40, v/v) adjusted to pH 3.0 as the mobile phase. The flow rate was 1.0 mL/min, detection wavelength was 238 nm, injection volume was 20 µL, and the total run time was 10 min. The drugs showed well-separated peaks at retention times of 2.34, 4.58, and 6.92 min for Amlodipine, Olmesartan, and Chlorthalidone, respectively. The method was validated according to ICH Q2(R2) guidelines. Good linearity was obtained with R² values of 0.9997, 0.9998, and 0.9996, respectively. Recovery was between 99.42% and 100.36%, and precision values were within the acceptable limit of 2% RSD. The LOD values were 0.27, 0.40, and 0.30 µg/mL, while LOQ values were 0.82, 1.21, and 0.91 µg/mL for the three drugs, respectively. Assay results for the marketed tablet were 99.60%, 100.30%, and 99.68% for Amlodipine, Olmesartan, and Chlorthalidone, respectively. Forced degradation studies showed 2.82–9.64% degradation under different stress conditions, with no interference from degradation products. The results confirmed that the method is suitable for routine analysis and stability studies of these drugs in combined pharmaceutical formulations.

title: MANAGEMENT OF TELOGEN EFFLUVIUM (INTITHAR AL-SHA'R) THROUGH UNANI INTERVENTION: A CASE REPORT
abstractText: Background: Telogen Effluvium is a prevalent cause of diffuse hair loss that significantly impacts emotional well-being and quality of life. Conventional treatments often fail to provide complete resolution and may be associated with adverse effects and poor adherence. In the Unani medical system, diffuse hair loss is termed Intithar al-Sha’r and is attributed to an imbalance in temperament (Su’-i-Mizaj), particularly ghalba-e-safrāwī mizāj. This report presents a successful case of Telogen Effluvium managed using a holistic Unani therapeutic approach. Case Presentation: A 24-year-old female presented with severe hair loss persisting for three months, onset following a febrile illness five months prior. She had no history of thyroid dysfunction, polycystic ovary syndrome, or androgenetic alopecia. Physical examination revealed pallor with stable vital signs and unremarkable systemic findings. Scalp examination demonstrated diffuse thinning with a positive hair pull test at multiple sites, without scarring, scaling, or central part widening. Nails, eyebrows, eyelashes, and body hair were normal. The clinical diagnosis was Telogen Effluvium (Intithar al-Sha’r). Intervention: Following informed consent, treatment comprised oral administration of Itrifal Ustukhuddus 10 g twice daily and nightly scalp massage with 5 mL of Roghan-e-Zaitoon. Supportive hair care advice included rinsing with cold water, avoiding hot water and tight hairstyles, maintaining scalp oiliness, and minimizing heat-based styling. Dietary recommendations emphasized nutrient-rich foods high in protein, iron, and essential fatty acids, such as egg yolk, milk, yogurt, leafy greens, nuts, and fruits. Treatment response was monitored biweekly using the Hair Shedding Visual Analog Scale (HSVS) and Dermatology Life Quality Index (DLQI). Outcome: After 60 days, HSVS decreased from 9 to 3, indicating a substantial reduction in hair shedding. DLQI improved from 17 to 5, reflecting enhanced quality of life and emotional well-being. No adverse effects were reported, and laboratory parameters remained within normal limits, supporting the safety and tolerability of the intervention. Conclusion: This case demonstrates that a holistic Unani regimen, incorporating Itrifal Ustukhuddus, topical Roghan-e-Zaitoon, personalized hair care, and dietary modifications, effectively reduces hair shedding and improves quality of life in Telogen Effluvium associated with ghalba-e-safrāwī mizāj. The favorable clinical response and absence of side effects underscore the potential of Unani medicine in managing diffuse hair loss. Larger, controlled studies are warranted to validate these findings.

title: FORMULATION AND EVALUATION OF HERBAL ANTIMICROBIAL GEL CONTAINING APRAJITA CLITORIA TERNATEA L.
abstractText: Skin infections caused by pathogenic microorganisms remain a major healthcare concern, and the increasing prevalence of antimicrobial resistance has highlighted the need for safer and more effective topical therapies. Herbal medicines have gained considerable attention because of their broad therapeutic potential, low toxicity, and improved patient acceptability. The present study aimed to formulate and evaluate a herbal antimicrobial gel containing the ethanolic extract of Clitoria ternatea L. (Aprajita). Fresh flowers of Clitoria ternatea were collected, authenticated, shade-dried, powdered, and extracted using ethanol. The extract was incorporated into a Carbopol-based gel using suitable excipients to obtain a stable topical formulation. The prepared gel was evaluated for its physicochemical properties, including appearance, homogeneity, pH, viscosity, spreadability, extrudability, washability, and stability. Antimicrobial activity was assessed against selected pathogenic microorganisms using a standard microbiological method. The formulated gel exhibited acceptable physical characteristics, good consistency, suitable pH for topical application, satisfactory spreadability, and excellent stability throughout the study period. The formulation demonstrated promising antimicrobial activity, indicating the presence of bioactive phytoconstituents in the ethanolic extract of Clitoria ternatea. These findings suggest that the developed herbal gel has potential as a safe and effective topical antimicrobial formulation for the management of superficial skin infections. Further preclinical and clinical investigations are recommended to establish its therapeutic efficacy and long-term safety.

title: ROLE OF SHIRODHARA IN MODULATING NEURODEVELOPMENTAL DISORDERS IN CHILDREN
abstractText: Neurodevelopmental disorders are disabilities associated primarily with the functioning of the neurological system and brain. These disorders typically manifest in early childhood, frequently persist into adulthood, and impose substantial limitations on personal, social, academic, and occupational functioning. Considering the chronic course and profound functional limitations associated with neurodevelopmental disorders, there is a growing emphasis on integrative and complementary therapeutic approaches. Shirodhara, a classical Ayurvedic therapy is traditionally recognized for its tranquilizing and stabilizing influence on the central nervous system. It is postulated to exert regulatory effects on neuroendocrine mechanisms, mitigate stress responses, improve sleep architecture, and enhance cognitive and behavioral modulation.

title: ROLE OF KHA VAIGUṆYA IN DISEASE SUSCEPTIBILITY AND LOCALIZATION: A CRITICAL ANALYTICAL REVIEW IN AYURVEDA
abstractText: Kha Vaiguṇya is a key concept in Ayurvedic pathogenesis explaining the susceptibility and preferential localization of disease in a tissue, organ, or Srotas. Disease manifestation is not attributed solely to systemic Doṣa aggravation; localization occurs when aggravated Doṣas encounter a susceptible site. Classical descriptions in Caraka Cikitsā Sthāna and Suśruta Sūtra Sthāna associate Kha Vaiguṇya with the site where circulating pathological factors localize and produce disease. This review analyses Kha Vaiguṇya in relation to Sthānasamśraya, Doṣa-Dūṣya Sammūrchanā, Srotoduṣṭi, disease susceptibility, and localization, drawing on classical literature and selected contemporary sources for conceptual interpretation. Kha Vaiguṇya represents a condition of local vulnerability facilitating the establishment of pathology at a particular site. Its relationship with Sthānasamśraya explains the transition from generalized Doṣa disturbance to localized manifestation, and accounts for individual variation, since similar causative exposure may produce different manifestations depending on site susceptibility. Modern concepts such as tissue susceptibility, structural alteration, organ vulnerability, and altered local microenvironment offer conceptual parallels, though not direct biomedical equivalents. A clearer understanding of Kha Vaiguṇya may aid Ayurvedic disease prevention, localization, prognosis, and individualized management.

title: UNDERSTANDING VYANAVATA IN ESSENTIAL HYPERTENSION: A CONCEPTUAL REVIEW
abstractText: Essential hypertension is a leading modifiable risk factor for cardiovascular disease and is rising steadily in India. Classical Ayurvedic texts do not describe a disease with the same name, so it has to be understood through dosha, dhatu, and srotas concepts. Vyanavata is the subtype of Vata seated in the hridaya (heart) that governs circulation, and it is the most relevant dosha to this condition. This article reviews the classical description of Vyanavata, explores its correlation with the physiology and pathogenesis of essential hypertension, and outlines the resulting management principles. The correlation is a conceptual hypothesis and needs clinical validation.

title: WILLINGNESS TO ACCEPT MALARIA VACCINE AMONG CAREGIVERS OF UNDER-5 CHILDREN: A CROSS-SECTIONAL STUDY AT PCMH AND CONNAUGHT HOSPITAL, FREETOWN
abstractText: Background: Sierra Leone has one of the highest malaria burdens in the world and children under 5 years of age are the most vulnerable. The malaria vaccine RTS,S/AS01 is a promising vaccine, but its use is still very low (around 50% of eligible children nationally). Knowledge of the willingness of caregivers and related factors is crucial for enhancing vaccine uptake. Objective: To evaluate the uptake of malaria vaccination among caregivers of under fives children attending two major government hospitals in Freetown and to determine factors influencing uptake of malaria vaccine. Method: A cross sectional study was carried out from January to July 2025 at Princess Christian Maternity Hospital (PCMH) and Connaught Hospital. The immunization registers were used to select 201 caregiver-child records through systematic random sampling. Structured questionnaires were employed to gather data on the socio-demographic characteristics, awareness, trust, and perceived effectiveness. Chi-square tests and logistic regression (SPSS v25) were used to identify predictors of vaccine acceptance. Results: Vaccine uptake was only 21.9% (44/201). The most common primary barriers were concerns about side effects (58.0%) and lack of awareness (29.3%). Significant predictors of acceptance were: awareness (χ²=17.82, p<0.001; OR=5.63, 95%CI: 2.36-13.45), perceived effectiveness (OR=3.12, 95%CI: 1.74-5.59, p<0.001), trust in healthcare workers (OR=2.89, 95%CI: 1.65-5.08, p<0.001), tertiary education (OR=2.34, 95%CI: 1.31-4.17, p=0.005), and urban residence (OR=2.12, 95%CI: 1.15-3.91, p=0.015). Conclusion: The acceptance of malaria vaccines among caregivers in Freetown is very low. The main obstacles are fear of side effects and lack of awareness. There is an urgent need for targeted health education with trusted health care providers to improve vaccine uptake and reduce child mortality due to malaria in Sierra Leone. This study explores the attitudes of caregivers towards the introduction of a malaria vaccine in under-fives in Sierra Leone, with a particular focus on vaccine acceptance.

title: INTEGRATIVE MANAGEMENT OF AVASCULAR NECROSIS OF FEMORAL HEAD THROUGH AYURVEDA AND PANCHAKARMA: A CRITICAL REVIEW OF CURRENT EVIDENCE
abstractText: Avascular necrosis (AVN), more precisely termed osteonecrosis of the femoral head (ONFH), is a progressive disorder caused by loss of blood supply to the subchondral bone, leading to osteocyte death, structural weakening, collapse of the femoral head and secondary osteoarthritis. It commonly affects younger adults and may result from corticosteroid exposure, excessive alcohol intake, trauma, sickle cell disease and several other systemic conditions. Early diagnosis is important because joint-preserving treatment becomes progressively less effective once subchondral fracture and femoral head collapse have occurred. Contemporary evidence supports magnetic resonance imaging as the most accurate imaging modality for early disease, while treatment is selected according to stage, lesion size, location, symptoms and patient factors.[1,2] Ayurveda does not describe AVN as a single classical disease entity. Published Ayurvedic reports have interpreted its clinical presentation through concepts such as Asthi-Majjagata Vata, Asthivaha Srotodushti, Dhatu Kshaya and Vata Prakopa.[3] This correlation remains interpretative and should not be considered an exact classical equivalent of ischemic osteonecrosis. Panchakarma-based management reported in case literature commonly includes Rukshana, Snehana, Swedana, Basti, Ksheera Basti, Shashtika Shali Pinda Sweda and internal medicines intended to address pain, stiffness and tissue depletion.[3,4] The available Ayurvedic evidence is encouraging mainly with respect to symptomatic outcomes such as pain, gait, range of motion and quality of life. However, most publications consist of individual case reports or small uncontrolled studies, and convincing evidence that Ayurveda can reverse necrotic bone, restore vascular supply or prevent structural collapse is currently lacking. Modern joint-preserving treatments such as core decompression, with or without biological augmentation, remain important particularly in pre-collapse disease, while arthroplasty is often required after advanced collapse.[5] This review critically examines the modern pathophysiology and staging of ONFH, its cautious Ayurvedic interpretation, the rationale for Panchakarma interventions, available clinical evidence and opportunities for integrative research. A safe integrative approach should aim to improve pain, function and quality of life while maintaining MRI-based staging and timely orthopedic referral. Future trials require standardized Ayurvedic protocols, validated functional outcomes, serial imaging and long-term follow-up before disease-modifying claims can be justified.

title: ROLE OF MEDOHARA AND PRAMEHAGHNA DRAVYAS IN THE MANAGEMENT OF METABOLIC DISORDERS: A COMPREHENSIVE AYURVEDIC REVIEW
abstractText: Metabolic disorders have emerged as major health concerns in the present era. Conditions such as obesity, type 2 diabetes mellitus, dyslipidemia, hypertension, and metabolic syndrome are commonly associated with inappropriate dietary habits, physical inactivity, stress, and sedentary behaviour. Their coexistence may contribute to an increased risk of cardiovascular disease and other chronic complications. Ayurveda explains disorders arising from excessive nourishment through concepts such as Santarpana, Medo Doṣa, Sthaulya, Prameha, Madhumeha, and impairment of Agni. Excessive consumption of heavy, oily, and sweet foods, overeating, and inadequate physical activity are described as important factors in the development of Santarpanajanya Vikāra. The concepts of Sthaulya and Prameha also show considerable relevance to obesity and metabolic disturbances in the contemporary context.[1,2]

title: DEVELOPMENT OF CONTROLLED RELEASE TRANSDERMAL FILMS CONTAINING ANTHRALIN
abstractText: Anthralin is an effective antipsoriatic agent widely used in the treatment of chronic skin disorders such as psoriasis; however, its therapeutic application is limited due to poor patient compliance, skin irritation, and the need for frequent administration. The present study was undertaken to develop and evaluate controlled release transdermal films containing Anthralin in order to enhance drug release control, improve therapeutic efficacy, and prolong drug delivery through the skin. Pre-formulation studies of Anthralin were carried out to determine its physicochemical properties, including organoleptic characteristics, solubility, melting point, λ max determination, calibration curve analysis, and FTIR spectroscopy. Anthralin exhibited maximum absorbance and showed compatibility with the selected excipients used in the transdermal patch formulation. The transdermal films were prepared by the solvent casting method using combinations of Eudragit L, polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP), hydroxypropyl methylcellulose (HPMC), polyethylene glycol 400, Tween 20, methanol, and glycerin. Six formulations (TPF1–TPF6) were prepared by varying the polymer composition. The prepared transdermal films were evaluated for folding endurance, tensile strength, percentage elongation, thickness uniformity, drug content, and in vitro drug release studies. Among all formulations, TPF5 exhibited the most desirable physicochemical characteristics; including excellent flexibility, tensile strength (25 kg/cm²), percentage elongation (42%), and maximum drug content (95.78%). The optimized formulation also demonstrated a sustained and controlled drug release profile with 95.06% cumulative drug release over 11 hours. Drug release kinetics of the optimized formulation was analyzed using zero-order, first-order, Higuchi, and Korsmeyer–Peppas kinetic models. The release profile showed the highest correlation with the zero-order kinetic model (R² = 0.976), indicating concentration-independent and controlled drug release. The Higuchi model also demonstrated good linearity, suggesting diffusion-controlled release behavior from the polymeric matrix. The overall findings of the study indicate that the developed Anthralin transdermal films possess satisfactory physicochemical properties, controlled drug release characteristics, and excellent formulation stability. Therefore, the optimized transdermal patch formulation can be considered a promising alternative drug delivery system for the effective management of psoriasis and related dermatological conditions.

title: A PHARMACEUTICO-ANALYTICAL STUDY OF PRIYANGVADI MOUTHWASH WITH REFERENCE TO SHEETADA (GINGIVITIS)
abstractText: Oral diseases such as gingivitis and plaque-induced inflammation are among the most common conditions affecting oral health. Although several chemical mouthwashes are available, their prolonged use may be associated with undesirable effects, creating a need for safe and effective herbal alternatives. The present study aimed to formulate and evaluate an herbal mouthwash using Priyangu (Callicarpa macrophylla), Musta (Cyperus rotundus), and Triphala (Terminalia chebula, Terminalia bellirica, and Emblica officinalis). These Ayurvedic drugs are traditionally known for their anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, antioxidant, wound-healing, and astringent properties, making them suitable for maintaining oral hygiene and managing gingival disorders. The mouthwash was prepared using standard pharmaceutical procedures and evaluated for its organoleptic characteristics and physicochemical parameters. The formulation exhibited acceptable appearance, odor and taste. The combined action of Priyangu, Musta, and Triphala may help reduce plaque accumulation, gingival inflammation, microbial growth, and oral discomfort while promoting overall oral health. The study suggests that Priyangvadi Mouthwash is a promising, cost-effective, and patient-friendly herbal formulation for oral care and may serve as a potential adjunct in the management of gingivitis and maintenance of oral hygiene.

title: A CASE STUDY ON THE AYURVEDIC MANAGEMENT OF BILATERAL RENAL CALCULI (VRIKKASHMARI)
abstractText: Ashmari is one of the most common conditions described in Ayurveda as an ailment of the Mutravaha Srotas, or urinary system.[1] Because of its extreme agony, recurrence, and difficulties, Sushruta classifies "Ashmari," which literally translates to "stone-like structure," as one of the "Ashtamahagada."[2] Ashmari is associated in contemporary medicine with urolithiasis, also known as nephrolithiasis, which is the development of calculi in the urinary tract. The increasing prevalence of the disease can be attributed to sedentary lifestyles, inadequate dietary practices, dehydration, and metabolic disorders. Current medical research indicates that between 70 and 80 percent of urinary calculi start in the kidneys, mostly in the renal pelvis and renal calyces, particularly the lower calyx. The ureters account for 15–25% of stones, whereas the bladder accounts for 2–10%.[3] Calyceal stones, especially those in the lower calyx, can last for extended periods of time, cause symptoms, and may eventually result in stone development, infection, or urinary blockage, even if smaller calculi may have the ability to pass spontaneously. As a result, "watchful waiting" is frequently insufficient on its own, necessitating active therapeutic involvement.[4] In the current investigation, Ayurvedic medicine was used to treat a 23-year-old female patient who had bilateral renal calyceal calculi. Calculi measuring 5 mm in the right kidney and 4 mm in the left kidney were discovered by ultrasonography. Pashanbhed Churna was used to treat the patient in addition to the proper dietary and lifestyle changes (Pathya-Apathya). Following treatment, ultrasonography showed a considerable improvement in clinical symptoms along with a marked reduction in stone size and partial to total disintegration. This example suggests that treating renal calyceal calculi with Ayurvedic medicine may be a secure and successful treatment choice.

title: DEVELOPMENT AND VALIDATION OF A STABILITY INDICATING RP-HPLC METHOD FOR SIMULTANEOUS ESTIMATION OF PREGABALIN AND ETORICOXIB IN PHARMACEUTICAL DOSAGE FORM
abstractText: The present study was carried out to develop and validate a stability-indicating Reverse Phase High-Performance Liquid Chromatography (RP-HPLC) method for simultaneous estimation of Pregabalin and Etoricoxib in pharmaceutical dosage forms. The method was developed by optimizing the detection wavelength, chromatographic column, mobile phase, flow rate, column temperature and other chromatographic conditions. An Inertsil ODS-3 C18 column (250 × 4.6 mm, 5 µm) was used for separation. The optimized mobile phase consisted of potassium dihydrogen phosphate buffer adjusted to pH 3.0 ± 0.05 with orthophosphoric acid and acetonitrile (60:40, v/v), with a flow rate of 1.0 mL/min and detection at 234 nm. The method was validated according to ICH guidelines for specificity, linearity, accuracy, precision, sensitivity, robustness and solution stability. The method showed good linearity for Pregabalin and Etoricoxib over the selected concentration ranges, with correlation coefficients of 0.9998 and 0.9999, respectively. Mean recoveries were within the acceptable range, and precision studies showed low variability. Forced degradation studies were performed under acidic, alkaline, oxidative, thermal, photolytic and neutral conditions. The degradation products were adequately separated from the main drug peaks, confirming the stability-indicating nature of the method. The method was also successfully applied to a marketed tablet formulation, giving assay values of 99.49% for Pregabalin and 99.52% for Etoricoxib. The developed method is simple, accurate, precise and suitable for routine quality control analysis of Pregabalin and Etoricoxib combination formulations.

title: VISHADA: AN AYURVEDIC PERSPECTIVE ON PSYCHOLOGICAL INHIBITION
abstractText: Vishada is an Ayurvedic concept describing a state of mental disturbance in which emotional strength, confidence, initiative, and engagement with daily life becomes diminished. It extends beyond temporary sadness and involves changes in mental, behavioural and physical functioning. The present discussion explores the classical understanding of Vishada with emphasis on its etiopathogenesis and therapeutic perspective. Psychological experiences such as Ishta Viyoga and prolonged stress may disturb the equilibrium of Satwa and Tamas, with subsequent involvement of Manas, Vatadi doshas and Manovaha Srotas. Its manifestations, including Kaya-Vak-Manas Sada, Apravritti, Karyeshu Asiddhi Bhaya and impairment of Dhi, Dhriti, and Smriti demonstrate the wide-ranging influence of Vishada on activity, motivation, cognition, communication and social interaction. The Ayurvedic approach further emphasizes restoration of mental well-being through different lines of treatment. Understanding Vishada through this holistic framework highlights the close relationship between emotional experience and overall functioning and provides a foundation for its deeper exploration in contemporary mental-health research.

authors.name: Dr. Janaki Y. S.2 Dr. Mahima Goswami*1

title: REGULATORY REQUIREMENTS FOR NASAL PRODUCTS AS PER CDSCO IN INDIA COMPARISON WITH GERMANY
abstractText: Drugs administered intranasally represent a viable alternative to parenteral delivery, serving as an effective option for medicines with low oral bioavailability due to gastrointestinal tract degradation or extensive first-pass metabolism. Enzymatic deactivation is a significant issue for polypeptide medicines; thus, the nasal route—offering low enzymatic activity and vascularized tissues with strong blood flow—serves as a non-invasive alternative to injections. The nasal membrane absorbs small drug molecules rapidly, while absorption of larger molecules can be augmented via mucociliary clearance modulation or permeation enhancers. Beyond systemic delivery, the nasal route presents opportunities for targeted central nervous system (CNS) transport bypassing the blood-brain barrier. This review evaluates the anatomical and physiological principles of the nasal cavity, categorizes drug delivery systems, and compares the regulatory requirements for import, manufacturing, sale, and export between India (Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation [CDSCO]) and Germany (Federal Institute for Drugs and Medical Devices [BfArM] / European Medicines Agency [EMA]).

authors.name: Dr. P. Ashok Kumar*, Athiya Rafath, Damini S., Maheshwari B. K., Pavithra M. G., Radhika U.

title: ASSOCIATION BETWEEN DMD GENE ALTERATIONS AND OVERALL SURVIVAL IN BREAST INVASIVE CARCINOMA
abstractText: Breast invasive carcinoma is a heterogeneous malignancy in which several well-established genes, such as BRCA1, BRCA2, and TP53, have undergone extensive study. More recently, the DMD gene, which codes for the protein dystrophin, has gained attention in cancer research because of its proposed tumour-suppressive functions and its association with tumour progression and patient prognosis (Wang et al., 2014; Luce et al., 2017). This study investigated the association between DMD alterations, based on the cBioPortal query function using the prompt "DMD", and overall survival in patients with breast invasive carcinoma. title: MANAGEMENT OF CHRONIC POST-TRAUMATIC TIBIAL OSTEOMYELITIS WITH INTRAMEDULLARY ABSCESS USING TILVAK KSHARA KARMA AND AYURVEDIC THERAPEUTICS: A CASE REPORT
abstractText: Background: Chronic osteomyelitis is a persistent infection of bone and bone marrow characterized by progressive inflammatory destruction of bone tissue, sequestrum formation, sinus tract development, and recurrent purulent discharge. It commonly occurs following open fractures, orthopedic implant procedures, or inadequately treated acute osteomyelitis. The condition remains a significant therapeutic challenge because of poor local vascularity, the presence of necrotic bone, and a high risk of recurrence. Conventional management generally involves prolonged antibiotic therapy combined with surgical debridement and, in advanced cases, reconstructive procedures. Despite advances in treatment, chronic osteomyelitis continues to be associated with substantial morbidity, prolonged treatment duration, and reduced quality of life.. The present case report describes favorable short-term outcomes in chronic post-traumatic tibial osteomyelitis with intramedullary abscess treated using Tilvak Kshara Karma and Ayurvedic therapeutics. Case Presentation: A 34-year-old male presented with persistent pus discharge from the right leg for three years following intramedullary tibial nailing in 2017. Despite implant removal and two months of conventional antibiotic therapy, symptoms persisted. MRI confirmed chronic osteomyelitis with intramedullary abscess, sequestrum formation, cortical erosion, cloaca formation, and adjacent soft tissue collection. Multi-stage orthopedic debridement with reconstructive surgery was advised but declined by the patient. Intervention: Drainage of the sinus tract was performed using trocar and cannula followed by local Tilvak Kshara Karma. Internal Ayurvedic medications including Manjistha Churna, Chopchini, Rasamanikya, Shuddha Gandhaka, Giloy Satva, Praval Pishti, Panchatikta Ghrita Guggulu, and Khadirarishta were administered. Panchavalkala Kwatha Prakshalana was used for local wound cleansing. Outcome: After three weeks of treatment, complete cessation of pus discharge was observed with closure of the sinus opening. Total leukocyte count decreased from 9800 to 6350 cells/mm³ (↓35.2%), erythrocyte sedimentation rate from 25 to 13 mm/hr (↓48.0%), and C-reactive protein from 5 to 1.83 mg/L (↓63.4%). No adverse events were observed. Conclusion: This case demonstrates favorable short-term clinical and laboratory improvement in chronic post-traumatic tibial osteomyelitis managed with Tilvak Kshara Karma and Ayurvedic internal medications. Larger controlled studies with longer follow-up are required to validate these findings.

title: RE-CONCEPTUALIZING BIOMEDICAL INQUIRY: HARMONIZING CLASSICAL AYURVEDIC EPISTEMOLOGY, DIALECTICS, AND HERMENEUTICS IN MODERN RESEARCH
abstractText: Contemporary biomedical investigations predominantly rely on reductionist frameworks, frequently encountering limitations when navigating the multifactorial, highly individualized clinical dynamics observed in medical practice. This paper investigates the systematic integration of foundational Ayurvedic epistemological principles with current scientific research architectures. By mapping Pratyaksha (empirical observation), Anumana (logical inference), and Yukti (experimental and rational synthesis) onto modern statistical analytics, investigators can establish a sound methodological grounding for evidence-based traditional medicine. Additionally, the academic and clinical application of Acharya Charaka’s forty-four dialectical categories (Vada) provides an advanced framework for negotiating complex modern bioethical challenges. The tripartite Trisutra construct—encompassing Hetu (etiological factors), Linga (clinical manifestations), and Aushadha (therapeutic modalities)—serves as a robust structural blueprint for designing systematic reviews and clinical trials. Concurrently, Tantra-yukti (textual hermeneutical tools) functions as a qualitative protocol to ensure accurate interpretation of classical Sanskrit source material. Together, these traditional paradigms merge historical empirical insights with modern scientific methodology to generate a comprehensive model for contemporary clinical investigation.

title: AYURVEDIC PROTOCOL IN THE MANAGEMENT OF DIABETIC DYSLIPIDEMIA: ADDRESSING GUT DYSBIOSIS AND METABOLIC IMBALANCE – A CASE REPORT
abstractText: Introduction: Diabetic dyslipidemia, characterized by elevated triglycerides, cholesterol, LDL, and low HDL, is a frequent metabolic abnormality in Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus. In India, its prevalence ranges between 60–75% among diabetics, contributing significantly to cardiovascular morbidity. Gut microbiota plays a key role in lipid metabolism through bile acid modulation, short-chain fatty acid production, and inflammatory regulation. Dysbiosis promotes hepatic lipogenesis, reduces HDL synthesis, and aggravates dyslipidemia in diabetes. Diabetic Dyslipidemia can be seen under the lens of Medorogam, arising from Agnimandya, Ama Utpatti, and Kapha Medo Dushti. Aim: To evaluate the efficacy of Ayurvedic Medoroga Chikitsa protocol in the management of diabetic dyslipidemia. Objective: To assess changes in symptoms, BMI, blood glucose, and lipid profile before and after treatment. Methods: In February 2025, a 42-year-old male presented with fatigue, heaviness of body, excessive thirst, sweating, increased micturition, weight gain, exertional dyspnoea, and loss of appetite for one year. He visited the OPD of SJSACH, Chennai, and was diagnosed with Diabetic Dyslipidemia/Medorogam based on blood glucose and lipid profile. Management began with Deepana and Pachana, followed by Udwarthanam, Sadhyo Virechanam, Podikizhi, and Lekhana Kashaya Vasti. Results: Post treatment showed marked reduction in symptoms, blood glucose, and lipid profile, along with mild weight loss. Conclusion: Agni Deepana and Ama Pachana restore Agni and remove Ama, correcting Agnimandya. Shodhana eliminates Kapha, Meda, and Ama; Pathyahara and Vyayama prevent Meda Vriddhi and enhance Dhatvagni. This integrative management may also have favourably modulated gut microbial dysbiosis, supporting metabolic and lipid homeostasis.

title: ROLE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE IN PERSONALIZED MEDICINE A COMPREHENSIVE REVIEW
abstractText: The idea behind personalized medicine is simple to explain but difficult to execute: prevention, diagnosis, prognosis and treatment should be based on the biological, clinical, environmental and behavioral specificities of the patient who is in front of the clinician, rather than the average patient of a trial population. In fact, one of the key technologies driving this goal is artificial intelligence (AI), which can manage data that is often too big, too complex, or too multidimensional to be comfortably handled by traditional statistical methods. Nevertheless, AI has not fully matured and is still experiencing its adolescence in the field of personalized medicine in the domains of biomarker discovery, disease subtyping, risk prediction, early diagnosis, treatment-response modelling, pharmacogenomics, digital pathology, longitudinal monitoring, and clinical decision support.t outlines the conceptual foundations, types of data that enable personalization, key clinical applications, ethical and legal issues yet to be resolved, and obstacles between potential research and clinical practice. The perpetual debate is that AI does not take over the doctor's decision-making, but rather helps doctors to access more information than they could retain within their minds all at once.

title: CHRONOBIOLOGICAL FOUNDATIONS IN CLASSICAL AYURVEDA: BRIDGING KALA-BHOJANA, DINACHARYA, RITUCHARYA, AND VEGA VIDHI WITH MOLECULAR EPIGENETICS AND CIRCADIAN BIOLOGY
abstractText: Contemporary preventive care faces challenges from lifestyle-related disorders, metabolic syndromes, and stress-linked psychiatric conditions. Many of these issues stem from circadian misalignment and elevated allostatic load. Millennia before the discovery of transcription-translation loops, classical Ayurvedic texts (Charaka Samhita, Sushruta Samhita, and Ashtanga Hridaya) formulated an advanced chronobiological framework based on Dinacharya (daily routines), Ritucharya (seasonal routines), Kala-Bhojana Siddhanta (chrononutrition), and Vega Vidhi (impulse regulation). This paper provides an original, independent critical analysis bridging these classical frameworks with modern molecular biology and chronobiology. Specifically, we examine. Kala-Bhojana Siddhanta alongside contemporary time-restricted feeding, focusing on peripheral metabolicentrainment, AMP-activated protein kinase pathways, and sirtuin regulation. • The mechanistic connections linking Dinacharya and Ritucharya to epigenetic modifications—exploring how behavioral entrainment regulates DNA methylation, histone acetylation, and non-coding RNA expression to support immunity and cellular proteostasis.• The neurobiological and autonomic consequences of Vega Dharana (suppression of somatic urges) versus Dharaniya Vega (restraint of destructive psychological impulses), with a focus on autonomic balance, visceral signaling, and limbic regulation. By synthesizing classical Sanskrit science with modern empirical chronobiology, this review outlines an integrated, personalized framework for lifestyle medicine.

title: SUVARNAPRASHANA IN CHILDREN: CLASSICAL FOUNDATIONS, PHARMACOLOGICAL PERSPECTIVES, CLINICAL EVIDENCE AND SAFETY CONSIDERATIONS
abstractText: Background: Suvarnaprashana is a traditional Ayurvedic pediatric practice described in Kashyapa Samhita under Lehana and newborn care. It involves oral administration of processed gold, traditionally with Madhu (honey), Ghrita (ghee), and selected herbal ingredients. Classical texts attribute benefits related to Medha (intellectual function), Agni (digestion), Bala (strength), longevity, and general health. Objective: To critically review the classical foundations and contemporary evidence regarding the immunomodulatory, nootropic, growth-related, and safety effects of Suvarnaprashana in children. Materials and Methods: Classical Ayurvedic literature and contemporary biomedical literature were reviewed, focusing on physicochemical characterization, experimental studies, clinical trials, and review literature. Study design, interventions, outcomes, and limitations were considered Results: Studies suggest that appropriately prepared Swarna Bhasma may contain nanostructured gold particles, although composition varies with preparation methods. Experimental studies report potential immunomodulatory and nootropic effects. A randomized clinical trial in healthy infants found Swarna Prashana to be well tolerated, but most between-group anthropometric, biochemical, and immunological outcomes were not statistically significant. Review evidence highlights substantial clinical heterogeneity and the need for better-designed trials. Conclusion: Suvarnaprashana provides an important link between classical Ayurvedic pediatrics and contemporary research. Current evidence remains insufficient to establish definitive clinical efficacy. Future studies should prioritize standardized formulations, physicochemical characterization, long-term safety assessment, and adequately powered randomized controlled trials.

title: COMPARATIVE EVALUATION OF VARUNADYA TAILA MATRA BASTI AND TRIKATU GUTIKA IN VATASHTHEELA (BENIGN PROSTATIC HYPERPLASIA)
abstractText: Vatashtheela, described in Ayurveda under Mootraghata, closely resembles Benign Prostatic Hyperplasia (BPH) in modern medicine and affects elderly males. The present single-blind comparative clinical study evaluated the efficacy of Varunadya Taila Matra Basti and Trikatu Gutika in 36 patients aged above 50 years. Group A received 30 ml Varunadya Taila Matra Basti per rectum once daily, while Group B received Trikatu Gutika orally twice daily. Therapeutic response was assessed using IPSS, uroflowmetry, Prostate volume and Post-void residual urine (PVRU). Both groups showed significant symptomatic and objective improvement, with reduction in IPSS, improvement in urinary flow, and decreased prostate volume and PVRU. No adverse effects were reported. The findings suggest that both interventions are safe and effective Ayurvedic approaches for the non-surgical management of Vatashtheela (BPH), with comparatively greater overall improvement observed with Varunadya Taila Matra Basti.

title: EFFECTS OF ETHANOL LEAF EXTRACT OF Spondia mombin ON SURGICALLY-INDUCED DUODENAL ULCER IN ADULT MALE WISTAR-RATS
abstractText: Background: Duodenal ulcer (DU) is a common gastrointestinal disorder resulting from disruption of the balance between aggressive factors and mucosal protective mechanisms. Although Spondias mombin has demonstrated gastroprotective and ulcer-healing properties, limited information is available regarding its effects on surgically-induced DU and duodenal histoarchitecture. This study investigated the effects of ethanol leaf extract of Spondias mombin on surgically induced DU in adult male Wistar rats. Methods: Thirty Wistar rats were randomly divided into six groups of five rats each. DU was induced in Groups II–VI by submucosal injection of 0.02 mL of 20% acetic acid. Group I is the normal control which received only normal saline (1 mL/kg) orally for 15 days. Group II served as the ulcer control and was sacrificed 24 h after ulcer induction, while Group III received normal saline (1 mL/kg) orally for 14 days as the recovery group. Groups IV–VI received ethanol leaf extract of S. mombin at 200, 400, and 800 mg/kg body weight, respectively, for 14 days. Duodenal tissues were assessed using haematoxylin and eosin (H&E) and Masson's trichrome staining. Results: The normal control group showed relatively intact and well-developed villous architecture with preserved glandular and connective-tissue organization. The ulcer control group demonstrated marked mucosal disruption, characterized by irregular, shortened, blunted and eroded villi, with architectural disorganization. The recovery group showed partial restoration of the duodenal architecture. Treatment with ethanol leaf extract of S. mombin resulted in progressive improvement in villous tissue organization, with the 800 mg/kg group showing the most pronounced morphological restoration and features comparatively closer to the normal control. Masson's trichrome staining demonstrated differences in collagen distribution and organization, consistent with connective-tissue remodeling during mucosal repair. Conclusion: Ethanol leaf extract of Spondias mombin restored the injured duodenal tissue, providing a beneficial effect on the histoarchitecture of acetic-acid-induced duodenal ulcer in Wistar rats.

title: MANAGEMENT OF STHAVARA VISHA W.S.R TO KERALEEYA VISHA CHIKITSA GRANTHAS
abstractText: In Agadatantra, Visha is broadly categorized into two major origin-based classes: Sthavara Visha and Jangama Visha. Sthavara Visha encompasses toxic substances derived from plant sources as well as minerals and metals. Survey data and classical literature highlight that among various Sthavara Visha exposures, Bhallataka (Semecarpus anacardium) poisoning is the commonest reported. Other poisons such as Agnishikha (Gloriosa superba), Datura (Datura metel), and Kupilu (Strychnos nux-vomica) are also frequently encountered. Furthermore, concepts such as Dooshivisha (latent/chronic toxin) and Bhinna Visha (partially neutralized or altered toxin) share close therapeutic parallels with Sthavara Visha, requiring structured management protocols. A conceptual study on how to manage sthavara visha as per Keraleeya visha granthas been carried out in this study.

title: FORMULATION, OPTIMIZATION AND ESTIMATION OF CELECOXIB TOPICAL EMULGEL
abstractText: Celecoxib, a selective cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) inhibitor, is widely used for chronic inflammatory disorders such as rheumatoid arthritis and osteoarthritis. However, its clinical utility via oral administration is restricted by negligible aqueous solubility, extensive first-pass hepatic metabolism by CYP2C9, and adverse gastrointestinal, renal, and cardiovascular effects. The objective of the present investigation was to formulate, optimize, and characterize a stable celecoxib topical emulgel to achieve sustained localized anti-inflammatory action, enhance cutaneous permeability, and minimize systemic exposure. A 23 factorial design was implemented to optimize the formulation parameters by evaluating three independent variables: gelling agent type (Carbopol 934 vs. HPMC), concentration of liquid paraffin (5.0% vs. 7.5% w/w), and emulsifier blend concentration (Tween 20 / Span 20 at 1.5% vs. 2.5% w/w). Preformulation screening included organoleptic testing, UV spectrophotometric calibration, equilibrium solubility profiling across multiple solvents, and forced degradation studies under stress conditions. Drug-excipient compatibility was investigated using Attenuated Total Reflectance Fourier-Transform Infrared (ATR-FTIR) spectroscopy and Differential Scanning Calorimetry (DSC). Formulations (F1–F8) were evaluated for physical appearance, pH, rheological behavior, spreadability, drug content uniformity, in vitro drug release via vertical Franz diffusion cells across synthetic dialysis membranes, mathematical release kinetics, ex-vivo permeation through excised porcine skin, and accelerated stability according to ICH Q1A(R2) guidelines. Preformulation confirmed drug purity with a melting endotherm at 161.8 °C and λmax of 252 nm. FTIR and DSC studies demonstrated the preservation of characteristic functional peaks (3336 cm−1 N–H stretch, 1348 cm−1 SO2 stretch) without chemical degradation. All eight batches exhibited skin-compatible pH (6.18 ± 0.04 to 6.42 ± 0.04), viscosity ranging between 21,450 ± 120 and 29,580 ± 180 cP, spreadability between 17.6 ± 0.30 and 24.6 ± 0.42 g·cm/s, and drug content between 97.42 ± 0.64% and 99.48 ± 0.29%. Formulation F6 (2.5% HPMC, 5% liquid paraffin, 2.5% surfactant) was identified as the optimal batch, demonstrating superior spreadability (22.4 ± 0.34 g·cm/s), desirable viscosity (24,120 ± 145 cP), and highest sustained in vitro cumulative drug release of 93.2 ± 1.2% over 36 hours compared to the standard formulation (45%). Release kinetics best fitted the Higuchi diffusion model (R2=0.996), confirming diffusion-controlled drug release. Ex-vivo permeation revealed a cumulative transdermal delivery of 75.6 ± 1.9% (4267±107 μg/cm2) and cutaneous retention of 12.8 ± 1.1%. Accelerated stability studies (40±2 ∘C / 75±5% RH for 3 months) showed no significant degradation or physicochemical alterations (p>0.05). The developed celecoxib emulgel (F6) provides controlled release, high skin permeation, and excellent physical stability, making it an effective alternative to conventional oral celecoxib delivery.

title: REGULATORY REQUIREMENTS FOR THE APPROVAL OF NARCOTIC DRUGS AS PER CDSCO IN INDIA IN COMPARISON WITH CANADA
abstractText: Narcotic drugs, derived largely from the opium poppy, have powerful pain-relieving effects but also carry a high risk of addiction. Therefore, most countries place strict controls on the manufacturing, trading, and use of these drugs. This report examines the regulatory frameworks governing narcotic drugs in India and Canada, alongside the international classification set out by the 1961 UN Single Convention. India relies on the NDPS Act, along with specialized bodies such as the CBN and NCB, working alongside the general regulator, CDSCO. Canada regulates narcotics mainly through Health Canada and the CDSA, using a single permit-based system under the Narcotic Control Regulations. The comparison highlights how each country licenses the manufacturing, import, export, and sale of narcotic drugs, and what these differences reveal about their regulatory approaches.

title: DEVELOPMENT AND EVALUATION OF AN ARTEMISIA ANNUA HERBAL GEL FOR ANTIMICROBIAL ACTIVITY
abstractText: The present study was undertaken with the aim of developing and evaluating an Artemisia annua L. herbal gel for antimicrobial activity. The aerial parts of A. annua were collected from Bagsiad, Mandi, Himachal Pradesh, during September 2025 and authenticated by a qualified botanist. The collected plant material was shade-dried, powdered, and extracted with ethanol using the Soxhlet extraction method. The prepared extract was subjected to loss on drying and preliminary phytochemical screening to identify the major classes of secondary metabolites. The ethanolic extract was subsequently incorporated into Carbopol 940-based topical gel formulations. Five formulations (F1–F5) were prepared using different concentrations of Carbopol 940 and propylene glycol, while methyl paraben, propyl paraben, and triethanolamine were used as preservatives and pH-adjusting/neutralizing agents. The prepared formulations were evaluated for physical appearance, homogeneity, pH, viscosity, spreadability, and extrudability. Among the formulations, F2 was selected as the optimized formulation based on its overall physicochemical properties. F2 showed a smooth and homogeneous appearance, pH of 5.80 ± 0.046, viscosity of 1285 ± 15.2 cP, spreadability of 6.80 ± 0.08, and excellent extrudability. The optimized formulation was further evaluated for in-vitro antibacterial activity using the agar disc diffusion method against Escherichia coli, Staphylococcus aureus, and Pseudomonas aeruginosa. F2 exhibited zones of inhibition of 10 mm against E. coli and 11 mm against P. aeruginosa, whereas no zone of inhibition was observed against S. aureus under the experimental conditions. The findings indicate that the ethanolic extract of A. annua can be successfully incorporated into a Carbopol 940-based topical gel with acceptable physicochemical characteristics and measurable antibacterial activity. The developed F2 formulation may therefore have potential as a topical herbal antimicrobial preparation. Further studies are recommended to evaluate its stability, safety, skin irritation, drug release, permeation, and antimicrobial efficacy against a broader range of microorganisms.

title: FORMULATION AND EVALUATION OF HERBAL ANTIMICROBIAL GEL CONTAINING APRAJITA CLITORIA TERNATEA L.
abstractText: Skin infections caused by pathogenic microorganisms remain a major healthcare concern, and the increasing prevalence of antimicrobial resistance has highlighted the need for safer and more effective topical therapies. Herbal medicines have gained considerable attention because of their broad therapeutic potential, low toxicity, and improved patient acceptability. The present study aimed to formulate and evaluate a herbal antimicrobial gel containing the ethanolic extract of Clitoria ternatea L. (Aprajita). Fresh flowers of Clitoria ternatea were collected, authenticated, shade-dried, powdered, and extracted using ethanol. The extract was incorporated into a Carbopol-based gel using suitable excipients to obtain a stable topical formulation. The prepared gel was evaluated for its physicochemical properties, including appearance, homogeneity, pH, viscosity, spreadability, extrudability, washability, and stability. Antimicrobial activity was assessed against selected pathogenic microorganisms using a standard microbiological method. The formulated gel exhibited acceptable physical characteristics, good consistency, suitable pH for topical application, satisfactory spreadability, and excellent stability throughout the study period. The formulation demonstrated promising antimicrobial activity, indicating the presence of bioactive phytoconstituents in the ethanolic extract of Clitoria ternatea. These findings suggest that the developed herbal gel has potential as a safe and effective topical antimicrobial formulation for the management of superficial skin infections. Further preclinical and clinical investigations are recommended to establish its therapeutic efficacy and long-term safety.

title: WILLINGNESS TO ACCEPT MALARIA VACCINE AMONG CAREGIVERS OF UNDER-5 CHILDREN: A CROSS-SECTIONAL STUDY AT PCMH AND CONNAUGHT HOSPITAL, FREETOWN
abstractText: Background: Sierra Leone has one of the highest malaria burdens in the world and children under 5 years of age are the most vulnerable. The malaria vaccine RTS,S/AS01 is a promising vaccine, but its use is still very low (around 50% of eligible children nationally). Knowledge of the willingness of caregivers and related factors is crucial for enhancing vaccine uptake. Objective: To evaluate the uptake of malaria vaccination among caregivers of under fives children attending two major government hospitals in Freetown and to determine factors influencing uptake of malaria vaccine. Method: A cross sectional study was carried out from January to July 2025 at Princess Christian Maternity Hospital (PCMH) and Connaught Hospital. The immunization registers were used to select 201 caregiver-child records through systematic random sampling. Structured questionnaires were employed to gather data on the socio-demographic characteristics, awareness, trust, and perceived effectiveness. Chi-square tests and logistic regression (SPSS v25) were used to identify predictors of vaccine acceptance. Results: Vaccine uptake was only 21.9% (44/201). The most common primary barriers were concerns about side effects (58.0%) and lack of awareness (29.3%). Significant predictors of acceptance were: awareness (χ²=17.82, p<0.001; OR=5.63, 95%CI: 2.36-13.45), perceived effectiveness (OR=3.12, 95%CI: 1.74-5.59, p<0.001), trust in healthcare workers (OR=2.89, 95%CI: 1.65-5.08, p<0.001), tertiary education (OR=2.34, 95%CI: 1.31-4.17, p=0.005), and urban residence (OR=2.12, 95%CI: 1.15-3.91, p=0.015). Conclusion: The acceptance of malaria vaccines among caregivers in Freetown is very low. The main obstacles are fear of side effects and lack of awareness. There is an urgent need for targeted health education with trusted health care providers to improve vaccine uptake and reduce child mortality due to malaria in Sierra Leone. This study explores the attitudes of caregivers towards the introduction of a malaria vaccine in under-fives in Sierra Leone, with a particular focus on vaccine acceptance.

title: PERI-SURGICAL PROCEDURES: A BOOK
abstractText: Surgery is one of the most important fields of modern medicine. It combines scientific knowledge, technical skill, patient care, safety, and continuous innovation. Over time, surgical practice has advanced from basic procedures to highly developed techniques supported by anesthesia, antisepsis, imaging, minimally invasive methods, and robotic technology. The purpose of this book “Peri-Surgical Procedures” is to provide a clear and structured understanding of how surgical procedures are planned, performed, monitored, and managed. It is aspired that this book will serve as a useful foundation for readers who wish to build their knowledge of peri-surgical procedures and patient care principles.

title: DEVELOPMENT OF ANALYTICAL SPECIFICATIONS AND VALIDATION OF DEFLAZACORT USING RP-HPLC
abstractText: Background: Deflazacort is a synthetic glucocorticoid used for its anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive effects. Reliable analytical methods are required for its accurate estimation in pharmaceutical formulations and for routine quality control. The present study aimed to develop and validate a simple, accurate, precise, robust, and stability-indicating reverse-phase high-performance liquid chromatography (RP-HPLC) method for the quantitative estimation of Deflazacort. Methods: The RP-HPLC method was developed using a reversed-phase C18 column (250 × 4.6 mm, 5 µm) with acetonitrile:water (80:20, v/v) as the mobile phase. The flow rate was maintained at 1.0 mL/min, injection volume was 20 µL, and detection was performed at 244 nm. Deflazacort standard and marketed tablet sample solutions were prepared and analyzed under the optimized chromatographic conditions. The method was validated for specificity, linearity, accuracy, precision, robustness, and solution stability. Forced degradation studies were performed under acidic, alkaline, oxidative, thermal, and photolytic stress conditions. Results: The developed method produced a distinct Deflazacort peak at approximately 4.18 min. The method showed good linearity over 50–150 µg/mL, with a correlation coefficient of 0.9998 and R² of 0.9996. The mean recovery was 99.59%, while precision and repeatability showed 0.08% RSD and intermediate precision showed 0.07% RSD. The method remained robust following deliberate changes in chromatographic conditions, and standard and sample solutions remained stable for 48 hours. Forced degradation showed the highest degradation under alkaline conditions (14.58%), followed by oxidative (10.34%), acidic (7.46%), photolytic (6.09%), and thermal (3.62%) conditions. The degradation peaks were adequately separated from the Deflazacort peak. Application of the method to the marketed tablet formulation gave a mean assay of 99.17% of the labelled claim with 0.42% RSD. Conclusion: The developed RP-HPLC method was found to be specific, accurate, precise, robust, and stability-indicating. The method can be suitably applied for the routine quantitative analysis and quality control of Deflazacort in pharmaceutical formulations.

title: CONCEPT, CLASSIFICATION, AND TOXICOLOGICAL PERSPECTIVES OF STHAVARA VISHA: A COMPREHENSIVE REVIEW OF CLASSICAL AYURVEDIC LITERATURE
abstractText: Agada Tantra, one of the eight classical branches of Ayurveda, provides a systematic description of poisons (Visha), their effects on the human body, methods of detoxification, and principles of management. Among the different categories of poisons, Sthavara Visha comprises toxic substances originating from immobile sources, predominantly poisonous plants, minerals, and metals. The knowledge related to Sthavara Visha is dispersed across various classical Ayurvedic texts, making comprehensive understanding difficult for students, clinicians, and researchers. The present review aims to compile, analyze, and critically interpret the classical descriptions of Sthavara Visha available in major Ayurvedic treatises. A narrative review methodology was adopted by reviewing authoritative Ayurvedic texts, including Charaka Samhita, Sushruta Samhita, Ashtanga Hridaya, Bhava Prakasha Nighantu, Kaiyadeva Nighantu, Sharangadhara Samhita, Rasatarangini, and other relevant classical references. Contemporary scientific literature was considered where appropriate to discuss the present-day relevance of these concepts.

title: CLINICAL EVALUATION OF KAMPILLAKADI TAILA IN DUSHTA- VRANA
abstractText: According to Ayurveda, every Vikriti is brought on by a disruption in Doshas, which in turn leads to the dysfunction of Dhatus and Srotas. These disturbances may produce ideal circumstances for the emergence of chronic illnesses. Similarly, Vrana is caused not just by the individual vitiated Dosha, but also with the combined vitiation of Dhatu, Srotas and some external factors. The clinical trial, titled “Clinical Evaluation of Kampillakadi Taila in Dushta-Vrana” aimed to evaluate the clinical efficacy of classical Ayurvedic formulation in the management of Dushta-Vrana. Total 34 patients were taken on the basis of diagnostic criteria based on inclusion and exclusion criteria. Kampillakadi Taila was applied locally, according to the size of Dushta-Vrana with the help of specially designed frame (Vrana-vasti) 15 minutes, once daily. Dressing was done with sterile bandage and changed daily. Assessment of therapeutic outcomes was conducted using subjective parameters (pain, itching) and objective parameters (tenderness, foul smell, floor/granulation tissue, size and discharges), with statistical analysis performed to evaluate the efficacy of Taila. The results demonstrated that the treatment was highly effective, with 73.5% of patients achieving complete or marked relief, and all patients demonstrating some degree of clinical improvement with no complications or recurrences during the treatment or follow up period.

title: A CASE REPORT ON MANAGEMENT OF RECURRENT ACNE VULGARIS WITH RAKTAMOKSHANA AND SHAMANA THERAPY
abstractText: Acne is a prevalent chronic inflammatory condition mostly affecting teenagers and young adults, According to Ayurveda, Yuvanpidika, a condition linked to Kapha, Vata, and Rakta involvement may be connected to Acne Vulgaris. For the treatment of such problems, several Shodhana and Shamana therapies are described. A 24-year-old female patient complained of acne over back that had been present for one year, accompanied by papules, pustules, sporadic pain, and post-inflammatory pigmentation. Based on clinical evaluation and Ayurvedic investigation the illness was identified as Yuvanpidika. Following a suitable clinical evaluation and informed permission, Raktamokshana was scheduled as part of the treatment along with internal medication Manjisthadi kwatha. Clinical indicators, including the number of papules and pustules, pain/tenderness, erythema, and post-inflammatory pigmentation, were used to evaluate the patient both before and after treatment. The purpose of the case study is to demonstrate that Raktamokshana actively contributes to the treatment of recurrent Acne Vulgaris. It was found that the Ayurvedic Score based on the data of Ayurvedic clinical assessment of the treatment of various lesions, proposed in this study, as a function of treatment duration is more reliable than the Global Acne Grading Score obtained from the data of baseline value based on the assessment criteria of most severe lesions.

title: AN AYURVEDIC REVIEW OF ETIOPATHOGENESIS AND MANAGEMENT OF PRAMEHA (DIABETES MELLITUS)
abstractText: Prameha is a major metabolic disorder described in Ayurveda, characterized by excessive quantity and abnormal quality of urine along with progressive disturbance of Dosha, Dhatu, Agni, and Srotas. Classical Ayurvedic texts explain Prameha as a Tridoshaja disorder with predominant Kapha involvement and significant association with Meda Dhatu and Mutravaha Srotas. Twenty varieties of Prameha have been described based on Dosha predominance, among which Madhumeha represents an advanced stage associated with Vata predominance and tissue depletion. The disease is considered a systemic metabolic derangement rather than a condition limited to urinary abnormality. Excessive intake of Kapha-promoting foods, sedentary lifestyle, obesity, excessive sleep, and hereditary factors are described as important causes.

title: ANALYTICAL QUALITY BY DESIGN (AQBD): CURRENT ADVANCES AND FUTURE PERSPECTIVES
abstractText: Analytical methods play a vital role in pharmaceutical development, quality control, stability testing, and regulatory decision-making, as the reliability of drug product identity, strength, purity, safety, and stability depends on the quality of analytical data generated. Conventional analytical method development has traditionally followed trial-and-error and one-factor-at-a-time approaches, which can require extensive experimentation and may fail to adequately evaluate interactions among method variables. Analytical Quality by Design (AQbD) has emerged as a systematic, science-based, and risk-based approach for developing analytical procedures that are robust, reliable, and fit for their intended purpose. The AQbD framework generally begins with defining an Analytical Target Profile (ATP), followed by identification of critical analytical attributes and performance characteristics, risk assessment, identification of critical method parameters, application of Design of Experiments (DoE), establishment of a Method Operable Design Region (MODR), and development of an appropriate analytical control strategy. The recently finalized ICH Q14 guideline provides a harmonized framework for analytical procedure development and lifecycle management, while ICH Q2(R2) establishes an updated framework for analytical procedure validation. Together, these guidelines emphasize a science- and risk-based approach extending beyond validation as a standalone activity. Recent advances in AQbD include integration with multivariate analysis, chemometrics, automation, artificial intelligence, machine learning, green analytical chemistry, and real-time analytical technologies. This review discusses the fundamental concepts, workflow, statistical tools, applications, regulatory significance, advantages, challenges, and future perspectives of AQbD in pharmaceutical analysis. The integration of AQbD with digital and sustainable technologies is expected to enhance method robustness, reduce experimental burden, and support continuous analytical procedure improvement throughout the analytical lifecycle.
