title: REGULATORY RECURRENCE FOR APPROVAL OF ANDA (GENERIC DRUG) AS PER CDSCO IN INDIA COMPARISON WITH JAPAN
abstractText: Generic medicines play an important role in providing safe, effective, quality and affordable healthcare. They are developed as equivalent alternatives to brand-name medicines and must meet regulatory requirements for quality, safety, efficacy and bio equivalence. Their availability reduces healthcare expenditure, improves access to essential medicines and promotes competition in the pharmaceutical market. The Abbreviated New Drug Application (ANDA) is an important pathway for generic drug approval. It allows manufacturers to demonstrate equivalence to a Reference Listed Drug without repeating the complete development programme of the original product. Major requirements include bioequivalence studies, pharmaceutical quality, Chemistry, Manufacturing and Controls (CMC), current Good Manufacturing Practices (cGMP), stability testing and impurity control. In India, generic medicines are regulated under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940, Drugs Rules, 1945 and applicable regulatory requirements. The Central Drugs Standard Control Organization (CDSCO) performs important functions related to drug quality, safety, efficacy, clinical trials, marketing authorization, imported drugs, pharmacovigilance and bioavailability/bioequivalence requirements. In Japan, the regulatory framework involves the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW) and the Pharmaceuticals and Medical Devices Agency (PMDA). PMDA conducts scientific and technical reviews, inspections and post-marketing safety activities, while MHLW provides final regulatory authorization. This comparative study evaluates the generic drug approval systems of India and Japan, focusing on regulatory requirements, bioequivalence, quality standards, review procedures and patient safety. It highlights major similarities and differences between the two regulatory frameworks and their approaches to ensuring the availability of safe, effective and affordable generic medicines.

title: OXALIDACEAE FAMILY: AN INTEGRATIVE REVIEW OF BOTANICAL DIVERSITY, PHARMACOGNOSTIC FEATURES, PHYTOCHEMICAL CONSTITUENTS AND AYURVEDIC–ETHNOMEDICINAL SIGNIFICANCE
abstractText: Background: Oxalidaceae R.Br. is a distinctive flowering-plant family placed in the order Oxalidales. Current Plants of the World Online (POWO) treatment recognizes five accepted genera—Averrhoa L., Biophytum DC., Dapania Korth., Oxalis L. and Sarcotheca Blume—and approximately 570 species, with Oxalis representing the largest genus. Members occur mainly in tropical and subtropical regions and include plants of nutritional, ornamental, ecological and medicinal importance.[1,2] Objective: This review integrates botanical characteristics, pharmacognostic significance, ethnomedicinal and Ayurvedic relevance, phytochemical composition, pharmacological evidence and toxicological considerations of selected medicinally important members of Oxalidaceae. Materials and Methods: A narrative literature review was prepared from the literature contained in the original manuscript and supplemented with current taxonomic information from Kew Plants of the World Online and peer-reviewed literature indexed in PubMed. Particular attention was given to Oxalis corniculata L., Biophytum sensitivum DC., Averrhoa carambola L. and Averrhoa bilimbi L. The evidence was interpreted according to the level of experimental or clinical support available. Results: The family is characterized by alternate leaves that are often compound, actinomorphic bisexual flowers, usually five sepals and five petals, ten stamens arranged in two whorls, a superior ovary and generally capsular fruits.[1] Selected medicinally investigated species contain flavonoids, phenolic compounds, biflavonoids, tannins, terpenoids, polysaccharides and organic acids. Experimental studies report antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, antidiabetic, wound-healing, immunomodulatory and anticancer activities for selected taxa, but most evidence remains preclinical.[3–6] Averrhoa carambola is of particular safety interest because oxalate and caramboxin have been associated with renal and neurological toxicity.[8–10] Conclusion: Oxalidaceae represents a valuable reservoir of medicinal and nutritionally important plants. Future research should emphasize botanical authentication, pharmacognostic standardization, chemical fingerprinting, mechanism-based investigations, pharmacokinetics, toxicity assessment, herb–drug interaction studies and well-designed clinical trials. Integration of classical Ayurvedic Dravyaguna knowledge with modern pharmacognosy and pharmacology may support scientifically rigorous evaluation of medicinal species.

title: A CASE STUDY OF KRIYAKALPA BIDALAKA'S EFFICACY IN BLEPHARITIS
abstractText: Background: Blepharitis is a chronic inflammatory disorder of the eyelid margins characterized by itching, redness, swelling, irritation, and discomfort. Conventional treatment mainly includes eyelid hygiene, antibiotics, and anti-inflammatory agents; however, recurrence is common. In Ayurveda, Bidalaka is a well-described Kriyakalpa indicated in the acute stage of ophthalmic disorders and is believed to reduce inflammation and promote healing. Aim: To evaluate the efficacy of Bidalaka Kriyakalpa in the management of blepharitis. Materials and Methods: A single-case clinical study was conducted in the Department of Shalakyatantra. A 64-year-old male patient presented with itching, swelling of both eyelids, and intermittent redness of both eyes for 15 days. Bidalaka was prepared using Triphala, Yashtimadhu, Haridra, Raktachandana, Spatika, and Sunthi powders mixed with sterile water to form a paste. The formulation was applied over the closed eyelids, excluding the lid margins, once daily for 20 minutes for 14 consecutive days. Clinical assessment was based on changes in itching, swelling, and redness before and after treatment. Results: After treatment, there was a noticeable improvement in clinical outcomes. Redness dramatically decreased from moderate to mild, eyelid swelling decreased, and itching totally disappeared. During the course of the treatment, the patient reported increased eye comfort and no side effects. Conclusion: In this instance of blepharitis, Bidalaka Kriyakalpa showed encouraging therapeutic results by lowering inflammation and easing related symptoms. The process is a useful Ayurvedic treatment option for eyelid diseases because it is easy, safe, economical, and non-invasive. To confirm these results and determine its long-term effectiveness, however, further extensive controlled clinical trials are required.

title: ETIOLOGICAL STUDY OF RHEUMATOLOGICAL DISEASES MENTIONED IN AYURVEDA
abstractText: According to National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases, U.S (NIAMS) “Rheumatic diseases are conditions that cause pain, stiffness, and swelling in joints and surrounding tissues, and may also affect internal organs in systemic forms.” 1 According to the World Health Organization, rheumatological diseases affect nearly 20–33% of the global population, making them one of the leading causes of disability worldwide. 2 In contemporary medicine, such conditions are commonly explained through mechanisms involving inflammation, autoimmunity, metabolic disturbances, and degenerative processes.

title: DEVELOPMENT AND VALIDATION OF A STABILITY INDICATING RP-HPLC METHOD FOR SIMULTANEOUS ESTIMATION OF PREGABALIN AND ETORICOXIB IN PHARMACEUTICAL DOSAGE FORM
abstractText: The present study was carried out to develop and validate a stability-indicating Reverse Phase High-Performance Liquid Chromatography (RP-HPLC) method for simultaneous estimation of Pregabalin and Etoricoxib in pharmaceutical dosage forms. The method was developed by optimizing the detection wavelength, chromatographic column, mobile phase, flow rate, column temperature and other chromatographic conditions. An Inertsil ODS-3 C18 column (250 × 4.6 mm, 5 µm) was used for separation. The optimized mobile phase consisted of potassium dihydrogen phosphate buffer adjusted to pH 3.0 ± 0.05 with orthophosphoric acid and acetonitrile (60:40, v/v), with a flow rate of 1.0 mL/min and detection at 234 nm. The method was validated according to ICH guidelines for specificity, linearity, accuracy, precision, sensitivity, robustness and solution stability. The method showed good linearity for Pregabalin and Etoricoxib over the selected concentration ranges, with correlation coefficients of 0.9998 and 0.9999, respectively. Mean recoveries were within the acceptable range, and precision studies showed low variability. Forced degradation studies were performed under acidic, alkaline, oxidative, thermal, photolytic and neutral conditions. The degradation products were adequately separated from the main drug peaks, confirming the stability-indicating nature of the method. The method was also successfully applied to a marketed tablet formulation, giving assay values of 99.49% for Pregabalin and 99.52% for Etoricoxib. The developed method is simple, accurate, precise and suitable for routine quality control analysis of Pregabalin and Etoricoxib combination formulations.

title: THERAPEUTIC ACTION OF TAKRABASTI IN GRAHANI ROGA: A CONCEPTUAL REVIEW
abstractText: Grahani Roga is an important disorder described in Ayurveda, primarily involving impairment of Agni and disturbance of the normal functioning of Grahani, resulting in irregular digestion and abnormal bowel movements. The pathogenesis of Grahani involves Agnimandya, Dosha Dushti and impaired digestion and absorption, with Vata playing a major role in the manifestation of irregular bowel movements. Takra is traditionally described as Laghu, Grahi, Deepana and beneficial in disorders associated with impaired digestion and bowel function. Takrabasti, in which Takra is administered as an Avapa dravya in Basti therapy, provides a therapeutic approach aimed at correcting Agni, regulating Vata and restoring the physiological function of Grahani. This review consolidates the classical Ayurvedic understanding of Grahani Roga and Takrabasti with findings from contemporary clinical literature to provide an integrated perspective on its possible therapeutic role in IBS. The potential mechanisms include modulation of gastrointestinal motility, improvement of digestive function, regulation of gut microbial balance and support of intestinal mucosal function. Available clinical studies and reported evidence suggest that Takrabasti may contribute to improvement in stool frequency, consistency, abdominal discomfort, bloating and other gastrointestinal symptoms.

title: VATARAKTA IN AYURVEDA: CLASSICAL CONCEPTS, CONTEMPORARY CORRELATION WITH GOUT AND EVIDENCE-BASED MANAGEMENT
abstractText: Background Vatarakta is a distinctive disorder described in Ayurvedic classics, characterized by the simultaneous vitiation and interaction of Vata Dosha and Rakta Dhatu. The disease manifests predominantly with severe pain, swelling, tenderness, burning sensation, stiffness and restricted joint movements. Owing to similarities in clinical presentation, particularly acute inflammatory arthritis involving peripheral joints, Vatarakta is frequently correlated with gouty arthritis in contemporary medicine. Aim To critically review the classical Ayurvedic understanding of Vatarakta, its etiopathogenesis, clinical manifestations, types, diagnostic considerations and therapeutic principles, and to examine its contemporary correlation with gout and hyperuricemia. Materials and Methods A narrative literature review was undertaken using major Ayurvedic classical texts, including Charaka Samhita, Sushruta Samhita and Ashtanga Hridaya, along with peer-reviewed literature indexed in PubMed and other scholarly databases. Contemporary studies concerning Ayurvedic management of gouty arthritis and Vatarakta were also reviewed. Results Ayurvedic literature describes Vatarakta as a disorder arising from the vitiation of Vata and Rakta, with obstruction and mutual aggravation playing a central role in its pathogenesis. The condition is broadly described as Uttana and Gambhira Vatarakta. Management is individualized according to Dosha, Dhatu, stage and severity of disease and includes Nidana Parivarjana, Shamana Chikitsa, Shodhana Chikitsa, external therapies, Raktamokshana where indicated, Basti, Virechana and Rasayana therapy. Contemporary clinical studies have reported improvements in pain, inflammatory manifestations and serum uric acid following selected Ayurvedic interventions; however, the available evidence remains heterogeneous and requires confirmation through larger, well-designed controlled trials. Conclusion Vatarakta represents an important Ayurvedic model of inflammatory and metabolic musculoskeletal disease. Its classical emphasis on dietary regulation, individualized treatment, correction of Dosha-Dushya imbalance and long-term lifestyle modification offers a potentially valuable complementary framework in the management of gout. Rigorous clinical research integrating Ayurvedic diagnostic parameters with validated biomedical outcomes is required.

title: PRESCRIBING PATTERNS OF PSYCHOTROPIC DRUGS IN PATIENTS WITH SCHIZOPHRENIA IN A TERTIARY CARE HOSPITAL: A CROSS-SECTIONAL STUDY
abstractText: Background: Prescription pattern studies help assess the rational use of medicines in real-world clinical practice. Objective: To describe psychotropic prescribing patterns and World Health Organisation and International Network for Rational Use of Drugs (WHO-INRUD) prescribing indicators among outpatients with schizophrenia. Methods: This cross-sectional observational study included 154 adults with DSM-5 schizophrenia attending the psychiatry outpatient department of Pt. B. D. Sharma PGIMS, Rohtak, Haryana. Prescription details were recorded and analysed descriptively. Results: The mean age was 45.75 ± 14.42 years; 80 participants (52.0%) were women. Second-generation antipsychotics accounted for 173 of 190 antipsychotic orders (91.05%) and olanzapine was the most frequently prescribed agent (104 orders, 54.74%). Two or more psychotropics were prescribed to 129 patients (83.8%), whereas high-level polypharmacy (five or more psychotropics) was seen in one patient (0.64%). Antidepressants were used in 72 encounters, mainly selective serotonin reuptake inhibitors (67, 93.06%). The mean number of drugs per prescription was 2.65 and 97.98% of psychotropic drugs were prescribed by generic name. Injectable drug use was 1.30%, no fixed-dose combination was prescribed and 90.75% of psychotropic drugs were listed in the Government of Haryana Essential Drug List.

title: RESEARCH ON IN-VITRO ANTI-ULCER AND ANTHELMINTIC ACTIVITY BY ETHANOLIC EXTRACT OF IPOMOEA OBSCURA
abstractText: Medicinal plants continue to be a rich source of pharmacologically active compounds, and Ipomoea obscura (L.) Ker Gawl. (Convolvulaceae), a climbing plant used in traditional medicine, is one such species worth closer study given its reported antioxidant, anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties. This study looked at the phytochemical composition of an ethanolic leaf extract of I. obscura alongside its in-vitro anti-ulcer and anthelmintic potential. Leaves were collected and authenticated, then shade-dried, powdered, and extracted using cold maceration with ethanol. Phytochemical screening revealed the presence of carbohydrates, proteins and amino acids, alkaloids, flavonoids, phenolics, tannins, terpenoids, glycosides and saponins; steroids were absent. Anti-ulcer activity was gauged using the acid-neutralizing capacity (ANC) method, with an aluminiumhydroxide–magnesium hydroxide formulation as the reference antacid. The extract yielded ANC values of 116, 64.5, 28.8 and 14.65 mEq/g at concentrations of 100, 200, 500 and 1000 µg/ml, compared to 27.5 mEq/g for the reference at 500 µg/ml. For anthelmintic activity, paralysis and death times were recorded in Pheretima posthuma. At 20 mg/ml, the extract induced paralysis in 12.03 minutes and death in 23.20 minutes close to albendazole's 10.54 and 22.37 minutes at the same concentration with effects becoming more pronounced at higher concentrations, while untreated worms stayed alive for up to 7 hours. Taken together, these results point to genuine acid-neutralizing and anthelmintic activity in the extract, though they represent early-stage in-vitro findings rather than proof of clinical benefit. Confirming any therapeutic releance will require more rigorous mechanistic, toxicological and in-vivo work.

title: ASSESS THE PROPORTION AND CONTRIBUTING FACTORS OF MIGRAINE AMONG NURSING STUDENTS
abstractText: The Present Study Was Conducted To Assess The Proportion And Contributing Factors Of Migraine Among Nursing Students In Selected Colleges Of Kollam District. A Quantitative Descriptive Research Design Was Adopted. A Total Of 400 Nursing Students Were Selected Using Convenience Sampling Technique. Data Were Collected Using A Socio Demographic Questionnaire, A Standardized Migraine Screening Tool, And A Self-Structured Questionnaire To Identify Contributing Factors. The Majority Of Participants Were Females (83.8%) And Belonged To The Age Group Of 20–22 Years (57.3%). The Findings Revealed That 16.8% Of Nursing Students Screened Positive For Migraine, While 83.3% Screened Negative. Among Students With Migraine, 67.2% Had Intermediate Contributing Factors, 19.4% Had Major Factors, And 13.4% Had Minor Factors. Major Contributing Factors Identified Were Lack Of Sleep, Exposure To Bright Light, And Loud Noise, While Factors Such As Prolonged Study Hours, Academic Stress, And Screen Usage Showed Moderate Influence. Caffeinated Drinks And Weather Changes Were Found To Have Minimal Impact. A Statistically Significant Association Was Found Between Migraine And Gender, Year Of Study, And Family History Of Migraine (P < 0.05). However, No Significant Association Was Observed Between Contributing Factors And Most Socio Demographic Variables, Except History Of Chronic Illness. The Study Concludes That Migraine Among Nursing Students Is Influenced By Both Biological And Lifestyle Factors, Particularly Sleep Disturbances And Academic-Related Stress. Early Identification, Effective Stress Ix Management, And Promotion Of Healthy Lifestyle Practices Are Essential To Reduce The Burden Of Migraine. The Findings Highlight The Need For Awareness Programs And Supportive Interventions Within Educational Institutions To Improve The Overall Well-Being And Academic Performance Of Nursing Students.

title: MAINSTREAM SCIENCE VS, TELEPATHY CLAIMS, AUTISTIC, INTROVERTPEOPLE AND PHYSICIAN CLINICAL PRACTICES
abstractText: The intersection of nonspeaking autism, neurodivergence (introversion), and alternative communication became a massive global focal point following the late 2024 viral release of the documentary podcast The Telepathy Tapes hosted by Ky Dickens. The series followed controversial research by psychiatrist Dr. Diane Powell, who claimed that nonverbal autistic children possess extraordinary telepathic abilities. While the general public was captivated, the scientific, medical, and autistic advocacy communities responded with severe criticism, sparking a crucial conversation regarding clinical practice frameworks, ethical care, and how the medical system interacts with autistic and introverted patients. The intersection of telepathy, autism, introversion, and physician clinical practices forms a complex dialogue between mainstream medical models, emerging neurodivergent frameworks, and controversial fringe science. The dynamics of how these concepts interconnect shape modern medical understanding and patient care.

title: COMPREHENSIVE REVIEW OF THE THERAPEUTIC POTENTIAL FOR THE PREVENTION AND TREATMENT OF SKELETAL MUSCLE ATROPHY
abstractText: The progressive loss of muscle mass, strength, and functional ability is the hallmark of skeletal muscular atrophy, a crippling medical condition. Prolonged glucocorticoid therapy, physical inactivity, cancer cachexia, ageing (sarcopenia), and chronic diseases constitute some of the physiological and pathological circumstances that cause it to develop. Chronic inflammation, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, impaired protein homeostasis, and activation of proteolytic pathways, such as the ubiquitin–proteasome, autophagy–lysosomal, and apoptotic systems, are some of the interrelated mechanisms involved in the pathogenesis of muscle atrophy. There is mounting evidence that bioactive substances produced from nature may provide useful treatment approaches to prevent muscle atrophy. Among these, ostivone has drawn notice for its strong anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects as well as its capacity to control anabolic signalling pathways

title: ANATOMICAL UNDERSTANDING OF BHUJANGASANA IN INITIAL STAGES OF LUMBAR SPONDYLOSIS
abstractText: Lumbar spondylosis, a degenerative condition affecting the intervertebral discs and facet joints of the lower spine, commonly presents with chronic low back pain, stiffness, and restricted mobility. In Ayurvedic and yogic rehabilitation, Bhujangāsana (Cobra Pose) is widely recommended as a therapeutic posture due to its spinal extension and strengthening effects. This asana gently mobilizes the lumbar vertebrae, stretches the anterior spinal structures, and strengthens the paraspinal and gluteal muscles, thereby improving lumbar stability. Regular practice helps to enhance inter vertebral space, reduce nerve root compression, and promote better postural alignment. Additionally, Bhujangasana increases blood circulation to the lumbosacral region, supports disc nutrition, and reduces muscular spasm. It's mindful breathing component further decreases pain perception by reducing stress-related muscle tension. Overall, Bhujangasana serves as an effective, non-invasive adjunct in the conservative management of lumbar spondylosis, contributing to pain reduction, improved flexibility, and enhanced functional outcomes. This article focuses on the anatomy and pathophysiology of lumbar spondylosis, its symptomatolgy and role of bhujangasana in it's management.

title: DEVELOPMENT AND CHARACTERIZATION OF SOLID DISPERSIONS OF SERTRALINE HYDROCHLORIDE FOR IMPROVED DISSOLUTION PERFORMANCE
abstractText: Sertraline hydrochloride (HCl) is a widely prescribed selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) characterized by poor aqueous solubility, that severely limits its oral bioavailability. This study is designed to increase the dissolution rate of sertraline HCl through solid dispersion formulations using hydrophilic polymeric carriers. Using a design of experiments (DOE) approach, nine solid dispersions were made using the solvent evaporation method at a 1:3 drug-to-carrier ratio. Formulations combined sertraline HCl (100 mg) with varying proportions of hydroxypropyl cellulose (HPC), polyethylene glycol 6000 (PEG 6000), polyvinylpyrrolidone K90 (PVP K90), and sodium lauryl sulfate (SLS). In vitro dissolution profiles were assessed in standard phosphate buffer (pH 6.8) using a USP Type II apparatus. All solid dispersions demonstrated significantly improved dissolution efficiency compared to pure sertraline HCl (60.92 ± 1.13% at 60 min). Formulation F7 (containing 65% HPC, 30% PEG 6000, and 5% PVP K90) emerged as optimal, achieving 95.38 ± 0.70% drug release at 60 minutes—representing a 56.56% relative improvement. F7 exhibited superior dissolution efficiency (61.96 ± 0.81%), remarkable reproducibility (RSD = 1.51%), and rapid initial kinetics. One-way ANOVA confirmed highly significant variations in drug release across formulations during early time intervals ($p < 0.001$), with profiles converging toward the 60-minute endpoint ($p = 0.626$). Pearson correlation analysis verified HPC as the primary performance-determining carrier ($r = +0.695, p = 0.038$). These findings demonstrate that solid dispersion strategies using optimized polymeric balances offer a robust and highly reproducible methodology for accelerating the dissolution profiles of BCS Class II antidepressants.

title: VATARAKTA: A COMPREHENSIVE REVIEW FROM AN AYURVEDIC PERSPECTIVE
abstractText: Vatarakta is a disease caused by the vitiation of Vata dosha and Rakta dhatu. Clinically, it presents with severe pain, swelling, discolouration, and restricted joint movements predominantly affecting the small joints of the extremities. Modern Lifestyle practises and dietary habits have contributed to the increasing prevalence of Vatarakta. Hence a comprehensive review of classical ayurvedic literature is essential.

title: AYURVEDIC REVIEW ON MANYASTHAMBHA AND ITS TREATMENT
abstractText: In the present era, stressful and busy lifestyles have increased the occurrence of various degenerative disorders. Manyastambha is one such condition, which is becoming increasingly common. It is characterized by pain, stiffness, and restricted movement of the neck. In Ayurveda, Manyastambha is described among the eighty Vataja Nanatmaja Vyadhis and also under Urdhwajatrugata Vikara. Manyastambha can be clinically correlated with cervical spondylosis in modern medicine. Cervical spondylosis is a degenerative condition affecting the cervical spine. The main symptoms are pain (Ruk) and stiffness (Stambha). In severe cases, compression of the nerve roots may occur, leading to sensory or motor disturbances.

title: OPTIMIZATION, DEVELOPMENT AND VALIDATION OF A STABILITY INDICATING RP-HPLC METHOD FOR SIMULTANEOUS QUANTIFICATION OF AMLODIPINE, OLMESARTAN AND CHLORTHALIDONE IN PHARMACEUTICAL FORMULATIONS
abstractText: The present study aimed to develop and validate a simple, rapid, accurate, precise, and stability-indicating RP-HPLC method for the simultaneous estimation of Amlodipine, Olmesartan, and Chlorthalidone in combined tablet dosage forms. The optimized method used a C18 column (250 × 4.6 mm, 5 µm) with Acetonitrile and Potassium Dihydrogen Phosphate buffer (60:40, v/v) adjusted to pH 3.0 as the mobile phase. The flow rate was 1.0 mL/min, detection wavelength was 238 nm, injection volume was 20 µL, and the total run time was 10 min. The drugs showed well-separated peaks at retention times of 2.34, 4.58, and 6.92 min for Amlodipine, Olmesartan, and Chlorthalidone, respectively. The method was validated according to ICH Q2(R2) guidelines. Good linearity was obtained with R² values of 0.9997, 0.9998, and 0.9996, respectively. Recovery was between 99.42% and 100.36%, and precision values were within the acceptable limit of 2% RSD. The LOD values were 0.27, 0.40, and 0.30 µg/mL, while LOQ values were 0.82, 1.21, and 0.91 µg/mL for the three drugs, respectively. Assay results for the marketed tablet were 99.60%, 100.30%, and 99.68% for Amlodipine, Olmesartan, and Chlorthalidone, respectively. Forced degradation studies showed 2.82–9.64% degradation under different stress conditions, with no interference from degradation products. The results confirmed that the method is suitable for routine analysis and stability studies of these drugs in combined pharmaceutical formulations.

title: CONCEPT, CLASSIFICATION, AND TOXICOLOGICAL PERSPECTIVES OF STHAVARA VISHA: A COMPREHENSIVE REVIEW OF CLASSICAL AYURVEDIC LITERATURE
abstractText: Agada Tantra, one of the eight classical branches of Ayurveda, provides a systematic description of poisons (Visha), their effects on the human body, methods of detoxification, and principles of management. Among the different categories of poisons, Sthavara Visha comprises toxic substances originating from immobile sources, predominantly poisonous plants, minerals, and metals. The knowledge related to Sthavara Visha is dispersed across various classical Ayurvedic texts, making comprehensive understanding difficult for students, clinicians, and researchers. The present review aims to compile, analyze, and critically interpret the classical descriptions of Sthavara Visha available in major Ayurvedic treatises. A narrative review methodology was adopted by reviewing authoritative Ayurvedic texts, including Charaka Samhita, Sushruta Samhita, Ashtanga Hridaya, Bhava Prakasha Nighantu, Kaiyadeva Nighantu, Sharangadhara Samhita, Rasatarangini, and other relevant classical references. Contemporary scientific literature was considered where appropriate to discuss the present-day relevance of these concepts.

title: ROLE OF KUSHTHADI AGAD IN KEETVISHA CHIKITSA W.S.R TO TRIKANTAK DAMSHA
abstractText: Introduction: Keetavisha (insect envenomation) is systematically described in classical Agadtantra literature, particularly within the Sushruta Samhita Kalpa Sthana Chapter 8, Keetakalpa Adhyaya. Acharya Sushruta identifies 67 distinct categories of Keetas, classifying Trikantaka (or Trikanta) under the Kanabha group of stinging insects. To counteract Keetavisha, Ayurvedic texts prescribe specialized anti-toxic formulations known as Agada Kalpas. An Agada works by neutralizing Gada—the pain, systemic distress and pathological damage resulting from toxic exposure. Among the diverse anti-poison remedies recorded in the Samhitas, a is recommended for treating Trikantaka Damsha (stings). This study investigates the clinical potential of Kushthadi Agada in treating Keetavisha, with a particular focus on Trikantaka Damsha, and is based on ancient manuscript principles for managing poisonous bites. Objective: To assess and analyze antitoxic action of and its potential mechanism of action in Keetvisha chikitsa. Material and Methods: Ayurvedic Samhitas were utilized to aid in the research of and Keetvisha. Information is conceptualized and synthesized from multiple papers, articles, and Samhitas. Conclusion: Ayurvedic remedies such as could assist in treating insect bites. Additional studies are required to verify their efficacy against insect bites.

title: EVALUATION OF NEUROPROTECTIVE EFFECT OF SITAGLIPTIN IN STREPTOZOTOCIN INDUCED ALZHEIMER'S DISEASE IN WISTAR RATS
abstractText: Background: This study explores the neuroprotective potential of sitagliptin, an anti-diabetic drug, in managing Alzheimer's disease (AD) symptoms in a streptozotocin (STZ)-induced rat model. Objective: This research aimed to assess whether sitagliptin could improve cognitive function and reduce anxiety by modulating acetylcholinesterase (AChE) activity. Methods: Rats were divided into five groups: a control, a negative control with only STZ, a standard treatment group with STZ and Rivastigmine, and low- and high-dose sitagliptin groups (5 mg/kg and 10 mg/kg, respectively). Cognitive performance was evaluated using the elevated plus-maze test, which measures spatial memory and anxiety-like behaviors. Results: It was showed that both low and high doses of sitagliptin led to significant behavioral improvements, with the high dose producing effects comparable to Rivastigmine, the standard AD treatment. Notably, sitagliptin administration reduced AChE activity, correlating with observed cognitive and anxiety-related improvements, suggesting its action may involve modulation of cholinergic pathways. These findings support sitagliptin's potential as an adjunct or alternative treatment for AD, especially considering its dose-dependent effects. Conclusion: The study underscores the need for further research into sitagliptin’s broader neuroprotective mechanisms, particularly its impact on AD biomarkers such as amyloid-beta and tau proteins. This research provides promising insights into the potential repositioning of sitagliptin for neurodegenerative disease management, highlighting its prospective benefits in AD treatment.

title: CURRENT AND EMERGING PHARMACOTHERAPY FOR DYSLIPIDEMIA: A COMPREHENSIVE STUDY
abstractText: Dyslipidemia is a primary driver of atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease. While statins reduce LDL-C and cardiovascular events, statin intolerance and failure to achieve guideline targets limit their utility. To review the mechanism, efficacy, safety, and clinical positioning of current and emerging antihyperlipidemic agents as of May 2026. High-intensity statins remain first-line with 50-60% LDL-C reduction. Ezetimibe and bempedoic acid provide incremental LDL-C lowering of 15-28% without muscle toxicity. PCSK9 inhibitors and inclisiran achieve 50-60% reduction via distinct mechanisms, with inclisiran offering twice-yearly dosing. Bempedoic acid and inclisiran demonstrated cardiovascular outcome benefit in statin-intolerant populations. Gene editing therapy VERVE-101 showed single-dose LDL-C reductions of 39-55% in early trials. Therapeutic options now address statin intolerance, adherence barriers, and residual risk. A stepwise algorithm starting with oral agents and escalating to RNA-based therapies optimizes outcomes and resource use.

title: RE-CONCEPTUALIZING BIOMEDICAL INQUIRY: HARMONIZING CLASSICAL AYURVEDIC EPISTEMOLOGY, DIALECTICS, AND HERMENEUTICS IN MODERN RESEARCH
abstractText: Contemporary biomedical investigations predominantly rely on reductionist frameworks, frequently encountering limitations when navigating the multifactorial, highly individualized clinical dynamics observed in medical practice. This paper investigates the systematic integration of foundational Ayurvedic epistemological principles with current scientific research architectures. By mapping Pratyaksha (empirical observation), Anumana (logical inference), and Yukti (experimental and rational synthesis) onto modern statistical analytics, investigators can establish a sound methodological grounding for evidence-based traditional medicine. Additionally, the academic and clinical application of Acharya Charaka’s forty-four dialectical categories (Vada) provides an advanced framework for negotiating complex modern bioethical challenges. The tripartite Trisutra construct—encompassing Hetu (etiological factors), Linga (clinical manifestations), and Aushadha (therapeutic modalities)—serves as a robust structural blueprint for designing systematic reviews and clinical trials. Concurrently, Tantra-yukti (textual hermeneutical tools) functions as a qualitative protocol to ensure accurate interpretation of classical Sanskrit source material. Together, these traditional paradigms merge historical empirical insights with modern scientific methodology to generate a comprehensive model for contemporary clinical investigation.

title: OCCUPATIONAL HEARING HAZARDS - AN AYURVEDIC PERSPECTIVE ON BADHIRYA
abstractText: Occupational hearing hazards are a major yet often neglected public health concern, particularly among individuals working in industries with prolonged exposure to excessive noise, pressure variations, water immersion, and ototoxic chemicals. Noise-induced hearing loss (NIHL) is one of the most common occupational disorders and is characterized by gradual, irreversible sensorineural hearing impairment resulting from damage to cochlear hair cells. Ayurveda considers hearing as the function of shrotrendriya, with karna being a vata sthana, and attributes hearing disorders to mithyayoga of shabdendriya, leading to vata-kapha dushti and impairment of shabdavaha srotas, ultimately resulting in Badhirya. Modern preventive measures such as engineering controls, administrative interventions, hearing protection devices, periodic audiological screening, and hearing conservation programs are essential in reducing occupational hearing loss. Ayurvedic management emphasizes nidana parivarjana, snehana, swedana, nasya, karna purana, basti, rasayana therapy, and adherence to dinacharya and sadvritta to maintain auditory health, pacify aggravated vata, and prevent disease progression. early identification of temporary hearing changes, prompt intervention, and lifestyle modifications are crucial to preventing permanent auditory damage. The present review integrates contemporary concepts of occupational hearing hazards with classical Ayurvedic principles to provide a comprehensive understanding of their etiopathogenesis, prevention, and management.

abstractText: The natural amino acid, 5 – Hydroxytryptophan (5 – HTP) is intermediate metabolite of the essential amino acid tryptophan (Trp). title: A CASE STUDY ON THE EFFECT OF SHATADHAUTA GHRITA IN SCAR HEALING

Lepa, Taila, Ghrita, and Rasayana are non-surgical Ayurvedic methods that focus on nourishing the skin and promoting tissue regeneration, whereas Kshar Karma, Agnikarma, Raktamokshana, and Shastra Karma are surgical methods that effectively control hypertrophic and keloid scars. Effective scar treatment is necessary to improve one's physical appearance and quality of life.

title: FORMULATION, OPTIMIZATION, AND ESTIMATION OF CELECOXIB TOPICAL EMULGEL: A COMPREHENSIVE REVIEW
abstractText: Celecoxib, a selective cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) inhibitor widely prescribed for osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, and acute pain, is limited in its oral use by poor aqueous solubility, variable bioavailability, and a well-documented risk of gastrointestinal and cardiovascular adverse effects on chronic administration. Topical delivery of celecoxib offers an attractive alternative by directing the drug to the site of musculoskeletal or dermal pathology, minimizing systemic exposure, and improving patient acceptability. Among semisolid carriers, the emulgel — a biphasic system in which a fine emulsion is dispersed within a gel network — has emerged as a preferred vehicle for lipophilic, poorly water-soluble drugs such as celecoxib because it combines the drug-loading capacity of an emulsion with the spreadability, patient compliance, and dual-controlled release behavior of a gel. This review consolidates the current literature on celecoxib emulgel systems, covering the physicochemical and pharmacological rationale for topical delivery, the excipients and preparation methods used to formulate conventional, nano-, and microemulsion-based emulgels, the application of Quality by Design (QbD) and statistical design of experiments (Box-Behnken, central composite, and factorial designs) for formulation optimization, the standard panel of physicochemical, rheological, ex vivo, and stability evaluations applied to these systems, and the analytical (UV spectrophotometric and HPLC) methods used to estimate celecoxib in bulk, formulation, and biological matrices. Reported optimized celecoxib emulgels have consistently demonstrated acceptable pH, non-Newtonian pseudoplastic rheology, high drug content, and substantially enhanced ex vivo skin permeation and anti-inflammatory activity relative to conventional gels or marketed products. The review concludes by identifying persistent challenges — including long-term physical stability of the dispersed phase, scale-up reproducibility, and the need for harmonized in vitro-in vivo correlation — and outlines directions for future research in this field.

title: ANXIOLYTIC PROPERTY OF CAESALPINIA PULCHERRIMA LEAVES EXTRACT IN EXPERIMENTAL ANIMALS
abstractText: Objectives: To evaluate the anxiolytic property of ethanolic extract of leaves of Caesalpinia pulcherrima in Albino Wistar rats and Swiss Albino mice. Methods: The anxiolytic activity was evaluated using behavioral models of anxiety like elevated plus maze test, light-dark transition test, hole board test and open field test. The ethanolic extract was screened for toxicity by acute oral toxicity studies according to OECD guidelines 425 for selection of dose. Results: Compared to control group, animals in diazepam (2mg/kg i.p) treated group and the extract (ethanolic 800mg/kg p.o) treated groups revealed a statistically significant increase in anxiolytic activity. (ethanolic extract at 400mg/kg was statistically not significant except in light/dark transition test). Conclusion: Ethanolic extract showed significant dose dependent anxiolytic effect. Phytochemical screening revealed presence of flavonoids, and saponins as major constituents. The results suggest that the ethanolic extract (800mg/kg) of CP leaves seems to possess pronounced anxiolytic effect with lower sedative activity than the ethanolic extract (400mg/kg) when compared to diazepam. The results could be attributed to the flavonoids content (quercetin and sitosterol) of the ethanolic extract.

title: FORMULATION AND EVALUATION OF PUNICA GRANATUM L. PEEL EXTRACT AND CURCUMA LONGA L. EXTRACT CO-LOADED MUCOADHESIVE GINGIVAL PATCH FOR LOCALIZED PERIODONTITIS THERAPY
abstractText: Periodontitis is a chronic inflammatory disease associated with periodontal pathogens such as Porphyromonas gingivalis. The present study aimed to formulate and evaluate a mucoadhesive gingival patch containing Punica granatum L. peel extract and Curcuma longa L. extract for localized periodontal therapy. The herbal extracts were selected for their potential antimicrobial, antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties. Punica granatum peel extract was prepared by Soxhlet extraction, while Curcuma longa extract was prepared by maceration. Three formulations (F1, F2 and F3) were prepared using the solvent-casting method with chitosan, HPMC K15M and PEG 400. The prepared patches were evaluated for physicochemical, mechanical, mucoadhesive and drug-release properties.

title: A CASE STUDY ON THE AYURVEDIC MANAGEMENT OF BILATERAL RENAL CALCULI (VRIKKASHMARI)
abstractText: Ashmari is one of the most common conditions described in Ayurveda as an ailment of the Mutravaha Srotas, or urinary system.[1] Because of its extreme agony, recurrence, and difficulties, Sushruta classifies "Ashmari," which literally translates to "stone-like structure," as one of the "Ashtamahagada."[2] Ashmari is associated in contemporary medicine with urolithiasis, also known as nephrolithiasis, which is the development of calculi in the urinary tract. The increasing prevalence of the disease can be attributed to sedentary lifestyles, inadequate dietary practices, dehydration, and metabolic disorders. Current medical research indicates that between 70 and 80 percent of urinary calculi start in the kidneys, mostly in the renal pelvis and renal calyces, particularly the lower calyx. The ureters account for 15–25% of stones, whereas the bladder accounts for 2–10%.[3] Calyceal stones, especially those in the lower calyx, can last for extended periods of time, cause symptoms, and may eventually result in stone development, infection, or urinary blockage, even if smaller calculi may have the ability to pass spontaneously. As a result, "watchful waiting" is frequently insufficient on its own, necessitating active therapeutic involvement.[4] In the current investigation, Ayurvedic medicine was used to treat a 23-year-old female patient who had bilateral renal calyceal calculi. Calculi measuring 5 mm in the right kidney and 4 mm in the left kidney were discovered by ultrasonography. Pashanbhed Churna was used to treat the patient in addition to the proper dietary and lifestyle changes (Pathya-Apathya). Following treatment, ultrasonography showed a considerable improvement in clinical symptoms along with a marked reduction in stone size and partial to total disintegration. This example suggests that treating renal calyceal calculi with Ayurvedic medicine may be a secure and successful treatment choice.

title: BRIDGING ANCIENT WISDOM AND MOLECULAR MEDICINE: CLINICAL APPLICATIONS OF CORE AYURVEDIC SIDDHANTAS IN CONTEMPORARY PATHOPHYSIOLOGY
abstractText: Ayurveda, the ancient science of life, relies on foundational philosophical and clinical principles known as Siddhantas. While traditionally viewed through a purely historical or qualitative lens, these principles offer profound correlations with modern molecular biology, systems biology, and chronic disease pathogenesis. This article provides a critical analysis of four core Siddhantas—Lok-Purusha Samya Siddhanta (macrocosm-microcosm correspondence), Kriya Kala Siddhanta (six stages of pathogenesis), Agni Siddhanta (metabolic fire and enzymatic integrity), and Srotas Siddhanta (systemic channels and microcirculation). This translational synthesis aims to establish a rigorous scientific foundation for personalized, systems-oriented clinical practice.

title: TRANSLATIONAL PHARMACOLOGICAL ANALYSIS OF LOCAL ORAL THERAPEUTICS (GAṆḌŪṢA, KAVALA, AND PRATISĀRAṆA) IN ŚĀRṄGADHARA SAṂHITĀ
abstractText: Background: The Śārṅgadharasaṃhitā, a seminal 13th-century Ayurvedic compendium, systematically codifies local oral therapeutic procedures—Gaṇḍūṣa (mouth holding), Kavala (gargling), and Pratisāraṇa (topical powder application)—in its Madhyama and Uttara Khaṇḍas. Despite their clinical prevalence in traditional practice, these modalities lack comprehensive translational pharmacological frameworks connecting classical descriptions to modern mucosal drug delivery science. Objective: To establish a translational pharmacological framework analyzing Gaṇḍūṣa, Kavala, and Pratisāraṇa through integrated textual exegesis of Śārṅgadharasaṃhitā and contemporary oral mucosal drug delivery research. Methods: Systematic review of Śārṅgadharasaṃhitā chapters on Ganduṣa-Kavala-Pratisāraṇa Vidhi, correlated with modern pharmacological literature on buccal/sublingual absorption, mucoadhesion, permeability enhancement, and clinical studies on Ayurvedic oral formulations. Results: Classical procedures demonstrate sophisticated understanding of oral mucosal pharmacokinetics: Gaṇḍūṣa achieves static distension maximizing mucosal contact time; Kavala enables dynamic distribution with mechanical cleansing; Pratisāraṇa provides localized high-concentration powder application. Modern evidence confirms sublingual/buccal routes bypass hepatic first-pass metabolism, with thin mucosal layers (500–800 μm buccal; thinner sublingual) permitting rapid lipid-soluble compound absorption. Clinical trials show Khadira, Triphala, and Yashtimadhu-based Pratisāraṇa formulations effectively manage stomatitis, periodontitis, and oral ulcers. Conclusion: Gaṇḍūṣa, Kavala, and Pratisāraṇa represent pharmacologically sophisticated local delivery systems anticipating modern principles of mucoadhesion, permeability enhancement, and targeted mucosal therapy. A five-dimensional translational framework (HP1–HP5) is proposed for future standardization and clinical validation.

title: EFFECTIVE AYURVEDIC MANAGEMENT OF SEVERE HEPATITIS OF UNKNOWN AETIOLOGY IN PREGNANCY-A CASE REPORT
abstractText: Pregnancy is a unique clinical state with several normal physiological changes that influence body organs including the liver. Liver disease may cause significant morbidity and mortality in both pregnant women and their infants. Despite tremendous progress made by modern medicine, it is a fact that reason of severe Hepatitis has been poorly understood. After ruling out all possible causes of hepatitis, we come to the conclusion of diagnosis as Hepatitis of unknown aetiology. Case study: This 27 year old pregnant woman developed hepatitis in second month of gestation. Her Serum Bilirubin and other parameters of Liver function tests were very high. All possible causes of Hepatitis were ruled out. Finally she was labelled as a case of Hepatitis of unknown aetiology. The guidelines of treatment of such cases are not clearly spelt out. She was referred to Ayurved. She was treated by Ayurvedic line of treatment. Within 2 months of Ayurvedic treatment, all the Liver function tests became normal. She was treated adequately by Ayurvedic treatment throughout her pregnancy. Her delivery was uneventful and healthy male baby was born. There is no relapse of Hepatitis after 4 years of follow up. Conclusion:-Ayurved has promising role in managing severe Hepatitis of unknown origin.

title: REGULATORY REQUIREMENTS ON PHARMACOVIGILANCE AS PER CDSCO IN INDIA COMAPARISON WITH NEW ZEALAND
abstractText: Pharmacovigilance is an essential component of medicine safety that involves the Detection, assessment, understanding, and prevention of adverse drug reaction and other medicine-related problems. In India CDSCO regulates post-marketing drug safety activities through requirements for marketing authorization holders [MAHs], individual case safety reports [ICSRs], periodic safety update reports [PSURs], signal detection, risk management, and pharmacovigilance system. CDSCO’S current post-marketing framework includes guidance for MAHs and electronic PSUR submission through the SUGAM portal. In New Zealand pharmacovigilance is regulated primarily by Medsafe with safety monitoring supported by the center for adverse reactions monitoring. Sponsors are required to maintain system for collecting and evaluating adverse reaction information and to report valid serious ICSRs occuring in New Zealand generally within 15 days calendar days of receipt the comparison examines regulatory authorities ADR/ICSR reporting requirements, reporting timeline, safety monitoring, signal detection, and responsibilities of pharmaceutical companies. Overall the study highlights similarities and differences in the two national systems and emphasizes and importance of effective post-marketing surveillance for ensuring the continued safe and rational use of medicines

title: FORMULATION AND EVALUATION OF HERBAL ANTIMICROBIAL GEL CONTAINING APRAJITA CLITORIA TERNATEA L.
abstractText: Skin infections caused by pathogenic microorganisms remain a major healthcare concern, and the increasing prevalence of antimicrobial resistance has highlighted the need for safer and more effective topical therapies. Herbal medicines have gained considerable attention because of their broad therapeutic potential, low toxicity, and improved patient acceptability. The present study aimed to formulate and evaluate a herbal antimicrobial gel containing the ethanolic extract of Clitoria ternatea L. (Aprajita). Fresh flowers of Clitoria ternatea were collected, authenticated, shade-dried, powdered, and extracted using ethanol. The extract was incorporated into a Carbopol-based gel using suitable excipients to obtain a stable topical formulation. The prepared gel was evaluated for its physicochemical properties, including appearance, homogeneity, pH, viscosity, spreadability, extrudability, washability, and stability. Antimicrobial activity was assessed against selected pathogenic microorganisms using a standard microbiological method. The formulated gel exhibited acceptable physical characteristics, good consistency, suitable pH for topical application, satisfactory spreadability, and excellent stability throughout the study period. The formulation demonstrated promising antimicrobial activity, indicating the presence of bioactive phytoconstituents in the ethanolic extract of Clitoria ternatea. These findings suggest that the developed herbal gel has potential as a safe and effective topical antimicrobial formulation for the management of superficial skin infections. Further preclinical and clinical investigations are recommended to establish its therapeutic efficacy and long-term safety.

title: CONCEPT OF VIKARAVIGHATA BHAVA IN ROGNIDAN: A REVIEW ARTICLE
abstractText: Classical Ayurvedic nosology does not treat disease as the automatic and mechanical outcome of exposure to a causative factor. Between Nidana (cause), Dosha and Dushya on one side and overt Vikara (disease) on the other, the Samhitas recognise an intervening host variable — Vikara Vighataka Bhava — that may inhibit, delay, soften or entirely prevent the expression of disease, and whose converse, Vikara Vighata Abhava, permits rapid, severe and complicated manifestation. This article undertakes a conceptual and literary review of Vikara Vighataka Bhava: its place within the broader Nidanadi Vishesha framework, its classical textual basis, the host and environmental factors traditionally held to constitute it, and its detailed, named application in the Prameha Nidana (fourth chapter of Charaka Samhita’s Nidana Sthana), where the term is very first defined in relation to the twenty varieties of Prameha.

title: ROLE OF MEDOHARA AND PRAMEHAGHNA DRAVYAS IN THE MANAGEMENT OF METABOLIC DISORDERS: A COMPREHENSIVE AYURVEDIC REVIEW
abstractText: Metabolic disorders have emerged as major health concerns in the present era. Conditions such as obesity, type 2 diabetes mellitus, dyslipidemia, hypertension, and metabolic syndrome are commonly associated with inappropriate dietary habits, physical inactivity, stress, and sedentary behaviour. Their coexistence may contribute to an increased risk of cardiovascular disease and other chronic complications. Ayurveda explains disorders arising from excessive nourishment through concepts such as Santarpana, Medo Doṣa, Sthaulya, Prameha, Madhumeha, and impairment of Agni. Excessive consumption of heavy, oily, and sweet foods, overeating, and inadequate physical activity are described as important factors in the development of Santarpanajanya Vikāra. The concepts of Sthaulya and Prameha also show considerable relevance to obesity and metabolic disturbances in the contemporary context.[1,2]

title: CONCEPT OF VIKARAVIGHATA BHAVA IN ROGNIDAN: A REVIEW ARTICLE
abstractText: Classical Ayurvedic nosology does not treat disease as the automatic and mechanical outcome of exposure to a causative factor. Between Nidana (cause), Dosha and Dushya on one side and overt Vikara (disease) on the other, the Samhitas recognise an intervening host variable — Vikara Vighataka Bhava — that may inhibit, delay, soften or entirely prevent the expression of disease, and whose converse, Vikara Vighata Abhava, permits rapid, severe and complicated manifestation. This article undertakes a conceptual and literary review of Vikara Vighataka Bhava: its place within the broader Nidanadi Vishesha framework, its classical textual basis, the host and environmental factors traditionally held to constitute it, and its detailed, named application in the Prameha Nidana (fourth chapter of Charaka Samhita’s Nidana Sthana), where the term is very first defined in relation to the twenty varieties of Prameha.

title: CARBON NANOTUBES: SYNTHESIS, PROPERTIES, AND MULTIDISCIPLINARY APPLICATIONS A COMPREHENSIVE REVIEW
abstractText: Carbon nanotubes (CNTs) have become one of the most versatile classes of nanomaterials in the last three decades, due to their outstanding mechanical strength, tunable electrical conductivity, high thermal stability and large accessible surface area. CNTs are cylindrical, sp2-hybridized carbon nanostructures. This review summarizes recent work on the synthesis, structure, and physicochemical behavior of single-walled and multi-walled carbon nanotubes, with special attention to arc discharge, laser ablation, and chemical vapor deposition routes, as well as post-synthesis purification and covalent or non-covalent functionalization strategies to improve dispersibility and biocompatibility. Based on these basic principles, four key application areas are discussed in the review: (i) biomedical applications, including targeted and controlled drug delivery, gene therapy, tissue engineering scaffolds, biosensing and photothermal or photodynamic cancer therapy; (ii) electrocatalytic and energy applications including fuel cells, batteries, electrochemical sensors and CO2 electroreduction; (iii) polymer-matrix composites produced by melt mixing, solution mixing, in-situ polymerization and additive manufacturing, which produce lightweight materials with improved mechanical, electrical and thermal properties for aerospace, automotive, construction and electronics applications; and (iv) natural nanotubular clay analogues such as halloysite that provide a lower-cost, more abundant alternative platform for carbon capture and environmental remediation. Toxicological issues such as biodegradability, dispersibility and long-term biocompatibility remain impediments to translation. The research finds that ongoing improvement in scalable synthesis, reproducible functionalization, and application-specific material design will be necessary for carbon nanotubes to move from laboratory-scale demonstrations to widely deployed industrial and clinical applications.

title: OXALIDACEAE FAMILY: AN INTEGRATIVE REVIEW OF BOTANICAL DIVERSITY, PHARMACOGNOSTIC FEATURES, PHYTOCHEMICAL CONSTITUENTS AND AYURVEDIC–ETHNOMEDICINAL SIGNIFICANCE
abstractText: Background: Oxalidaceae R.Br. is a distinctive flowering-plant family placed in the order Oxalidales. Current Plants of the World Online (POWO) treatment recognizes five accepted genera—Averrhoa L., Biophytum DC., Dapania Korth., Oxalis L. and Sarcotheca Blume—and approximately 570 species, with Oxalis representing the largest genus. Members occur mainly in tropical and subtropical regions and include plants of nutritional, ornamental, ecological and medicinal importance.[1,2] Objective: This review integrates botanical characteristics, pharmacognostic significance, ethnomedicinal and Ayurvedic relevance, phytochemical composition, pharmacological evidence and toxicological considerations of selected medicinally important members of Oxalidaceae. Materials and Methods: A narrative literature review was prepared from the literature contained in the original manuscript and supplemented with current taxonomic information from Kew Plants of the World Online and peer-reviewed literature indexed in PubMed. Particular attention was given to Oxalis corniculata L., Biophytum sensitivum DC., Averrhoa carambola L. and Averrhoa bilimbi L. The evidence was interpreted according to the level of experimental or clinical support available. Results: The family is characterized by alternate leaves that are often compound, actinomorphic bisexual flowers, usually five sepals and five petals, ten stamens arranged in two whorls, a superior ovary and generally capsular fruits.[1] Selected medicinally investigated species contain flavonoids, phenolic compounds, biflavonoids, tannins, terpenoids, polysaccharides and organic acids. Experimental studies report antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, antidiabetic, wound-healing, immunomodulatory and anticancer activities for selected taxa, but most evidence remains preclinical.[3–6] Averrhoa carambola is of particular safety interest because oxalate and caramboxin have been associated with renal and neurological toxicity.[8–10] Conclusion: Oxalidaceae represents a valuable reservoir of medicinal and nutritionally important plants. Future research should emphasize botanical authentication, pharmacognostic standardization, chemical fingerprinting, mechanism-based investigations, pharmacokinetics, toxicity assessment, herb–drug interaction studies and well-designed clinical trials. Integration of classical Ayurvedic Dravyaguna knowledge with modern pharmacognosy and pharmacology may support scientifically rigorous evaluation of medicinal species.

title: ASTAXANTHIN AS A NEUROPROTECTIVE AGENT AGAINST ACUTE STRESS-INDUCED COGNITIVE IMPAIRMENT
abstractText: The sympathetic-adrenomedullary system and the hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis are both activated by acute stress. Although adaptive initially, excessive acute stress causes glucocorticoid overload, oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, and neuroinflammation. These changes particularly affect the hippocampus and prefrontal cortex, impairing synaptic plasticity, neurogenesis, and cognition, including working memory, spatial learning, attention, and executive function. Oxidative stress and inflammation are now recognised as key mediators linking HPA-axis hyperactivation to cognitive decline. Astaxanthin, a xanthophyll carotenoid derived from microalgae such as Haematococcus pluvialis, yeast, and marine organisms, has drawn attention for its anti-inflammatory, anti-apoptotic, and antioxidant qualities. It is a prospective neuroprotective drug because of its lipophilic nature and capacity to pass the blood–brain barrier. According to preclinical research, astaxanthin improves learning and memory in stress and neurodegenerative models, lowers lipid peroxidation, increases endogenous antioxidants, inhibits inflammatory mediators, and stimulates the Nrf2/HO-1 pathway. Methods: Relevant experimental, preclinical, and clinical studies were identified through systematic searches of major scientific databases focusing on acute stress, cognitive dysfunction, oxidative stress, and astaxanthin-mediated neuroprotection. Results: All of these results point to astaxanthin as a viable multi-target treatment option, but more carefully planned human trials are needed to determine its effectiveness, dosage recommendations, and long-term safety in stress-related cognitive impairment.

title: FORMULATION AND EVALUATION OF EMULGEL FOR TOPICAL DRUG DELIVERY
abstractText: Topical drug delivery systems offer a convenient and effective mode of delivery of drugs to the skin surface, which increases local concentration of the drug while minimizing systemic adverse effects. Emulgels are considered as one of the potential dosage forms, which offer solution for topical drug delivery. They are mixtures of an emulsion and gel matrix and allow delivery of both hydrophilic and hydrophobic drugs. This article highlights a discussion on topical drug delivery and emulgels, including their types, formulating ingredients, methods of preparation, and evaluation parameters. A brief description on the anatomy of the skin and its barrier properties towards topical drug delivery is also presented. Emulgels are described with a focus on the aqueous and oily phases, emulsifying agents, permeation enhancers, and gelling agents. The physiological, physicochemical, and formulation factors that may influence topical drug absorption are also outlined. Moreover, the article discusses the various types of emulgels: macroemulgels, microemulgels, and nanoemulgels, and their characteristics such as particle size and stability. Other evaluation parameters include physical appearance, pH, viscosity, stability, irritation, and zeta potential, particle size distribution, polydispersity index, swelling index, drug content, spreadability, and extrudability. Emulgels can be used as a versatile topically applicable dosage form due to their enhanced spreading ability, patient acceptability, high drug loading, stability, and controlled release property. Future work focused on the evaluation and formulation of emulgels would be of paramount importance in topical and transdermal drug delivery.

title: PLANT-DERIVED BIOACTIVES FOR DANDRUFF MANAGEMENT: PHYTOCHEMISTRY, ANTIFUNGAL MECHANISMS AND MODERN FORMULATION STRATEGIES
abstractText: Dandruff is a common chronic scalp disorder characterised by excessive shedding of superficial scalp skin, producing visible flakes accompanied by itching, irritation, and mild inflammation. It commonly develops after puberty and is associated with interactions among Malassezia yeasts, sebaceous gland activity, scalp-barrier function, and individual susceptibility. Although dandruff shares features with seborrheic dermatitis, dandruff is generally limited to scaling and itching, whereas seborrheic dermatitis involves more prominent erythema and inflammation and may affect other sebaceous areas.[1-3,8]

title: VISHADA: AN AYURVEDIC PERSPECTIVE ON PSYCHOLOGICAL INHIBITION
abstractText: Vishada is an Ayurvedic concept describing a state of mental disturbance in which emotional strength, confidence, initiative, and engagement with daily life becomes diminished. It extends beyond temporary sadness and involves changes in mental, behavioural and physical functioning. The present discussion explores the classical understanding of Vishada with emphasis on its etiopathogenesis and therapeutic perspective. Psychological experiences such as Ishta Viyoga and prolonged stress may disturb the equilibrium of Satwa and Tamas, with subsequent involvement of Manas, Vatadi doshas and Manovaha Srotas. Its manifestations, including Kaya-Vak-Manas Sada, Apravritti, Karyeshu Asiddhi Bhaya and impairment of Dhi, Dhriti, and Smriti demonstrate the wide-ranging influence of Vishada on activity, motivation, cognition, communication and social interaction. The Ayurvedic approach further emphasizes restoration of mental well-being through different lines of treatment. Understanding Vishada through this holistic framework highlights the close relationship between emotional experience and overall functioning and provides a foundation for its deeper exploration in contemporary mental-health research.

title: DEVELOPMENT OF ANALYTICAL SPECIFICATIONS AND VALIDATION OF DEFLAZACORT USING RP-HPLC
abstractText: Background: Deflazacort is a synthetic glucocorticoid used for its anti-inflammatory and immunosuppressive effects. Reliable analytical methods are required for its accurate estimation in pharmaceutical formulations and for routine quality control. The present study aimed to develop and validate a simple, accurate, precise, robust, and stability-indicating reverse-phase high-performance liquid chromatography (RP-HPLC) method for the quantitative estimation of Deflazacort. Methods: The RP-HPLC method was developed using a reversed-phase C18 column (250 × 4.6 mm, 5 µm) with acetonitrile:water (80:20, v/v) as the mobile phase. The flow rate was maintained at 1.0 mL/min, injection volume was 20 µL, and detection was performed at 244 nm. Deflazacort standard and marketed tablet sample solutions were prepared and analyzed under the optimized chromatographic conditions. The method was validated for specificity, linearity, accuracy, precision, robustness, and solution stability. Forced degradation studies were performed under acidic, alkaline, oxidative, thermal, and photolytic stress conditions. Results: The developed method produced a distinct Deflazacort peak at approximately 4.18 min. The method showed good linearity over 50–150 µg/mL, with a correlation coefficient of 0.9998 and R² of 0.9996. The mean recovery was 99.59%, while precision and repeatability showed 0.08% RSD and intermediate precision showed 0.07% RSD. The method remained robust following deliberate changes in chromatographic conditions, and standard and sample solutions remained stable for 48 hours. Forced degradation showed the highest degradation under alkaline conditions (14.58%), followed by oxidative (10.34%), acidic (7.46%), photolytic (6.09%), and thermal (3.62%) conditions. The degradation peaks were adequately separated from the Deflazacort peak. Application of the method to the marketed tablet formulation gave a mean assay of 99.17% of the labelled claim with 0.42% RSD. Conclusion: The developed RP-HPLC method was found to be specific, accurate, precise, robust, and stability-indicating. The method can be suitably applied for the routine quantitative analysis and quality control of Deflazacort in pharmaceutical formulations.

title: DEVELOPMENT OF CONTROLLED RELEASE TRANSDERMAL FILMS CONTAINING ANTHRALIN
abstractText: Anthralin is an effective antipsoriatic agent widely used in the treatment of chronic skin disorders such as psoriasis; however, its therapeutic application is limited due to poor patient compliance, skin irritation, and the need for frequent administration. The present study was undertaken to develop and evaluate controlled release transdermal films containing Anthralin in order to enhance drug release control, improve therapeutic efficacy, and prolong drug delivery through the skin. Pre-formulation studies of Anthralin were carried out to determine its physicochemical properties, including organoleptic characteristics, solubility, melting point, λ max determination, calibration curve analysis, and FTIR spectroscopy. Anthralin exhibited maximum absorbance and showed compatibility with the selected excipients used in the transdermal patch formulation. The transdermal films were prepared by the solvent casting method using combinations of Eudragit L, polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP), hydroxypropyl methylcellulose (HPMC), polyethylene glycol 400, Tween 20, methanol, and glycerin. Six formulations (TPF1–TPF6) were prepared by varying the polymer composition. The prepared transdermal films were evaluated for folding endurance, tensile strength, percentage elongation, thickness uniformity, drug content, and in vitro drug release studies. Among all formulations, TPF5 exhibited the most desirable physicochemical characteristics; including excellent flexibility, tensile strength (25 kg/cm²), percentage elongation (42%), and maximum drug content (95.78%). The optimized formulation also demonstrated a sustained and controlled drug release profile with 95.06% cumulative drug release over 11 hours. Drug release kinetics of the optimized formulation was analyzed using zero-order, first-order, Higuchi, and Korsmeyer–Peppas kinetic models. The release profile showed the highest correlation with the zero-order kinetic model (R² = 0.976), indicating concentration-independent and controlled drug release. The Higuchi model also demonstrated good linearity, suggesting diffusion-controlled release behavior from the polymeric matrix. The overall findings of the study indicate that the developed Anthralin transdermal films possess satisfactory physicochemical properties, controlled drug release characteristics, and excellent formulation stability. Therefore, the optimized transdermal patch formulation can be considered a promising alternative drug delivery system for the effective management of psoriasis and related dermatological conditions.

title: FORMULATION, OPTIMIZATION, AND ESTIMATION OF CELECOXIB TOPICAL EMULGEL: A COMPREHENSIVE REVIEW
abstractText: Celecoxib, a selective cyclooxygenase-2 (COX-2) inhibitor widely prescribed for osteoarthritis, rheumatoid arthritis, and acute pain, is limited in its oral use by poor aqueous solubility, variable bioavailability, and a well-documented risk of gastrointestinal and cardiovascular adverse effects on chronic administration. Topical delivery of celecoxib offers an attractive alternative by directing the drug to the site of musculoskeletal or dermal pathology, minimizing systemic exposure, and improving patient acceptability. Among semisolid carriers, the emulgel — a biphasic system in which a fine emulsion is dispersed within a gel network — has emerged as a preferred vehicle for lipophilic, poorly water-soluble drugs such as celecoxib because it combines the drug-loading capacity of an emulsion with the spreadability, patient compliance, and dual-controlled release behavior of a gel. This review consolidates the current literature on celecoxib emulgel systems, covering the physicochemical and pharmacological rationale for topical delivery, the excipients and preparation methods used to formulate conventional, nano-, and microemulsion-based emulgels, the application of Quality by Design (QbD) and statistical design of experiments (Box-Behnken, central composite, and factorial designs) for formulation optimization, the standard panel of physicochemical, rheological, ex vivo, and stability evaluations applied to these systems, and the analytical (UV spectrophotometric and HPLC) methods used to estimate celecoxib in bulk, formulation, and biological matrices. Reported optimized celecoxib emulgels have consistently demonstrated acceptable pH, non-Newtonian pseudoplastic rheology, high drug content, and substantially enhanced ex vivo skin permeation and anti-inflammatory activity relative to conventional gels or marketed products. The review concludes by identifying persistent challenges — including long-term physical stability of the dispersed phase, scale-up reproducibility, and the need for harmonized in vitro-in vivo correlation — and outlines directions for future research in this field.

title: EFFECTIVE AYURVEDIC MANAGEMENT OF SEVERE HEPATITIS OF UNKNOWN AETIOLOGY IN PREGNANCY-A CASE REPORT
abstractText: Pregnancy is a unique clinical state with several normal physiological changes that influence body organs including the liver. Liver disease may cause significant morbidity and mortality in both pregnant women and their infants. Despite tremendous progress made by modern medicine, it is a fact that reason of severe Hepatitis has been poorly understood. After ruling out all possible causes of hepatitis, we come to the conclusion of diagnosis as Hepatitis of unknown aetiology. Case study: This 27 year old pregnant woman developed hepatitis in second month of gestation. Her Serum Bilirubin and other parameters of Liver function tests were very high. All possible causes of Hepatitis were ruled out. Finally she was labelled as a case of Hepatitis of unknown aetiology. The guidelines of treatment of such cases are not clearly spelt out. She was referred to Ayurved. She was treated by Ayurvedic line of treatment. Within 2 months of Ayurvedic treatment, all the Liver function tests became normal. She was treated adequately by Ayurvedic treatment throughout her pregnancy. Her delivery was uneventful and healthy male baby was born. There is no relapse of Hepatitis after 4 years of follow up. Conclusion:-Ayurved has promising role in managing severe Hepatitis of unknown origin.

title: DEVELOPMENT AND CHARACTERIZATION OF SOLID DISPERSIONS OF SERTRALINE HYDROCHLORIDE FOR IMPROVED DISSOLUTION PERFORMANCE
abstractText: Sertraline hydrochloride (HCl) is a widely prescribed selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) characterized by poor aqueous solubility, that severely limits its oral bioavailability. This study is designed to increase the dissolution rate of sertraline HCl through solid dispersion formulations using hydrophilic polymeric carriers. Using a design of experiments (DOE) approach, nine solid dispersions were made using the solvent evaporation method at a 1:3 drug-to-carrier ratio. Formulations combined sertraline HCl (100 mg) with varying proportions of hydroxypropyl cellulose (HPC), polyethylene glycol 6000 (PEG 6000), polyvinylpyrrolidone K90 (PVP K90), and sodium lauryl sulfate (SLS). In vitro dissolution profiles were assessed in standard phosphate buffer (pH 6.8) using a USP Type II apparatus. All solid dispersions demonstrated significantly improved dissolution efficiency compared to pure sertraline HCl (60.92 ± 1.13% at 60 min). Formulation F7 (containing 65% HPC, 30% PEG 6000, and 5% PVP K90) emerged as optimal, achieving 95.38 ± 0.70% drug release at 60 minutes—representing a 56.56% relative improvement. F7 exhibited superior dissolution efficiency (61.96 ± 0.81%), remarkable reproducibility (RSD = 1.51%), and rapid initial kinetics. One-way ANOVA confirmed highly significant variations in drug release across formulations during early time intervals ($p < 0.001$), with profiles converging toward the 60-minute endpoint ($p = 0.626$). Pearson correlation analysis verified HPC as the primary performance-determining carrier ($r = +0.695, p = 0.038$). These findings demonstrate that solid dispersion strategies using optimized polymeric balances offer a robust and highly reproducible methodology for accelerating the dissolution profiles of BCS Class II antidepressants.

title: DIAGNOSIS AND TREATMENT IN A SINGLE SWIPE: TERRA FIRMA-FORME DERMATOSIS
abstractText: Terra firma-forme dermatosis (TFFD) is a benign keratinization disorder characterized by dirt-like brown-gray lesions, predominantly affecting children and young adults. A 10-year-old girl presented with an asymptomatic brown-gray patch on the posterior aspect of the right lower leg that had been present for two months. No improvement had been observed despite previous treatment with topical corticosteroids, antifungal agents, and moisturizers. The lesion was completely cleared after wiping with 70% isopropyl alcohol, confirming the diagnosis of TFFD. Recognition of TFFD and the use of a simple alcohol-wiping test enable rapid diagnosis and immediate treatment while helping to avoid unnecessary diagnostic procedures and inappropriate therapies.
